title: S3b: a failed setup must not stop Orca from starting (supersedes dbu.3: FROZEN named the implementation, not the test)
description:
Same slice as claude-orca-dbu.3, re-registered because its contract froze scripts/container/entrypoint.sh -- the implementation -- instead of the test, which inverts the RED/GREEN ritual. Text otherwise unchanged:

scripts/container/entrypoint.sh:237-241 calls die() when setup.sh fails, and die() exits. On the built-image path setup.sh is a VERIFICATION pass (every phase 'already present'), so its failure says something is wrong with the image, not that there is nothing to run. Killing the container there removes the only thing that could report the problem: no Orca, no terminal, no Claude Code.

Demote it: record the failure (run/provision/setup.status holding the non-zero exit, plus the existing run/setup.log), warn, and carry on to the privilege drop and orca-ide --serve. The one case that stays fatal is an ORCA_BIN that is not executable (entrypoint.sh:634), because there is then genuinely nothing to serve. Write run/provision/setup.status on SUCCESS too (0), so 'never ran' and 'ran fine' are distinguishable.

title: outbound-guard: a compound git push must not carry the marker-gated verbs past their gate
description:
Found in review of claude-orca-diz (PASSed its own contract; this is a defect that contract never named).

The new git push branch ends in a bare 'exit 0', so MARKER_RE is never evaluated for any command that also matched GIT_PUSH_RE. With a live GitHub connection, prefixing 'git push &&' now carries gh pr create / gh repo create / bd dolt push past the prompt-marker gate that the diz bead deliberately left in place.

Reproduced twice, independently -- by the orchestrator with a scratchpad probe and by the verifier -- with a stubbed gh reporting connected and an empty state dir:
  old guard: plain push DENIED | plain pr-create DENIED | compound DENIED
  new guard: plain push ALLOWED | plain pr-create DENIED | compound ALLOWED  <-- regression

The 38 frozen cases stay green because none of them pairs two verbs in one command line. That omission is the orchestrator's, not the executor's: the contract only ever asked for the verbs standalone.

FIX: delete the 'exit 0' from the git push branch and let a connected push fall through. MARKER_RE does not match a plain 'git push', so a lone connected push still ends in a clean allow; a compound line reaches the marker gate exactly as it did before diz. The has_sid fail-open below is unchanged, so 'git push && gh pr create' with no session_id keeps the pre-existing open posture.
acceptance_criteria:
CHECK: bats tests/outbound-guard.bats

PASS-IF: the run prints a TAP plan line '1..N' with N >= 43, zero lines beginning 'not ok', and one 'ok' line for each of these cases, named verbatim:
  a connected git push compounded with gh pr create still requires the prompt marker
  a connected git push compounded with gh repo create still requires the prompt marker
  a connected git push compounded with bd dolt push still requires the prompt marker
  a connected git push on its own is still allowed with no marker
  a disconnected git push compounded with gh pr create is denied for the connection
All thirty-eight cases already in the file at GREEN-AT 6952fcb must still be present and still pass.

FROZEN: tests/outbound-guard.bats

CLASS: authorization guard, tightening. The five new cases pin the boundary the diz contract left open: a compound command must be evaluated against EVERY rule it matches, not only the first. The single-verb behaviour delivered by diz must not regress -- a lone connected git push still allows, a lone disconnected one still denies naming the connection, and the warehouse-CLI deny stays first and unconditional.
notes:
RED-AT: 7bbb2583443478ccac82444d0ef501fa47a8258f  GREEN-AT: cdccfae31c7b2178368b7296863a1e2a04f42f0c
VERIFIER: PASS. C1 1..43 zero not-ok, five PASS-IF names matched grep -Fxq, all 38 prior cases present and green; C2 frozen file byte-identical 7bbb258..cdccfae; C2b red confirmed at 7bbb258 with exactly 3 not-ok (39,40,41 -- the compounded cases), matching the executor's claim; C3 only scripts/outbound-guard.sh +7-2 and config/claude-user-memory.md 1 line; C4 the only functional line in the diff is '- exit 0'; C5 marker machinery and --prompt byte-identical, warehouse deny still first.
Decision table vs 8dbe6d9^: exactly ONE cell more permissive (plain git push, connected, sid present, no marker: DENY->ALLOW, the intended change). TWO cells strictly tighter (plain and compound push, disconnected, marker present: ALLOW->DENY). All three no-sid fail-open cells identical.

title: S2 the card itself: card-update writes it with haiku, card-view draws it without scrolling
description:
scripts/card-update.sh -- the Stop hook's worker. Reads the hook JSON on stdin and takes .transcript_path (or a path as $1). Walks the transcript's user/assistant entries, skips isSidechain, drops thinking blocks, flattens text blocks and tool_use blocks to 'name + command/file_path/description', keeps the tail under a byte budget with a per-row cap so one runaway message cannot fill it. Sends that to 'claude -p --model ${CARD_MODEL:-claude-haiku-4-5-20251001}' with a prompt that fixes the shape -- NOW / WHY / DONE (up to 3) / NEXT / SNAG, at most 12 lines, no line over 68 characters, no preamble -- and writes the result to .claude-dev/run/card.md through a temp file and mv, so the viewer never reads half a card.

scripts/card-view.sh -- runs inside the pane. Clears and repaints; never appends, so the pane cannot scroll. Redraws on a change to the card file's mtime and on SIGWINCH, and otherwise sleeps. Clips every line to the pane width and the card to the pane height. Hides the cursor and restores it on exit.

Both fail open: no payload, no transcript, no jq, no model, a model that returns nothing -- exit 0 and leave the previous card alone.

  card-update takes transcript_path from the hook payload on stdin and writes the card file

  card-update exits 0 and leaves the previous card in place when there is no transcript or the model returns nothing
  card-view draws one boxed card clipped to the pane and repeats no line of it
  card-view repaints when the card file changes and not otherwise

title: S1 card control: bin/card on|off|toggle|status|autostart, anchored to this terminal's own pane
description:
scripts/card.sh + bin/card (symlink, like bin/lane -> ../scripts/lane.sh).

Resolves the terminal it is running in: ORCA_PANE_KEY is '<tabId>:<leafId>'; match the leafId against 'orca terminal list --json' to get the handle. 'card on' splits that handle vertically running card-view, renames the new pane 'CARD', and records the handle in .claude-dev/run/card.pane and 'on' in .claude-dev/run/card.state. 'card off' closes the recorded pane and records 'off'. 'card toggle' flips. 'card status' prints one line. 'card autostart' is the SessionStart entry: open a pane when the state is on OR unset (default on), do nothing when it is off, and never open a second one when the recorded pane is still live.

Fails open, always: no ORCA_PANE_KEY, no orca CLI, an unreachable runtime, a stale handle -- each is 'exit 0, say so on one line', never an error that could stop a session starting.
acceptance_criteria:
CHECK: bats tests/card-control.bats
PASS-IF: the TAP output has the plan line '1..7', zero lines beginning 'not ok', and one 'ok' line for each of these seven case names, verbatim:
  card resolves its own terminal handle from the leaf id in ORCA_PANE_KEY
  card on splits that terminal, renames the pane CARD, and records the handle and the on state
  card on is idempotent: a second call while the recorded pane is live splits nothing
  card off closes the recorded pane and records the off state
  card toggle flips on to off and off to on
  card autostart opens a pane when the state is on or unset and stays quiet when it is off
  card exits 0 with one explanatory line when there is no ORCA_PANE_KEY, no orca CLI, or an unreachable runtime

(2) scripts/container/openrouter-guard.py (python3 stdlib, no deps): listens on 127.0.0.1:4141, reads the real key from OPENROUTER_API_KEY at start and the policy file; for POST /api/v1/chat/completions, /api/v1/completions, /api/v1/responses, /api/v1/messages it parses JSON, sets body.provider = {only: allowlist, allow_fallbacks: false, data_collection: 'deny'} (a client-supplied provider.order is kept only when every entry is in the allowlist; anything else is dropped and logged), forwards to https://openrouter.ai with the real key, streams SSE back; GET paths proxied; refuses any client key other than the guard token with 401; appends one line per request {ts, model, providers_forced, client_order_dropped} to <project>/.claude-dev/run/openrouter-guard.log. title: v3 S2: Mac side — bootstrap preflight for Apple container, claude-dev register/open/stop/shell/logs/doctor/update/teardown against the image, web-url open
description: Why: the Mac half that creates and drives the VM (plan §5). What: bootstrap.sh preflight: Darwin + arm64 + macOS major >= 26 (sw_vers -productVersion), 'container' on PATH else print https://github.com/apple/container/releases and the installer line and exit 1, 'container system start' (idempotent; tolerate 'already running'), gh authenticated, git; then clone/pull the template into .claude-dev/template, link bin/, exec register. No brew bundle, no srt, no DMG, no rc-hook install. cmd_register: mkdir .claude-dev/{home,run,state}; seed .claude-dev/claude-orca.json {version:3, port:null, cpus:null, memory:null, extraMounts:[]} if absent; seed home .gitconfig from the Mac's global git config; choose the port once (claude-orca.json port, else 6768 or the next free via a bind probe; write run/port); 'container registry login ghcr.io' with gh auth token (username = gh api user login) then 'container image pull ghcr.io/joe-rayment/claude_orca:<tag>' where <tag> comes from .claude-dev/template/IMAGE_TAG (a one-line file, default latest) — on pull failure fall back to 'container build -t <same ref> -f <template>/Dockerfile <template>'; then cmd_open. cmd_open: if the container exists and is running → just open the URL; if it exists but stopped → 'container start'; else 'container run -d --name claude-orca-<name> --volume <project>:<project> --volume <project>/.claude-dev/home:/home/agent -p 127.0.0.1:<port>:<port> -e PROJECT_DIR=<project> -e ORCA_PORT=<port> -e HOST_UID=<id -u> -e GH_TOKEN=<gh auth token> [--cpus N --memory M from claude-orca.json] [--volume extra:ro] <image>'; then wait up to 120 s for <project>/.claude-dev/run/orca-web-url.txt (removed before the run so a stale one never opens), then 'open <url>' (CLAUDE_ORCA_OPEN=0 prints it instead) and print the three-line how-to-run. Container name = claude-orca-<derive_project_name>. stop: 'container stop <name>'. shell: 'container exec -it <name> zsh -l' (with --workdir <project>). logs: 'container logs -f <name>'. --doctor: container CLI present, service reachable ('container system status' or 'container ls' exit 0), image present, container state, port, web-url file, exits 2 on findings. --update: git pull template, image pull, stop+rm+recreate. --teardown: stop, rm, snapshot beads (existing helper), remove .claude-dev and ./claude-dev; also remove any v2 rc-hook block (existing rc_remove_block) since v2 folders may be upgraded. GH_TOKEN never printed. Every 'container' invocation goes through one function so tests can assert argv from a stub.

title: orca-launch: Orca uses the real ~/Library/Application Support (Electron ignores HOME on macOS) -> singleton lock EPERM, instant exit; pass --user-data-dir under a short per-project root
description: Why: on the user's Mac (2026-09-06) Orca.app exits immediately. orca-launch.log: readlink/create /Users/joerayment/Library/Application Support/orca/SingletonLock -> Operation not permitted, then Orca's own '[single-instance] Another Orca instance is already running' and exit; repo add times out waiting for orca-runtime.json. Root cause, verified from the extracted 1.4.197 bundle (out/main/index.js ~6808-6832): packaged Orca never calls app.setPath('userData'); Electron's appData on macOS comes from NSSearchPath, which ignores $HOME; and kei() then overwrites process.env.ORCA_USER_DATA_PATH with app.getPath('userData'), so our env var is discarded too. The Seatbelt profile denies /Users, so every write to the real Application Support fails, the lock first. Verified fix on the Linux build here (orca-linux-arm64.AppImage under Xvfb): with --user-data-dir=<dir>, SingletonLock, orca-runtime.json and the unix socket all landed in <dir> and nothing under ~/.config/orca -- Electron honors the switch natively, before Orca's lock. Second latent failure (claude-orca-qt9.10 part 1): the folder's userData path is ~90 bytes, plus o-<pid>-<4>.sock exceeds macOS's 104-byte sockaddr_un limit, so the transport would fail next. What: scripts/sandbox/orca-launch (1) host-side before sandbox-exec, creates a short per-project root: Darwin /private/tmp/co-<first 8 hex of sha1(project)>, elsewhere /tmp/co-<hash>, as a symlink to <project>/.claude-dev/home; refreshes it if it points elsewhere; refuses (exit 2, clear message) if the path exists and is not our symlink; CLAUDE_ORCA_SHORT_ROOT overrides the root. (2) exports ORCA_USER_DATA_PATH=<short root>/Library/Application Support/orca, mkdir -p the real dir, and passes --user-data-dir=<that path> as the first argument to the Orca binary. (3) refuses with a clear message when ORCA_USER_DATA_PATH length + 20 exceeds 100. (4) --print-command prints the exact env exports and sandbox-exec command line and exits 0 without launching, generating a profile, creating the symlink, or requiring sandbox-exec; --print-env prints just the exports. HOME and TMPDIR stay as they are. gen-orca-profile.sh needs no change: /private/tmp is readable and writes through the symlink resolve into the project.
design: Env knobs: CLAUDE_ORCA_SHORT_ROOT (override the short root, used by tests to force a too-long path), existing CLAUDE_ORCA_METADATA_TIMEOUT. Alternatives rejected: ORCA_BYPASS_SINGLE_INSTANCE_LOCK=1 (only skips the first casualty; the data dir is still denied); ORCA_E2E_USER_DATA_DIR (works but flips Orca's E2E mode on); a profileExceptions write-allow on the real Application Support (leaks Orca state outside the folder and makes every project share one lock). Supersedes part (1) of claude-orca-qt9.10; its dark-mode and doctor parts stay there. Mac behaviour (Seatbelt resolving the symlink into the project) is unverifiable here; the test proves the argv/env/symlink logic with a stub sandbox-exec.

title: orca-socket-unreachable probe FAILs on a real Mac with Orca running; register refusal gives no next step
description: User's first real run: [FAIL] orca-socket-unreachable -- orca status --json unexpectedly succeeded (orca.cli=false). Enforcement is allowUnixSockets=[] in gen-settings.sh + Seatbelt AF_UNIX deny; hypothesis: real orca CLI reaches the app over the localhost HTTP hook channel (or exits 0 without connecting), so the probe premise is wrong on any Mac with the app up — prior test passes were vacuous (stubbed orca). Awaiting DMG/CLI transport recon (scout-orca-dmg). Fix probe to test the enforced property, and make the register refusal print what to do next.

CHECK: bats tests/selftest.bats tests/orca-cli-mode.bats, then ./run-tests.sh.
PASS-IF: each bats run prints its 1..N plan, zero 'not ok' lines, and one 'ok' line per named case, names verbatim: 'socket probe: cli=false and runtime unreachable is a PASS' / 'socket probe: cli=false and runtime reachable is a FAIL naming the leak' / 'socket probe: cli=true and runtime reachable is a PASS' / 'socket probe: cli=true and runtime unreachable is N/A telling the user to launch Orca' / 'socket probe: unparseable status JSON falls back to the plain status exit code' / 'register refusal names the FAILed probes and the next step'; ./run-tests.sh exits 0 with zero 'not ok' lines.
FROZEN: tests/selftest.bats and tests/orca-cli-mode.bats from RED-AT.
CLASS: behavioral-bugfix.
NOTE: supersedes the cli-mode assertions at tests/orca-cli-mode.bats:263-302 whose stub modeled 'orca status --json exits 1 when unreachable' — falsified by the v1.4.197 binary (cli/handlers/core.js: exitCode=1 only when !json).
notes:

title: V6 First-real-run fixes: short HOME symlink for Orca's socket, dark-mode default, doctor socket check (verified with the Linux Orca)
description:
Why: the first real Orca run (Linux AppImage in this container, with the folder's .claude-dev/home as HOME) exposed one blocker and one preference. Blocker: Orca's daemon socket lives under the user-data dir derived from HOME, and a deep project path pushes it past the sockaddr_un limit (108 bytes on Linux, 104 on macOS) — Orca shows "couldn't start its local command transport… path is too long", the CLI becomes unavailable, and our launch-time `repo add` and the opt-in orchestration mode silently break. A short symlink to the same home directory (e.g. /tmp/oh → <project>/.claude-dev/home) fixed it. Preference: the user wants the sandboxed Orca in dark mode by default.
What: (1) scripts/sandbox/orca-launch creates, host-side before launch, a short per-project symlink to <project>/.claude-dev/home under a short root — Darwin: /private/tmp/co-<8 hex of sha1(project)> (readable in layer 1, never writable by layer 1 or 2; the symlink target resolves into the project so the profile's project rules apply); Linux: /tmp/co-<hash> — refreshes it if it points elsewhere, refuses (exit 2) if the path exists and is not our symlink, and exports HOME=<symlink> (TMPDIR and ORCA_USER_DATA_PATH stay as they are); it also computes the expected socket path length and refuses with a clear message when it would still exceed 100 bytes. `orca-launch --print-env` prints the exact env it would use (for the Linux demo and tests) and `--print-command` the sandbox-exec command line. (2) claude-dev --doctor warns when the socket path for the folder would exceed 100 bytes without the symlink and shows the symlink in the Orca section. (3) Dark mode: registration pre-seeds Orca's global settings file in the in-folder user-data dir (find the key and file from src/shared/global-settings-types.ts and src/main/global-settings* in the Orca clone; write only when the file is absent so a user's later choice is never overwritten) with the dark theme; the seed writes both the macOS location (Library/Application Support/orca/…) and the Linux one (.config/orca/…) under <project>/.claude-dev/home so either build picks it up; `sandbox.json` `orca.theme` (dark|light|system, default dark) selects it. (4) The Linux demo becomes the verification: launch the AppImage with `orca-launch --print-env`'s environment (no bypass switches added to the product; on Linux orca-launch itself refuses to launch because sandbox-exec is absent — the demo uses the printed env), confirm Orca starts in dark mode with the CLI transport working (no "path too long" modal), `repo add` succeeds, and screenshot it.
Boundaries: no profile content changes beyond none needed (the symlink target resolves into the project); no docs beyond README's sandbox.json options line for orca.theme and a knowledge-base note on the socket limit.
design: Evidence from the Linux run: socket path limit hit with HOME=<project>/.claude-dev/home; /tmp/oh symlink fixed it; user data at <HOME>/.config/orca; orca-runtime.json lists the unix socket and ws://127.0.0.1:6768; Linux CLI binary is resources/bin/orca-ide (macOS: Contents/Resources/bin/orca). Keep bash 3.2 lint clean; PASS-IF names verbatim as @test names; dry-run assertions before RED.

title: V2d Wrapper writes under layer 1: srt settings to a private per-launch temp dir agents cannot write; config-hash to run/
description:
Why: the wrapper (claude-orca-shell) and config-sync run INSIDE layer 1 when Orca launches a terminal, and layer 1 write-denies .claude-dev/state (host-owned). Two wrapper outputs still target it: the srt settings file state/srt-<sha1>.json and config-sync's state/config-hash. On the Mac every Orca terminal would fail to start (settings unwritable) or re-sync every time. The settings file is also security-sensitive: it defines layer 2, so it must not be written anywhere an agent (layer 2) can write — .claude-dev/run and tmp are agent-writable and an agent could race the wrapper between write and exec.
What: claude-orca-shell writes the srt settings file to a private per-launch directory that layer 1 allows and layer 2 denies: on Darwin `mktemp -d "$(getconf DARWIN_USER_TEMP_DIR)/claude-orca.XXXXXX"` (under /private/var/folders, which the Orca profile allows and srt's allowWrite never includes), mode 700, file mode 600, removed by an EXIT trap after exec is unreachable — or kept for srt to read: srt reads the file at startup before sandboxing, so the wrapper writes, execs srt, and the directory is cleaned by the next launch (document); elsewhere `mktemp -d`. config-sync's checksum moves to run/config-hash (the hash only gates re-sync; an agent tampering with it can only force or skip a sync, powers it already has via the config dir). gen-settings/gen-orca-profile: document which paths each layer writes. Tests in tests/wrapper-writes.bats (frozen) with the named cases; update tests/config-sync.bats / sandbox-config.bats / selftest.bats paths (unfrozen).
Boundaries: no probe additions (V3), no docs (V5).
design: Layer-1 allowed write roots per gen-orca-profile.sh: <project>, /private/var/folders, /dev. Layer 2 (srt) allowWrite: project-scoped only, so /private/var/folders is agent-denied. getconf DARWIN_USER_TEMP_DIR returns /var/folders/xx/.../T/ on macOS; absent on Linux (fall back to mktemp -d). Keep bash 3.2 lint clean.

title: V2b Keychain denied for the whole folder (services block, orca.keychain switch, doctor line); clipboard kept
description:
Why: the user wants no access to the Mac's Keychain from anything running in the folder — Orca and the agents keep their own credential stores inside the folder — while the clipboard keeps working. Seatbelt can deny the Keychain mach services by name for the whole process tree; nested layers inherit it.
What: scripts/sandbox/gen-orca-profile.sh gains a marked "services" block: (deny mach-lookup (global-name "com.apple.SecurityServer") (global-name "com.apple.securityd.xpc") (global-name "com.apple.ctkd") (global-name "com.apple.SecurityAgent") …) — derive the exact names from srt's macos-sandbox-utils.ts (it allows SecurityServer explicitly, which shows the name) and Apple's App Sandbox documentation; never deny com.apple.trustd, com.apple.pasteboard.1, com.apple.windowserver.active, com.apple.CoreDisplay, com.apple.fonts, com.apple.cfprefsd.daemon, com.apple.coreservices.launchservicesd. A sandbox.json switch orca.keychain (default false = denied) re-allows the family for users who want Mac Keychain sharing, documented as an isolation trade-off. Inside the sandbox, Claude Code's `security find-generic-password` fails (the S3 probe keychain-denied now has a real cause) and Claude Code stores `.credentials.json` in the folder config dir (S5 behaviour). Doctor prints "keychain: denied (folder-local credentials)" / "shared with macOS (orca.keychain=true)".
Boundaries: no other profile changes (V2 owns the filesystem rules), no docs (V5).

title: S2b Shell-entry hardening: bash 3.2 compatibility, non-interactive login shells, rc block placement
description:
Why: three findings from S2's verification and the real install run must be closed before the wrapper is trusted on a Mac. (1) macOS /bin/bash is 3.2: `arr+=("${empty[@]}")` under `set -u` aborts there, so gen-settings.sh (and any sibling script with the same idiom) would fail closed on every Mac shell whenever extraAllowWrite is empty — every script under scripts/ must run under bash 3.2. (2) Non-interactive login shells (`zsh -l -c …`, `bash -l -c …`) do not read .zshrc/.bashrc, so they start unsandboxed inside a bootstrapped folder; Orca's agent terminals are interactive and covered, but the hook must also live in .zprofile/.bash_profile-login path and preserve the -c command through the re-exec (zsh: $ZSH_EXECUTION_STRING; bash: $BASH_EXECUTION_STRING). (3) rc-install must append its block LAST (after Homebrew shellenv lines) and the bash side must cover .bash_profile and .profile-less setups consistently.

What: scripts/sandbox/* and scripts/launcher.sh rc-install made bash-3.2-safe (guard idiom `${arr[@]+"${arr[@]}"}`, no associative arrays, no mapfile, no ${var,,}); shellrc.zsh/.bash re-exec that carries the execution string: `exec claude-orca-shell --root R -- zsh -l -c "$ZSH_EXECUTION_STRING"` when set (bash likewise), interactive re-exec unchanged; claude-orca-shell accepts a trailing `-c <cmd>` for the inner shell; rc-install writes the marker block into ~/.zprofile as well as ~/.zshrc (both guarded by CLAUDE_ORCA_SANDBOXED so the second source is a no-op), keeps ~/.bash_profile, and always appends after existing content; tests/helpers/ensure_bash32 builds GNU bash 3.2.57 into tests/.cache/bash32 (from the scratchpad copy at /tmp/claude-1000/-workspace/7037bfad-67da-4b5e-9adb-944b260fc264/scratchpad/bash32/install when present, else from ftp.gnu.org) so the suite can run the scripts under the real macOS bash version.

Boundaries: no self-test probes (S3), no config sync (S4). tests/sandbox-config.bats and tests/bootstrap.bats are unfrozen (S1/S2 closed) and must stay green; add cases there only if a premise changed.

title: S2 Sandbox wrapper: srt settings generator, scope derivation, env, shell re-exec, fail-closed
description:
Why: the security core. Every shell opened in a bootstrapped folder (by Orca, Terminal.app, or `orca terminal create`) must re-exec itself inside srt/sandbox-exec with a scope derived from the folder, before any agent binary runs.

What: ~/.claude-orca/bin/claude-orca-root (primary checkout via `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`, falls back to walking up for .claude-dev/sandbox.json), ~/.claude-orca/bin/claude-orca-shell (generates srt settings, sets env, `exec srt --settings <file> -c 'exec zsh -l'`), shellrc.zsh + shellrc.bash (sourced from the user's rc via one marker-delimited line installed/removed idempotently by `claude-dev`), scripts/sandbox/gen-settings.sh (pure function: inputs → JSON).

Scope: primary session allowWrite=[<project>, <project>/.claude-dev/home, <project>/.claude-dev/tmp]; linked worktree session allowWrite=[<worktree>, <primary>/.git, <primary>/.beads, <primary>/.claude-dev/home, <primary>/.claude-dev/tmp]. denyRead=[real HOME]; allowRead=[<project>, <worktree>, ~/.claude-orca, ~/.local/bin, ~/.local/share/claude, ~/.orca/agent-hooks]. Extra denyWrite (host-executed files): orca.yaml, .worktreeinclude, .envrc, .beads/hooks/**. network.allowedDomains = defaults ∪ validated sandbox.json extras; strictAllowlist true; allowLocalBinding true; allowPty true; enableWeakerNetworkIsolation true; allowAppleEvents false; allowUnixSockets [] (S9 may add the Orca runtime dir). Env inside: HOME=<primary>/.claude-dev/home, CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=$HOME/.claude, TMPDIR=<primary>/.claude-dev/tmp, GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL, GH_CONFIG_DIR, BEADS_DIR=<primary>/.beads, ORCA_USER_DATA_PATH=<real ~>/Library/Application Support/orca, DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1, CLAUDE_ORCA_SANDBOXED=1, CLAUDE_ORCA_REAL_HOME, PATH=/opt/homebrew/bin:<real ~>/.local/bin:~/.claude-orca/template/bin:...

Fail closed: srt or sandbox-exec missing, generator error, or unvalidated sandbox.json → the shellrc defines refusing functions for claude, codex, gemini, opencode and prints the reason; never continue unsandboxed silently.

Boundaries: no auth/credential masking config beyond the hook point (S5), no Orca hook merge (S6), no self-test (S3). The wrapper treats everything under <project> as untrusted data.
design: gen-settings.sh is a pure bash function taking (primary, worktree, real_home, sandbox_json, mode) and printing JSON via jq so tests can assert exact documents. Settings file path: <primary>/.claude-dev/state/srt-<sha1(worktree)>.json. Schema validation test uses `node -e` importing the installed sandbox-runtime package (stub-installed in tests from the scratchpad clone or npm cache; skip with a clear reason only if node is absent). Real srt facts used: deny default; writes allow-only; allowLocalBinding opens localhost outbound; allowPty for /dev/ttys*; mandatory write-denies under cwd for shell rc files, .mcp.json, .claude/agents, .claude/commands, .git/hooks, .git/config (srt src/sandbox/sandbox-utils.ts:15-40, macos-sandbox-utils.ts:79-106).

title: S2 Sandbox wrapper: srt settings generator, scope derivation, env, shell re-exec, fail-closed
description:
Why: the security core. Every shell opened in a bootstrapped folder (by Orca, Terminal.app, or `orca terminal create`) must re-exec itself inside srt/sandbox-exec with a scope derived from the folder, before any agent binary runs.

What: ~/.claude-orca/bin/claude-orca-root (primary checkout via `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`, falls back to walking up for .claude-dev/sandbox.json), ~/.claude-orca/bin/claude-orca-shell (generates srt settings, sets env, `exec srt --settings <file> -c 'exec zsh -l'`), shellrc.zsh + shellrc.bash (sourced from the user's rc via one marker-delimited line installed/removed idempotently by `claude-dev`), scripts/sandbox/gen-settings.sh (pure function: inputs → JSON).

Scope: primary session allowWrite=[<project>, <project>/.claude-dev/home, <project>/.claude-dev/tmp]; linked worktree session allowWrite=[<worktree>, <primary>/.git, <primary>/.beads, <primary>/.claude-dev/home, <primary>/.claude-dev/tmp]. denyRead=[real HOME]; allowRead=[<project>, <worktree>, ~/.claude-orca, ~/.local/bin, ~/.local/share/claude, ~/.orca/agent-hooks]. Extra denyWrite (host-executed files): orca.yaml, .worktreeinclude, .envrc, .beads/hooks/**. network.allowedDomains = defaults ∪ validated sandbox.json extras; strictAllowlist true; allowLocalBinding true; allowPty true; enableWeakerNetworkIsolation true; allowAppleEvents false; allowUnixSockets [] (S9 may add the Orca runtime dir). Env inside: HOME=<primary>/.claude-dev/home, CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=$HOME/.claude, TMPDIR=<primary>/.claude-dev/tmp, GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL, GH_CONFIG_DIR, BEADS_DIR=<primary>/.beads, ORCA_USER_DATA_PATH=<real ~>/Library/Application Support/orca, DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1, CLAUDE_ORCA_SANDBOXED=1, CLAUDE_ORCA_REAL_HOME, PATH=/opt/homebrew/bin:<real ~>/.local/bin:~/.claude-orca/template/bin:...

Fail closed: srt or sandbox-exec missing, generator error, or unvalidated sandbox.json → the shellrc defines refusing functions for claude, codex, gemini, opencode and prints the reason; never continue unsandboxed silently.

Boundaries: no auth/credential masking config beyond the hook point (S5), no Orca hook merge (S6), no self-test (S3). The wrapper treats everything under <project> as untrusted data.
design: gen-settings.sh is a pure bash function taking (primary, worktree, real_home, sandbox_json, mode) and printing JSON via jq so tests can assert exact documents. Settings file path: <primary>/.claude-dev/state/srt-<sha1(worktree)>.json. Schema validation test uses `node -e` importing the installed sandbox-runtime package (stub-installed in tests from the scratchpad clone or npm cache; skip with a clear reason only if node is absent). Real srt facts used: deny default; writes allow-only; allowLocalBinding opens localhost outbound; allowPty for /dev/ttys*; mandatory write-denies under cwd for shell rc files, .mcp.json, .claude/agents, .claude/commands, .git/hooks, .git/config (srt src/sandbox/sandbox-utils.ts:15-40, macos-sandbox-utils.ts:79-106).

title: Main-session off-ramp: stop (default) or compact-and-continue at ~40% context
description:
OBJECTIVE: the MAIN Claude Code session (the orchestrator, no agent_id) takes an off-ramp at ~40% of its context window instead of running on to 80%+. User's report (2026-10-04): in a remote session the context goes to 80%+ and they cannot see it. Two modes: `stop` (default) -- save state to a bead, stop, and SAY WHY; `continue` -- save state, keep going, the session compacts itself and resumes from the bead.

MEASURED 2026-10-04 on Claude Code 2.1.288 (interactive TUI in a pty, haiku, --setting-sources project):
- Default is REACTIVE: no threshold compaction at all; the TUI shows "N% context used" and the session grows to the full window (19->79% observed, no compact). Opus 5.5 has a native 1M window, so 80% = 800k tokens.
- CLAUDE_AUTOCOMPACT_PCT_OVERRIDE alone: no effect (still reactive).
- CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW=100000: threshold compaction enforced ("N% until auto-compact"), compacted at preTokens ~70k, continued the task after the compact.
- settings env {CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW:1000000, CLAUDE_AUTOCOMPACT_PCT_OVERRIDE:40} via --settings: window clamps to the model window (200k haiku), compacted at preTokens 91.8k after a 77.8k call -> threshold 80k = 40%. So window=1000000 + PCT=P compacts at P% of ANY model's window. Code: threshold = min(floor(w*P/100), w-13000).
- Native-1M models in 2.1.288's table: claude-opus-4-7, -4-8, -5, -5-5, claude-sonnet-5, -5-5, claude-fable-5, -5-1. Everything else 200k (haiku-4-5, older).

SHARED CONTRACT (slice .1 implements, slice .2 wires):

Script scripts/offramp.sh, bin/offramp -> ../scripts/offramp.sh (relative symlink). bash, `set -u`, sources scripts/lib/paths.sh for run_dir (CLAUDE_ORCA_ROOT overrides the root, as everywhere).

Mode file: "$(run_dir)/offramp.json" = {"mode":"stop"|"continue", "pending":{"bead":"<id>","at":"<UTC ISO-8601>"}} (pending optional). Mode = file .mode if valid, else env CLAUDE_ORCA_OFFRAMP_MODE if "stop"/"continue", else "stop".

Settings (env; a value that is not a non-negative integer falls back to its default):
- CLAUDE_ORCA_OFFRAMP_AT        default 40; 0 turns every hook mode off (silent).
- CLAUDE_ORCA_OFFRAMP_STOP_AT   default 45 -- stop-mode refusal line.
- CLAUDE_ORCA_OFFRAMP_BACKSTOP_AT default 60 -- continue-mode refusal line.
- CLAUDE_ORCA_OFFRAMP_WINDOW    tokens; a positive value overrides the window.
Compaction is ON iff CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW is a positive integer AND CLAUDE_AUTOCOMPACT_PCT_OVERRIDE is an integer 1..100; COMPACT = that pct. Effective mode E = mode, except continue with compaction OFF -> E=stop (and texts add the NO-COMPACT line).

Context: from .transcript_path (the main transcript), the LAST row (tail -n 400) with .type=="assistant" and .message.usage: tokens = input_tokens + cache_read_input_tokens + cache_creation_input_tokens (NO output_tokens -- this matches Claude Code's own "% context used"). Window: CLAUDE_ORCA_OFFRAMP_WINDOW if positive; else 200000 if CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_1M_CONTEXT is non-empty and not 0/false; else 1000000 if that row's .message.model contains "[1m]" or matches claude-opus-4-7*|claude-opus-4-8*|claude-opus-5*|claude-sonnet-5*|claude-fable-5*; else 200000. pct = floor(tokens*100/window).

Main loop only: a payload with a non-empty .agent_id exits 0 silently (sub-agents are context-meter's). Fails open everywhere: no jq, bad stdin, missing transcript, no usage row -> exit 0, no output.

HOOK MODES
--post (PostToolUse): pct < AT -> delete this session's marker, no output. pct >= AT -> marker = "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/claude-orca-offramp/<transcript_path with every / replaced by _>"; marker absent -> FULL text for E, create marker; marker present -> E=stop: REMINDER; E=continue: no output. Output JSON {hookSpecificOutput:{hookEventName:"PostToolUse",additionalContext:TEXT}}.
--pre (PreToolUse): line R = STOP_AT when E=stop, BACKSTOP_AT when E=continue. pct < R -> no output. pct >= R -> allowed silently when tool_name=="Bash" and the first word of .tool_input.command (leading whitespace stripped) is bd, git or offramp; anything else -> {hookSpecificOutput:{hookEventName:"PreToolUse",permissionDecision:"deny",permissionDecisionReason:TEXT}} with REFUSAL text for E.
--session-start (SessionStart): if the mode file has .pending -> print RESUME (plain stdout) and remove .pending (mode kept); else no output.

CLI (output is for the user; /offramp prints it verbatim)
offramp | offramp status -> STATUS. offramp stop | offramp continue -> write .mode (keep .pending), print SWITCH text. offramp handoff <id> -> id must match ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$ else exit 2; writes .pending {bead,at}, prints "off-ramp: handoff recorded -- the next session (after /clear or a compaction) is pointed at bead <id>." Anything else -> usage on stderr, exit 2.

EXACT TEXTS ({pct} {at} {stop} {backstop} {compact} {bead} {mode} substituted; lines joined with \n)
FULL, E=stop:
[off-ramp] this session's context is at {pct}% of its window -- past the {at}% off-ramp (mode: stop). Take the off-ramp now; start nothing new:
1. Finish only the step in hand and commit it.
2. Save a HANDOFF to the bead you are working on (bd create one if the work has none): bd update <id> --notes "HANDOFF / done: ... / left: ... / facts: ... / next: ..."
3. Run: offramp handoff <id>
4. End your turn with one message to the user that starts "Off-ramp: context is at {pct}%, so I stopped." -- then what is finished, what is left, the bead id, and: "Type /clear, then resume to carry on -- or /offramp continue to let the session compact itself and keep going."
From {stop}% every tool call except bd, git and offramp is refused.
NO-COMPACT line (inserted as line 2 of FULL and appended to REFUSAL when mode=continue but compaction is OFF):
(mode is continue, but this session has no auto-compaction -- it started before that setting -- so it stops instead; a new session compacts.)
REMINDER, E=stop:
[off-ramp] context at {pct}% (off-ramp {at}%): save the HANDOFF, run offramp handoff <id>, and end your turn telling the user why you stopped.
FULL, E=continue:
[off-ramp] this session's context is at {pct}% of its window -- past the {at}% off-ramp (mode: continue). Save your place now, then keep working:
1. Finish the step in hand and commit it.
2. Save a HANDOFF to the bead you are working on (bd create one if the work has none): bd update <id> --notes "HANDOFF / done: ... / left: ... / facts: ... / next: ..."
3. Run: offramp handoff <id>
4. Carry on with the work. The session compacts itself at about {compact}% and resumes from that bead; keep the HANDOFF current as you go.
REFUSAL, E=stop:
[off-ramp] context is at {pct}% -- past the {stop}% stop line (mode: stop): only bd, git and offramp commands run now. Save the HANDOFF (bd update <id> --notes "HANDOFF ..."; offramp handoff <id>), then end your turn with a message to the user that starts "Off-ramp: context is at {pct}%, so I stopped." and tells them to type /clear, then resume.
REFUSAL, E=continue:
[off-ramp] context is at {pct}% -- past the {backstop}% backstop and the session has not compacted (mode: continue): only bd, git and offramp commands run now. Save the HANDOFF (bd update <id> --notes "HANDOFF ..."; offramp handoff <id>), then end your turn with a message to the user that starts "Off-ramp: context is at {pct}%, so I stopped." and tells them to type /compact or /clear, then resume.
RESUME:
[off-ramp] the previous context ended at the off-ramp; its HANDOFF is in bead {bead}. Run bd show {bead} and continue from its "left:" line -- do not redo "done:". (mode: {mode})
STATUS (line 2 depends on compaction; line 3 only with a pending handoff):
off-ramp: mode {mode} -- at {at}% context the session <stop: "saves a HANDOFF to its bead and stops, saying why; tool calls are refused from {stop}%." | continue: "saves a HANDOFF to its bead and keeps going; tool calls are refused from {backstop}% if it has not compacted.">
compaction: at {compact}% of the window.   | compaction: off in this session -- one started after the settings change compacts at the configured percent.
pending handoff: {bead} (since {at-timestamp})
switch: /offramp stop | /offramp continue
SWITCH:
stop: off-ramp mode: stop -- at {at}% context the session saves a HANDOFF to its bead and stops, saying why; /clear, then resume to carry on.
continue: off-ramp mode: continue -- at {at}% context the session saves a HANDOFF to its bead and keeps going; it compacts itself at about {compact}% and resumes from the bead. title: 15-claude-on-path failed on the 2026-10-01 Mac boot: its download temp file vanished from versions/ before the checksum
description: Evidence (claude-orca-34g's observation, 2026-10-01 23:18 recreate): run/provision/15-claude-on-path.status 1, log 'sha256sum: ~/.local/share/claude/versions/.2.1.287.claude-orca.tmp: No such file or directory ... installing 2.1.287 failed; ~/.local/bin/claude is untouched' -- the folder stayed on 2.1.284. The same script run alone on 2026-10-02 into a scratch HOME installs 2.1.287 in 5 s, so the download itself works. curl -fsS ... -o "$tmp" only reaches sha256sum when curl exits 0, so the file existed and then disappeared, or curl wrote nothing: the temp file is a fixed name INSIDE versions/, the directory Claude Code's own native installer manages (and cleans) -- a claude starting during boot, or a second concurrent run of the step, can remove or truncate it. Fix: download to a unique mktemp file outside versions/ but on the same filesystem (e.g. ~/.local/share/claude/.claude-orca-dl.XXXXXX), refuse an empty file ([ -s ]), then mv -f into versions/<v> atomically; log curl's exit code and a checksum mismatch distinctly so the next failure names itself. Container script: mac-e2e debt, commit subject says UNVERIFIED on a Mac.
acceptance_criteria:
FILES: scripts/container/provision.d/15-claude-on-path, tests/provision-claude-on-path.bats only.
CHANGE (the install block near the end, today: tmp="$VDIR/.$latest.claude-orca.tmp"; curl ... -o "$tmp" && sha256sum -c && chmod && mv -f && ln -sfn):
 - download dir: DL_DIR="$(dirname "$VDIR")" (i.e. ~/.local/share/claude -- same filesystem as versions/, but not the directory Claude Code's own installer manages); tmp="$(mktemp "$DL_DIR/.claude-orca-dl.XXXXXX")" (fail -> message + exit 1).

Keep the final 'installing <v> failed; <link> is untouched' line on every failure path.

title: recon fan-out: parallel calls started in the same second share one log/receipt and clobber each other's answers
description: Seen 2026-10-02: four 'recon "..." &' calls launched together; scripts/recon.sh names its log/receipt STEM=$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)-$SLUG, so calls on the same model in the same second share <run>/recon/<STEM>.log -- each truncates it (: >"$LOG") and opencode writes into it, and each then parses the shared log for its stdout answer. The rulebook and memory recon-follows-the-tier-backend both prescribe run_in_background fan-out, so this is the normal path. title: B3 tier: openai:<family|id> binds the OpenAI subscription, distinct from OpenRouter
description:
OBJECTIVE
/tier can bind a role to the user's OpenAI subscription and visibly tell it apart from the same OpenAI model on OpenRouter. Read epic claude-orca-c3p (GROUND TRUTH, DESIGN). Slice B2 (claude-orca-c3p.2, merged before this starts) already added to scripts/lib/tier-roles.sh: TIER_OPENAI_WORKER_MODEL, TIER_OPENAI_RECON_MODEL, tier_openai_role_default, tier_openai_auth_file, tier_openai_ready, tier_openai_catalogue, tier_openai_resolve -- use them, do not re-implement them.

THE GRAMMAR (everything that exists today keeps its meaning)
- `openai`                 -> backend orca, agent opencode, model = tier_openai_role_default <role> (worker openai/~gpt-terra-latest, recon openai/~gpt-luna-latest)
- `openai:<family|id>`     -> backend orca, agent opencode, model from openai_spec_model (below)
- unchanged: a bare route name (luna, glm-flash ...), a bare vendor/model id (openai/gpt-5.6-luna) and a free-text phrase are OpenRouter, exactly as today.
- an effort rides on it as everywhere: openai:luna@high, "openai:luna (high)", "recon openai:luna high".

FILES (edit/create only these)
- scripts/tier-set.sh
- config/claude-commands/tier.md   (description and argument-hint mention openai:luna; keep the body line untouched)
- tests/tier-openai.bats           (new)
- tests/tier-phrases.bats          (ONLY the one expectation `applies to OpenRouter roles only` at ~line 179, updated to the new wording)
- tests/INDEX.md                   (one entry for the new file)

scripts/tier-set.sh
(a) new helper openai_spec_model <rest> -- prints openai/<...> or returns 1 with a message on stderr:
    n = <rest> lower-cased, each run of whitespace -> "-", a leading "openai/" stripped. Empty n -> "tier-set: 'openai:' needs a model family or id, e.g. openai:luna or openai:gpt-5.6-luna -- nothing bound".
    n of the form ~*-latest -> openai/<n> as is.
    cat = "$(tier_openai_catalogue 2>/dev/null)" (empty on failure). When cat is a non-empty array:
      some .id == n                      -> openai/<n>
      fam = n when it starts with "gpt-", else "gpt-<n>"; some .family == fam -> openai/~<fam>-latest
      otherwise -> "tier-set: no OpenAI model or family '<rest>' -- families: <the catalogue's distinct families, "gpt-" stripped, sorted, space-separated>; or pin one with openai:<id> (/tier models openai lists them); nothing bound", return 1.
    When cat is empty: n containing a digit -> openai/<n>, else openai/~gpt-<n without a leading gpt->-latest, plus the stderr note "tier-set: no OpenAI model list to check '<rest>' against -- bound unchecked".
(b) resolve_worker_recon_phrase: add `openai)` and `openai:*)` cases (before the `openrouter)` case) producing b=orca a=opencode and the model above.
(c) the checker case: add `openai)` / `openai:*)` the same way (B=orca A=opencode PIN=true), alongside its openrouter forms.
(d) not signed in: after any bind whose model starts with openai/ and `tier_openai_ready` fails, print exactly these two lines (once per command):
      → not signed in to OpenAI yet -- this binding is saved but cannot run until this folder is signed in with your ChatGPT subscription.
      → run  /tier auth openai  to open a sign-in tab now.
    In the worker|recon and checker paths this replaces the OpenRouter not-authenticated note for an openai/ model (an openrouter model keeps today's note, unchanged). The positional trio path (which prints no auth note today) prints this pair once when the worker or recon model is openai/ and not signed in -- and still prints nothing for OpenRouter there.
(e) the effort-ignored note, in every place it is printed: "tier: effort '<e>' applies to opencode roles only (OpenRouter or OpenAI) -- ignored for <role>".
(f) `tier-set models openai [<words>]` -- handled BEFORE the existing `models` block, only when $2 is openai:
      cat empty -> stderr "tier-set: no OpenAI model list available -- run /tier auth openai first", exit 1.
      header: tier_openai_ready -> "OpenAI models your ChatGPT subscription serves (opencode models openai):"; else "OpenAI catalogue -- not signed in, so your subscription may serve fewer (/tier auth openai):"
      "families -- each follows its newest release:" then one line per distinct non-empty family, sorted: "  openai:<family minus gpt->  -> <tier_openai_resolve openai/~<family>-latest, minus the openai/ prefix>"
      "pin one model:" then "  openai:<id>" per id (only ids containing every one of <words>, lower-cased substring match, when words are given). Exit 0.
(g) preset_reserved: add openai and openrouter to its reserved words.
(h) show_guide: add, keeping the existing column layout,
      under HOW TO SET IT:  /tier opus openai:terra openai:luna@high         your OpenAI (ChatGPT) subscription: openai: before the name
      under NAMES, after the OpenRouter lines:
        OpenAI:     openai:luna  openai:terra  openai:sol  openai:astra   your ChatGPT subscription, through opencode
                    a family follows its newest release your plan serves; openai:gpt-5.6-luna pins one; bare openai = the role's default
                    no openai: prefix = OpenRouter -- luna and openai/gpt-5.6-luna both name OpenRouter's copy
      EFFORT header becomes: EFFORT -- OpenRouter and OpenAI models (a Claude role ignores it)
      under ALSO: /tier auth openai  sign in with your ChatGPT subscription    /tier models openai  what your subscription serves
(i) show_help: one paragraph: an openai: binding is opencode on the openai provider, signed in with the user's ChatGPT subscription; a family alias (openai/~gpt-luna-latest) is resolved when the worker starts to the newest model of that family the subscription serves; requests go straight to OpenAI, so no guard and no provider allowlist is involved (OpenAI serves them itself); an unsigned folder still saves the binding and names /tier auth openai.
(j) the header comment's v2 spec list gains: openai | openai:<family|id> -> backend orca, agent opencode, model openai/...
Do NOT implement `tier-set auth openai` here -- that is slice B4; leave the auth block as it is.

tests/tier-openai.bats (fast; no network, no real opencode). Copy the setup of tests/tier-phrases.bats (TIER_STATE_FILE, TIER_SETTINGS_LOCAL, TIER_ROUTES_FILE = the shipped routes, TIER_MODELS_FETCH=0, TIER_ORCA_PROBE_DISABLE=1, pinned script path), plus TIER_OPENAI_MODELS_FILE = a fixture array [gpt-5.6-luna, gpt-5.6-luna-fast (gpt-luna, 2026-07-09); gpt-5.6-terra (gpt-terra, 2026-07-09); gpt-5.6-sol (gpt-sol, 2026-07-09); gpt-6.1-sol (gpt-sol, 2026-09-29); gpt-5.4-mini (gpt-mini, 2026-03-17)] and TIER_OPENAI_AUTH_FILE = a signed-in fixture ({"openai":{"type":"oauth","refresh":"rt-x","access":"a","expires":1,"accountId":"acct"}}) unless a case says not signed in (point it at a missing path). Every @test opens with `# Guards:` / `# Fails if:` / `# Run:`. Cases:
 1. `opus openai:terra openai:luna@high` -> roles.worker == {backend:"orca",agent:"opencode",model:"openai/~gpt-terra-latest",pinned:true}; roles.recon has model "openai/~gpt-luna-latest", variant "high"; output contains "orca:opencode:openai/~gpt-luna-latest@high".
 2. the distinction holds: `opus luna luna@high` binds recon model "openrouter/~openai/gpt-luna-latest"; `opus openai/gpt-5.6-luna` binds worker model "openrouter/openai/gpt-5.6-luna".
 3. an id pins one model: `worker openai:gpt-5.6-luna` -> "openai/gpt-5.6-luna"; the single comma argument "opus, openai:GPT 5.6 Luna, openai:luna (high)" -> worker "openai/gpt-5.6-luna", recon "openai/~gpt-luna-latest" with variant "high".
 4. `worker openai:nope` -> exit 1, stderr contains "luna" and "terra", tier.json byte-identical to before.
 5. bare: `recon openai` -> "openai/~gpt-luna-latest"; `worker openai` -> "openai/~gpt-terra-latest".
 6. not signed in: `worker openai:luna` -> exit 0, binding saved, output contains "/tier auth openai"; signed in -> output does not.
 7. the trio when not signed in prints the sign-in pair exactly once.
 8. `checker openai:sol` -> roles.checker model "openai/~gpt-sol-latest", agent "opencode", backend "orca".
 9. `models openai` -> output contains "openai:luna" and "gpt-5.6-luna", and "openai:sol" on the same line as "gpt-6.1-sol"; `models openai mini` lists openai:gpt-5.4-mini and not openai:gpt-5.6-luna.
10. `fable sonnet@high haiku` -> output contains "OpenAI" in the ignored-effort note.
11. no catalogue at all (TIER_OPENAI_MODELS_FILE at an empty array, TIER_OPENAI_AUTH_FILE missing, TIER_OPENCODE_MODELS_CACHE at a missing path): `worker openai:luna` binds "openai/~gpt-luna-latest" and says "bound unchecked".

BOUNDARIES

title: B2 openai launch: openai/ models through orca-dispatch and recon (one launch-config writer)
description:
OBJECTIVE
An `openai/...` model (OpenAI through the user's ChatGPT subscription, signed in with opencode's own login) runs through the same two launch paths an `openrouter/...` model does: orca-dispatch (headless worker-run AND --tui) and `recon`. Read the epic claude-orca-c3p first: its GROUND TRUTH and DESIGN are the spec's background. Every openrouter/ behaviour stays byte-for-byte what it is today.

FILES (edit/create only these)
- scripts/lib/tier-roles.sh        (append the OpenAI helpers below; bash 3.2)
- scripts/lib/opencode-launch.sh   (new, sourced; bash 3.2)
- scripts/lib/orca-orch.sh         (orca_opencode_command)
- scripts/orca-dispatch.sh
- scripts/recon.sh
- tests/opencode-openai-launch.bats (new)
- tests/INDEX.md                    (one entry for the new file)

1. scripts/lib/tier-roles.sh -- append, next to the OpenRouter helpers:
   TIER_OPENAI_WORKER_MODEL="openai/~gpt-terra-latest"
   TIER_OPENAI_RECON_MODEL="openai/~gpt-luna-latest"
   tier_openai_role_default <role>  -- recon -> TIER_OPENAI_RECON_MODEL, anything else -> TIER_OPENAI_WORKER_MODEL.
   tier_openai_auth_file  -- prints $TIER_OPENAI_AUTH_FILE when set, else ${XDG_DATA_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share}/opencode/auth.json.
   tier_openai_ready  -- exit 0 when that file is readable JSON and either (.openai.type == "oauth" and .openai.refresh is a non-empty string) or (.openai.type == "api" and .openai.key is a non-empty string); else 1. Never prints. jq missing -> 1.
   tier_openai_catalogue  -- prints a JSON array of {id, family, release_date} (strings; missing -> ""). Source, first that yields a non-empty array:
     a) $TIER_OPENAI_MODELS_FILE when set: that file's JSON array, verbatim (tests);
     b) when tier_openai_ready: `${TIER_OPENCODE_BIN:-opencode} models openai --verbose 2>/dev/null`, parsed as: drop every line that starts with "openai/", then `jq -s 'map({id: (.id // ""), family: (.family // ""), release_date: (.release_date // "")})'`;
     c) ${TIER_OPENCODE_MODELS_CACHE:-$HOME/.cache/opencode/models.json}: `.openai.models | to_entries | map({id: .key, family: (.value.family // ""), release_date: (.value.release_date // "")})`.
     Nothing usable -> print nothing, exit 1.
   tier_openai_resolve <model>  -- prints the model to launch:
     openai/~<fam>-latest  -> openai/<id>, the newest catalogue entry whose .family == <fam>: highest release_date, then the SHORTEST id (gpt-5.6-luna beats gpt-5.6-luna-fast), then the lexically larger id. No entry for <fam> -> message on stderr naming the family and `opencode models openai`, exit 1.
     anything else (openai/<id>, openrouter/..., other) -> printed unchanged, exit 0, catalogue not consulted.

title: B1 tests: a stub OpenAI (ChatGPT backend + auth server) that the real opencode talks to
description:
OBJECTIVE
A reusable test harness that lets the REAL opencode binary run an `openai/...` model under a FAKE ChatGPT login with no traffic to OpenAI, so later slices can prove their launch path end to end. opencode honours HTTPS_PROXY (measured), so the stub is an HTTP proxy that terminates TLS for chatgpt.com and auth.openai.com with a test CA and tunnels every other host untouched.

FILES (create/edit only these)
- tests/helpers/openai-stub.py      (new; python3 stdlib + the `openssl` CLI only)
- tests/helpers/openai-stub.bash    (new; functions sourced by bats files)
- tests/openai-stub-real.bats       (new)
- tests/INDEX.md                    (one entry for the new bats file, same format as its neighbours)
- run-tests.sh                      (ONLY if the new bats file takes > 20 s: add openai-stub-real.bats to SLOW_FILES)

tests/helpers/openai-stub.py
- Usage: python3 tests/helpers/openai-stub.py --dir <D>
- At start, with the openssl CLI, write into <D>: ca.key + ca.pem (self-signed, CN=claude-orca-test-ca, 2 days) and leaf.key + leaf.pem signed by that CA with subjectAltName DNS:chatgpt.com,DNS:auth.openai.com (use an -extfile for the SAN).
- Listen on 127.0.0.1 port 0 (a free port); once listening write the port number to <D>/port. Run until killed. One thread per connection.
- It is an HTTP proxy. On `CONNECT host:port HTTP/1.1`:
  * host chatgpt.com or auth.openai.com: reply `HTTP/1.1 200 Connection established\r\n\r\n`, wrap the client socket server-side with ssl (leaf cert), then serve HTTP/1.1 requests on it in a loop (keep-alive; read the body by Content-Length, or decode `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`).
  * any other host: connect to host:port and pipe bytes both ways until either side closes (blind tunnel -- opencode's catalogue/npm fetches must keep working).
- Append one JSON line per served request to <D>/requests.jsonl: {"host","method","path","headers":{lower-cased name: value},"body": parsed JSON when the body is JSON, the urldecoded form as an object when it is application/x-www-form-urlencoded, else the raw string}.
- Routes:
  * chatgpt.com POST /backend-api/codex/responses -> 200, content-type text/event-stream, a Responses-API SSE stream whose assistant text is env STUB_REPLY (default STUB-OK). Start from this sequence and adjust until real opencode accepts it: response.created, response.output_item.added (type message, role assistant, empty content), response.content_part.added (output_text ""), response.output_text.delta (the text), response.output_text.done, response.content_part.done, response.output_item.done (message with [{type:output_text,text,annotations:[]}]), response.completed (status completed, usage {input_tokens:11,output_tokens:3,total_tokens:14,input_tokens_details:{cached_tokens:0},output_tokens_details:{reasoning_tokens:2}}). Each event as `event: <type>\ndata: <json>\n\n`; echo the request body's model in the response objects.
  * auth.openai.com POST /oauth/token -> JSON {access_token: JWT, id_token: JWT, refresh_token: "rt-<n>" with n counting 1,2,3 per call, expires_in: 3600, token_type: "Bearer"}. JWT = base64url(header) "." base64url(payload) "." "sig", payload {"https://api.openai.com/auth":{"chatgpt_account_id":"acct-test"},"exp": now+3600}.
  * auth.openai.com POST /api/accounts/deviceauth/usercode -> {"device_auth_id":"dev-1","user_code":"TEST-CODE","interval":"1"}
  * auth.openai.com POST /api/accounts/deviceauth/token -> {"authorization_code":"ac-test","code_verifier":"cv-test"}
  * anything else on those two hosts -> 404 {"error":"stub: no route"} (still logged).

tests/helpers/openai-stub.bash (functions)
- openai_stub_start <dir>: start the stub in the background (pid -> <dir>/pid), wait up to 10 s for <dir>/port, export OPENAI_STUB_DIR and OPENAI_STUB_PORT.
- openai_stub_stop: kill that pid (from teardown).
- openai_stub_env: print the env assignments a client needs, one per line: HTTPS_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:<port> and NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=<dir>/ca.pem. ONLY if real opencode ignores NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS (find out by running it), print NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0 instead -- and say in the file's header comment which one was needed and the evidence.
- openai_stub_login <data-home> [expired]: write <data-home>/opencode/auth.json, mode 600: {"openai":{"type":"oauth","refresh":"rt-0","access":<JWT as above>,"expires":<epoch ms: now+1 day, or now-1 hour when $2 = expired>,"accountId":"acct-test"}}.
- openai_stub_home <dir>: create <dir>/home and copy $HOME/.cache/opencode/models.json to <dir>/home/.cache/opencode/models.json so opencode need not fetch its catalogue (callers `skip` when the source file is absent).

tests/openai-stub-real.bats
- skip the whole file when `opencode`, `openssl` or `python3` is not on PATH. setup: openai_stub_home + openai_stub_start in $BATS_TEST_TMPDIR; teardown: openai_stub_stop.
- Every opencode call runs as: env -u OPENAI_API_KEY -u OPENROUTER_API_KEY HOME=<tmp>/home XDG_DATA_HOME=<tmp>/data <the openai_stub_env lines> opencode ...
- Cases (each @test opens with the rulebook's three comment lines `# Guards:` / `# Fails if:` / `# Run:`):
  1. a fake ChatGPT login reaches the stub through opencode's own OAuth path: openai_stub_login (fresh); `opencode run -m openai/gpt-5.6-luna --format json "say hi"` exits 0 and its output contains STUB-OK; requests.jsonl holds a POST to chatgpt.com /backend-api/codex/responses with authorization "Bearer <that fake access token>", chatgpt-account-id "acct-test" and body.model "gpt-5.6-luna".
  2. an expired access token is refreshed and written back: openai_stub_login <data> expired; the same run exits 0; requests.jsonl holds a POST to auth.openai.com /oauth/token with grant_type refresh_token and refresh_token rt-0; auth.json afterwards has .openai.refresh == "rt-1".
  3. the effort reaches the request: `opencode run -m openai/gpt-5.6-luna --variant high ...` -> the codex request body has .reasoning.effort == "high".
  4. the model list is what the subscription serves: with the fake login, `opencode models openai` lists openai/gpt-5.6-luna and does NOT list openai/gpt-6-luna.

title: OpenAI subscription as a second opencode provider beside OpenRouter
description:
User request 2026-10-01: handle an OpenAI (ChatGPT) subscription in addition to OpenRouter. /tier must tell an OpenAI-direct model from the same OpenAI model on OpenRouter. Claude stays the orchestrator and delegates to OpenAI models when asked; the setup mirrors OpenRouter's.

GROUND TRUTH (measured on this box 2026-10-01, opencode 1.18.25)
- opencode ships ChatGPT sign-in for provider `openai`: methods "ChatGPT Pro/Plus (browser)" (callback on localhost:1455) and "ChatGPT Pro/Plus (headless)" (device code, https://auth.openai.com/codex/device). `opencode auth login --provider openai --method "ChatGPT Pro/Plus (headless)"` skips both pickers.
- Tokens land in ${XDG_DATA_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share}/opencode/auth.json as {"openai":{"type":"oauth","refresh","access","expires"(ms),"accountId"}}. opencode refreshes them itself (POST auth.openai.com/oauth/token) and rewrites every /v1/responses call to https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses with Bearer + ChatGPT-Account-Id.
- Under that login `opencode models openai --verbose` (0.8 s) lists ONLY what the subscription serves, each with .family and .release_date, cost 0. With a fake login: gpt-5.3-codex-spark, gpt-5.4, gpt-5.4-mini, gpt-5.5, gpt-5.6-luna, gpt-5.6-sol, gpt-5.6-terra, gpt-6.1-sol (plus -fast/-flex twins sharing family+date). opencode's own filter drops gpt-6-luna and gpt-6-sol although models.dev lists them.
- Families (models.dev): gpt-luna = efficient, gpt-terra = balanced, gpt-sol = frontier, gpt-astra = most capable, gpt-mini, gpt-nano, gpt (gpt-5.4/5.5).
- Effort on provider openai = provider.openai.models.<id>.options.reasoningEffort (opencode's own openai variants); OpenRouter's reasoning.effort does not apply. `opencode run --variant <e>` also exists.
- opencode (Bun) honours HTTPS_PROXY (measured with a CONNECT logger) -- that is how tests stub OpenAI.

DESIGN
1. The provider is the opencode model prefix in tier.json's model ref: openrouter/... vs openai/.... Both are agent opencode, backend orca. No tier.json schema change; labels read orca:opencode:openai/~gpt-luna-latest@high vs orca:opencode:openrouter/~openai/gpt-luna-latest@high.
2. /tier grammar: `openai:<family|id>` and a bare `openai` (worker default newest GPT Terra, recon default newest GPT Luna). Every existing form keeps its meaning: a bare name, a route or a vendor/model id is still OpenRouter (`openai/gpt-5.6-luna` without the colon stays the OpenRouter model).
3. Family aliases follow releases the way OpenRouter's ~-latest aliases do: openai:luna binds openai/~gpt-luna-latest, resolved AT LAUNCH to the newest id of that family the subscription serves (newest release_date, then the shortest id, so gpt-5.6-luna beats gpt-5.6-luna-fast). openai:gpt-5.6-luna pins one model.
4. Sign-in: /tier auth openai opens an Orca tab running scripts/openai-auth.sh (opencode's headless device login). No guard: OpenAI itself serves the request (US, inside DATA_RESIDENCY.md's allowed set), so there is no provider choice to police; the credential lives in opencode's auth store exactly as opencode's own OpenRouter login already does.
5. One launch-config writer (scripts/lib/opencode-launch.sh) for orca-dispatch (TUI + headless) and recon; an openai launch carries no OpenRouter guard env; dispatch and recon refuse cleanly when OpenAI is not signed in.
6. Out of scope: delegate routes (delegate.sh runs each job under its own HOME, which has no opencode auth store -- documented, not built); the auto-derived default of a plain /tier <top> (unchanged); scripts/container/ and the Mac launcher (no host-side change, so no mac-e2e debt).

SLICES: B1 stub-OpenAI harness || B2 launch path -> B3 /tier grammar + sign-in -> B4 docs.
KNOWN RISK (documented in B4): two opencode processes that find the access token expired at the same instant both spend the same refresh token; OpenAI rotates refresh tokens, so one of them can fail and need a fresh sign-in.
close_reason: All five slices merged (B1 stub harness, B2 launch path, B3 /tier grammar, B4 sign-in, B5 docs); 159/159 across the touched test files on integrated main; real opencode proven against the stub for sign-in, recon and headless dispatch.

title: End to end: real agents stopped at the ceiling write a HANDOFF the relay recognises (detect_handoff reads bold markers and list-style left:)
description:

This bead does 7lz.7's parser work below and carries the end-to-end real-run acceptance, registered before any run: real agents stopped at the ceiling must write a report the relay's detect_handoff accepts.

OBJECTIVE: orca-wait's detect_handoff (scripts/orca-wait.sh) recognises the HANDOFF blocks real models actually write. Both would lose work on the Orca path.

FILES (nothing else): scripts/orca-wait.sh (detect_handoff only), tests/orca-relay-format.bats (new; FROZEN from its RED commit), tests/fixtures/handoff-chain-1.txt and tests/fixtures/handoff-chain-2.txt (new; the two real scout reports, byte for byte from /tmp/claude-501/-workspace-claude-orca/631aeb0f-21f8-4fb1-a5c2-9215526c0e47/scratchpad/handoff-chain-1.txt and /tmp/claude-501/-workspace-claude-orca/631aeb0f-21f8-4fb1-a5c2-9215526c0e47/scratchpad/handoff-chain-2.txt -- copy them, do not retype).

SPEC -- detect_handoff:
- Matching works on a NORMALISED copy of each line: every '*' removed, then leading whitespace, '#' and '>' characters removed, then trailing whitespace removed. The block that gets saved/returned is still the ORIGINAL lines, from the HANDOFF line to the end.
- The HANDOFF line: a line whose normalised form is exactly "HANDOFF" or "HANDOFF:". A longer line that merely contains HANDOFF is still not one.
- The left: line: the first line after the HANDOFF line whose normalised form starts with "left:" (case-insensitive). Its value = the rest, trimmed, lowercased, one trailing "." dropped.
  * value is none / nothing / n/a / - -> NOT a handoff (unchanged).
  * value is empty -> look at the following lines up to the next FIELD line (normalised form starting with done:, left:, facts:, next: or relay:, case-insensitive) or the end: any non-blank line there -> it is a list -> a handoff; all blank -> NOT a handoff.
  * no left: line at all -> a handoff (unchanged).
Keep the function's interface (returns 0 and prints the block, or returns 1) and every current caller unchanged.

TESTS -- tests/orca-relay-format.bats, exercising the real path (a worker_done message through $WAIT --poll-loop, asserting the receipt's .handoff and the HANDOFF-AT note) with the stub harness tests/orca-relay.bats uses (tests/helpers/orca-stub.bash); pin the scripts, never via PATH. 1 "**HANDOFF**" then "**left:** read scripts/recon.sh" -> handoff true; the HANDOFF-AT note carries the original "**HANDOFF**" line.
2 "## HANDOFF" then "left: read scripts/recon.sh" -> handoff true.
3 "HANDOFF:" then "left: read scripts/recon.sh" -> handoff true.
4 "HANDOFF", "left:", "1. read scripts/lib/paths.sh", "2. continue the chain", "next: resume at paths.sh" -> handoff true.
5 "HANDOFF", "left:", "", "next: nothing to do" -> NOT a handoff.
6 "HANDOFF", "**Left:** None." -> NOT a handoff.
7 a body whose only mention is the prose line "we skip the **HANDOFF** step here" -> NOT a handoff.
8 the body is tests/fixtures/handoff-chain-1.txt verbatim -> handoff true.
9 the body is tests/fixtures/handoff-chain-2.txt verbatim -> handoff true.
Assertions are [ ] and functions, never a bare [[ ]].

REAL RUNS (after GREEN; each goes in bd notes as "REAL-RUN <n>: <command>, <report file>, detect_handoff rc, <transcript/log path>"). Save each final report text to $SP2/real-<n>.txt (SP2 = a scratch dir outside the repo). The live opencode plugin must be byte-identical to config/opencode/plugin/context-meter.js (compare; copy it to ~/.config/opencode/plugin/ only if it differs; never touch <project>/.claude-dev/template). Claude runs 1-2, from /workspace/claude-orca, with $SP2/meter-settings.json = {"hooks":{"PostToolUse":[{"matcher":"","hooks":[{"type":"command","command":"/workspace/claude-orca/bin/context-meter --post"}]}],"PreToolUse":[{"matcher":"","hooks":[{"type":"command","command":"/workspace/claude-orca/bin/context-meter --pre"}]}]}}: CLAUDE_ORCA_CONTEXT_BUDGET=1 CLAUDE_ORCA_CONTEXT_CEILING=8 claude -p --dangerously-skip-permissions --settings $SP2/meter-settings.json --output-format json "Use the Agent tool exactly once: subagent_type scout, model haiku, prompt: 'Start with scripts/orca-dispatch.sh: read it and list its functions with line numbers. title: Context meter, revised: the ceiling carries the HANDOFF template, the block is for unfinished work, and 'left: none' never relays
description:

Measured 2026-09-24 in real runs (epic notes): the SOFT NOTICE is advisory -- a haiku scout and luna both finish a small task past it, then usually append a block saying "left: None"; the CEILING is what bounds context, and a refused agent that never saw the block template improvises a report nothing can relay. So: (1) the ceiling text carries the block template and is what the model sees once past the ceiling; (2) the block is asked for only when work remains; (3) a block that says nothing is left never triggers a relay. NEW SHARED TEXTS (the epic is updated to these; copy byte for byte, {pct} {budget} {ceiling} substituted): SOFT NOTICE (7 lines): [context-meter] context is at {pct}% of this agent's window (budget {budget}%); past this point answer quality drops. Stop exploring: finish the step in hand and stop. If work remains, end your final report with this block; if the task is complete, just report. HANDOFF done: left: facts: next: relay: this agent is finished -- start a fresh one from this block; never message or resume it. HARD REFUSAL (7 lines): [context-meter] context is at {pct}% of this agent's window, past the {ceiling}% ceiling: tool calls are refused. Write your final report now and stop. If work remains, end it with this block: followed by the same six lines as the SOFT NOTICE (HANDOFF through relay:). title: opencode context meter, amended: the notice rides in the system prompt (models ignore instructions inside tool output)
description:
OBJECTIVE: supersedes claude-orca-7lz.2 (read its notes: EVIDENCE a-d and REAL-RUN). The opencode context meter must reach the MODEL through a channel it obeys. Measured 2026-09-23 on openai/gpt-5.6-luna: the SOFT NOTICE appended to tool output (tool.execute.after) landed byte-for-byte and was ignored twice -- models treat instructions inside tool results as untrusted data. title: [bug] git refuses /workspace/<name>: the mounted project root reads as uid 0, so 55-git-init fails and commits/Orca worktrees break
description: Observed 2026-09-23 at session start: provision 55-git-init FAILED with 'detected dubious ownership in repository at /workspace/claude-orca'. stat: /workspace/claude-orca 0:0 and /workspace/claude-orca/.claude-dev/home 0:0 through the /workspace mount, yet .git 501:1000 and /home/agent (the same home dir, its own virtiofs mount) 501:1000; agent is uid 501 (HOST_UID=501). No safe.directory anywhere (repo grep, system and global config). Effect: every git call in the folder fails -- commits, worktree-gc, Orca worktrees, orca-dispatch workers. Session workaround: git -c safe.directory='*' per command (no config change). Fix direction: the entrypoint (root, before dropping to agent) or 55-git-init declares PROJECT_DIR and its worktrees safe in the system gitconfig, or finds why the mount root reads as root. Host-side: needs a mac-e2e run.
acceptance_criteria:
DECISION (orchestrator, 2026-10-02): the 2026-10-01 boot did not reproduce it (55-git-init ok, git works), but the mount root's owner still flips (one stat read 0:0, the next 501:1000), so the fix is the documented git remedy, applied where it ships without an image rebuild: provision step 55-git-init marks PROJECT_DIR safe in the agent's GLOBAL git config before its first git call.
FILES: scripts/container/provision.d/55-git-init, tests/provision-git-init.bats only.

title: Claude-side context meter: a PostToolUse/PreToolUse hook enforces the budget in every in-process sub-agent; scout/executor/verifier know the rule
description:
OBJECTIVE: a Claude Code hook meters every in-process sub-agent's context and enforces the epic's SHARED CONTRACT (read it: bd show <parent>): a soft notice from the budget on, refused tool calls from the ceiling on. The main loop (the orchestrator) is never metered. Parent epic holds the exact notice texts -- copy them byte for byte.

FILES (nothing else): scripts/context-meter.sh (new), bin/context-meter (new symlink -> ../scripts/context-meter.sh, like bin/auth-guard), config/claude-settings.json (two hook entries), config/agents/scout.md, config/agents/executor.md, config/agents/verifier.md (one short section each), tests/context-meter.bats (new; FROZEN from its RED commit).

FACTS (verified 2026-09-23, Claude Code 2.1.280):
- Hook stdin for a tool call inside a sub-agent carries agent_id (populated) and agent_type; main-loop payloads have NO agent_id key (python/delegation-gate.py:201-209). transcript_path is the MAIN session transcript for both.
- The sub-agent's own transcript: "${transcript_path%.jsonl}/subagents/agent-${agent_id}.jsonl"; beside it agent-${agent_id}.meta.json, e.g. {"agentType":"executor",...,"model":"sonnet"}.
- Each assistant row of that jsonl has .type=="assistant" and .message.usage {input_tokens, cache_read_input_tokens, cache_creation_input_tokens, output_tokens} and .message.model (e.g. "claude-sonnet-5").
- Context emitter shape used in this repo: python/delegation-gate.py:397-406.

SPEC -- scripts/context-meter.sh, invoked as `context-meter --post` (PostToolUse) or `context-meter --pre` (PreToolUse). Runs only in the container (bash 4, GNU tools, jq fine). ALWAYS exits 0 and prints nothing unless it has something to say; any missing file, bad JSON or odd value = silent exit 0 (fail open).
1. Read stdin. No agent_id (absent or empty) -> exit 0.
2. Settings per the epic. budget 0 -> exit 0.
3. T = the sub-agent transcript above; missing -> exit 0. Take the LAST row with .type=="assistant" and a .message.usage object (read with tail -n 400, not the whole file). context = input_tokens + cache_read_input_tokens + cache_creation_input_tokens + output_tokens (missing fields = 0). No such row -> exit 0.
4. window = CLAUDE_ORCA_CONTEXT_WINDOW when positive; else 1000000 when the meta.json .model OR that row's .message.model contains "[1m]"; else 200000.
5. pct = floor(context*100/window).
6. --post and pct >= budget: print {"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PostToolUse","additionalContext":<SOFT NOTICE>}}.
   --pre and pct >= ceiling: print {"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","permissionDecision":"deny","permissionDecisionReason":<HARD REFUSAL>}}.
   Build JSON with jq -n --arg, never by string concatenation.
Header comment 5-8 lines: what it meters, why (quality drops past ~30%), the two thresholds, the relay (a fresh agent continues from the HANDOFF block).

config/claude-settings.json: add a PostToolUse entry {"matcher": "", "hooks": [{"type":"command","command":"[ -x \"__HOST__/template/bin/context-meter\" ] && exec \"__HOST__/template/bin/context-meter\" --post; exit 0"}]} and a PreToolUse entry with matcher "" and the same command with --pre. Keep every existing entry and its order; append the new entries at the end of each event's array.

Agent definitions: add a section "## Context budget" to config/agents/scout.md, executor.md and verifier.md, this text exactly:
Your answers get measurably worse once your context passes about 30% of your window. Keep it lean: search narrowly, read the lines you need rather than whole files, and never re-read what you already have. A `[context-meter]` notice is an order, not advice: finish the step in hand and end your report with the HANDOFF block it gives -- a fresh agent continues from it.
Place it after the first section of each file's body. Run the doc suites listed in CHECK -- some cap words or assert headings; if one fails because of this section, report it instead of editing that test.

TESTS -- tests/context-meter.bats. Each case runs the pinned script: env -i PATH="$PATH" HOME="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/h" [CLAUDE_ORCA_CONTEXT_*=...] bash "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../scripts/context-meter.sh" --post|--pre <<<"$payload", never via PATH. A helper writes a fixture session: $S/sess.jsonl (main transcript, any content) and $S/sess/subagents/agent-a1.jsonl with assistant rows carrying a usage object, plus agent-a1.meta.json. payload = {"tool_name":"Bash","agent_id":"a1","agent_type":"scout","transcript_path":"$S/sess.jsonl"}.
