title: opencode context meter: a plugin enforces the same budget in headless workers and recon
description:
OBJECTIVE: headless opencode runs (orca-worker-run workers and recon) get the same context meter as Claude sub-agents: an opencode plugin enforcing the epic's SHARED CONTRACT (bd show <parent>; copy the notice texts byte for byte). The current tier binds BOTH worker and recon to opencode, so this is the half the user feels first.

FILES (nothing else): config/opencode/<plugin dir>/context-meter.js (new), scripts/config-sync.sh (install it), tests/opencode-context-meter.bats (new; FROZEN from its RED commit).

FACTS (recon 2026-09-23): opencode 1.18.25 (/usr/local/lib/node_modules/opencode-ai); @opencode-ai/plugin and @opencode-ai/sdk 1.18.25 under ~/.config/opencode/node_modules. Plugin hooks: event (plugin/dist/index.d.ts:173-177), "tool.execute.before", "tool.execute.after" (:249-258). PluginInput.client is the SDK client (:36-46): client.session.abort (sdk/dist/gen/sdk.gen.d.ts:148-150), client.config.providers(). Message tokens {total?, input, output, reasoning, cache:{read, write}} (types.gen.d.ts:98-133). Headless runs: scripts/orca-worker-run.sh:114-120 and scripts/recon.sh:212-214 (recon sets OPENCODE_CONFIG to its own file). config/opencode/ holds only opencode.json today; config-sync copies it at scripts/config-sync.sh:209-220 (manifest :20-31). Cached windows: z-ai/glm-5.3-flash 1310720, openai/gpt-5.6-luna 1050000 (~/.cache/opencode/models.json). node v22 is on PATH.

VERIFY FIRST, record each answer in bd notes as "EVIDENCE: ...", stop and report if one contradicts this spec:
a. Which directory opencode 1.18.25 loads GLOBAL plugins from (plugin/ or plugins/ under ~/.config/opencode) -- find the glob in its bundled source. That directory name is <plugin dir> above, in config/ and in the synced home.
b. Whether it still loads them when OPENCODE_CONFIG points at another file (recon's case).
c. The StepFinishPart type: a part with type "step-finish" and a tokens object, delivered through event {type:"message.part.updated", properties:{part}} with part.sessionID. Each step-finish is ONE model call's usage -- that is the meter's reading.
d. The exact shapes of tool.execute.after's output ({title, output, metadata}?), of client.config.providers()'s response, and of client.session.abort's argument.

SPEC -- context-meter.js, plain ESM JavaScript, no imports (it must load with no node_modules). Exports exactly ONE binding, `export const ContextMeter = async ({ client }) => ({ ... })` -- opencode calls every export as a plugin, so no helper may be exported.
- Settings per the epic, read from process.env when the plugin is created.
- Per sessionID state: context tokens, providerID/modelID, consecutive refusals.
- event: message.updated with info.role === "assistant" -> remember info.providerID/info.modelID for info.sessionID. message.part.updated with part.type === "step-finish" -> context = part.tokens.total when > 0, else input + output + reasoning + cache.read + cache.write (missing = 0); ignore a zero reading.
- window = CLAUDE_ORCA_CONTEXT_WINDOW when positive; else limit.context of that provider/model from client.config.providers() (looked up once per model, cached; any error = unknown); unknown -> 200000.
- "tool.execute.after"(input, output): pct >= budget -> output.output += "\n\n" + SOFT NOTICE. Any error inside -> leave output untouched.
- "tool.execute.before"(input, output): pct >= ceiling -> count a refusal; on the 3rd consecutive refusal in that session call client.session.abort for it (once, errors swallowed); then throw new Error(HARD REFUSAL). Below the ceiling -> reset the count, do nothing.
- budget 0 -> every hook is a no-op.
Header comment 5-8 lines, mirroring scripts/context-meter.sh's purpose (the Claude-side twin another slice writes).

config-sync.sh: install the plugin to ~/.config/opencode/<plugin dir>/context-meter.js the same way opencode.json is installed (manifest entry + copy), so a checksum change re-syncs it. Nothing else in config-sync changes.

title: Orca relay + reaper: a HANDOFF re-dispatches from bead notes; stalled and closed-bead workers are released and their terminals closed
description:
OBJECTIVE: the Orca side of the relay and of idle-agent shutdown. (1) A worker whose worker_done report carries a HANDOFF block (epic SHARED CONTRACT, bd show <parent>) is released like any finished worker, its block is saved to the bead's notes, and the next orca-dispatch of that bead starts a fresh worker from it. (2) No finished or stalled worker stays resident: the stall scan releases workers it gives up on and closes their terminals.

FILES (nothing else): scripts/orca-wait.sh, scripts/lib/orca-orch.sh, tests/orca-relay.bats (new; FROZEN from its RED commit).

FACTS (read 2026-09-23):
- process_batch (orca-wait.sh:418-527): on worker_done it notes the bead (orch_note_bead, :463-465, "$subject: $body"), releases (:474-505: worker-release; a non-terminal state closes the TUI terminal, a headless one is skipped because "its terminal ended with the run"), rec_mark_done (:507-509), then emit_receipt (:513-524).
- stall_scan (:323-413): a closed bead only marks the record done (:346-358) -- the worker is never released; the second stall (:361-381) emits the in-process fallback and marks the record "stalled" but leaves the worker running, so the fallback executor and the stalled worker share one worktree; the first stall nudges (:383-410). --keep sets KEEP=1 (skip release).
- orch_spec (lib/orca-orch.sh ~270-300) builds the dispatch spec from bd show JSON: title, description, acceptance contract, WORKER RULES. It never reads .notes.

SPEC
1. release_worker <disp_id> <term> <mode> <reap>: move the release block at :474-505 into one function (sets released / terminal_closed as today). reap=0 is today's behaviour exactly. reap=1 (a worker that has NOT finished): after worker-release, close the terminal whenever release did not say released|closed|gone and a terminal id is known -- headless included, because a stalled headless run is still running. KEEP=1 skips it all, as today, with note "kept <disp> (--keep)".
2. Relay: in the worker_done branch, when $body has a line that is exactly HANDOFF (surrounding whitespace allowed), the block (that line to the end of $body) is appended to the bead's notes via orch_note_bead as "HANDOFF-AT <UTC, date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ> dispatch=<disp_id>" followed by the block on the next lines. The record gets .handoff = true (rec_mark_done still sets state done). The receipt gains handoff: true and relay_with: "orca-dispatch <bead>"; every other worker_done receipt gains handoff: false. Stderr note: "[relay] <bead> handed off at its context budget -- orca-dispatch <bead> starts a fresh worker from the HANDOFF in its notes". "HANDOFF" inside a longer line is not a handoff.
3. orch_spec: when the bead JSON's .notes contain a line starting "HANDOFF-AT ", insert before WORKER RULES:
CONTINUE FROM HANDOFF
A previous worker on this bead stopped at its context budget. Continue from its handoff below; do not redo what it lists as done.
<the LAST handoff: the lines after the last "HANDOFF-AT " line, through the first following line that starts with "relay:" -- or, with no such line, up to the next line starting with "ORCA " or the end of the notes>
Without a HANDOFF-AT line the spec is byte-identical to today's.
4. Reaper in stall_scan: the closed-bead branch calls release_worker with reap=1 before marking the record done; the second-stall branch calls release_worker with reap=1 BEFORE emitting the fallback receipt (the in-process executor must not share the worktree with a live worker). Both set .reaped = true and .terminal_closed on the record and print note "[reap] <disp> (<bead>): <closed bead|stalled twice> -- worker released<, terminal closed>". The first stall is unchanged (nudge only).

TESTS -- tests/orca-relay.bats. Reuse the stub harness of tests/orca-wait.bats / tests/orca-wait-retained.bats (stub orca that logs its argv and answers worker-release with a configurable state; stub bd; dispatch records under the run dir). Run the pinned scripts, never via PATH. Cases, in this order:
1 worker_done whose body ends with a HANDOFF block -> the bead note appended carries "HANDOFF-AT " and the block's "next:" line; receipt .handoff == true and .relay_with == "orca-dispatch <bead>"; record .handoff == true and .state == "done"; worker-release was called.
2 worker_done without HANDOFF -> receipt .handoff == false, no .relay_with, no HANDOFF-AT note.
3 body line "no HANDOFF needed here" -> not a handoff.
4 orch_spec, notes holding two HANDOFF-AT entries (with ORCA lines between) -> "CONTINUE FROM HANDOFF" appears once, carries the second block's next: line and not the first's, and sits before "WORKER RULES".
5 orch_spec without HANDOFF-AT -> output identical to the same bead without notes.
6 stall scan, bead closed, release answers "retained" -> worker-release called for that dispatch, terminal close called, record .reaped == true and .state == "done".
7 first stall -> no worker-release, no terminal close.
8 second stall of a headless record, release answers "retained" -> worker-release and terminal close both called BEFORE the stalled receipt is emitted; the receipt still carries .fallback; record .reaped == true.
9 --keep, second stall -> no worker-release, no terminal close.
Assertions are [ ] and functions, never a bare [[ ]].

WORKER RULES:
- git is refused in this folder today (dubious ownership). Run EVERY git command as git -c safe.directory='*' ... ; never change git config.
- Two other executors are editing this same working tree right now (they own scripts/context-meter.sh, bin/context-meter, config/claude-settings.json, config/agents/*.md, config/opencode/, scripts/config-sync.sh and their own new tests). Stage only your files; commit with an explicit pathspec: git -c safe.directory='*' commit -m "..." -- <your paths>. Never git stash/reset/checkout/restore/clean/add -A. index.lock busy -> wait 2 s, retry. A neighbour failure in a file another slice owns is not yours: note it.
- Before RED, run the CHECK's neighbour suites once and record failures as "BASELINE: <file> <case>" via bd update <bead> --append-notes.
- Commit tests/orca-relay.bats ALONE first (RED), record "RED-AT <sha>"; then the rest (GREEN), record "GREEN-AT <sha>". Never edit the test after RED; a fixture bug found after RED = stop and report.
- Write/Edit in <=150-line pieces, one file per response. Report under 60 lines.

All other 38 tests pass.

title: Context budget: agents hand off at ~30% of their window; finished or stalled agents are shut down
description:
OBJECTIVE: every delegated agent -- in-process Claude sub-agents (scout, executor, verifier) and headless opencode workers/recon -- stops at a context budget and hands its work to a fresh agent, and the orchestrator shuts down agents that are finished or stalled instead of leaving them resident. User's premise (2026-09-23): answer quality drops substantially past ~30% of the context window; sub-agents, scouts especially, keep working far past it.

SHARED CONTRACT (slices .1 and .2 implement it identically; .3 parses it):

Settings, read from the environment at hook/plugin time. A value that is not a non-negative integer falls back to its default.
- CLAUDE_ORCA_CONTEXT_BUDGET   percent, default 30; 0 turns the meter off entirely.
- CLAUDE_ORCA_CONTEXT_CEILING  percent, default 40.
- CLAUDE_ORCA_CONTEXT_WINDOW   tokens; a positive value overrides the window lookup.

pct = floor(context_tokens * 100 / window), where context_tokens is the size of the agent's MOST RECENT model call (not a running sum).

SOFT NOTICE, when pct >= budget -- appended to every tool result the agent sees from then on. Exact text ({pct} and {budget} substituted, 7 lines):
[context-meter] context is at {pct}% of this agent's window (budget {budget}%); past this point answer quality drops. Stop exploring: finish the step in hand and stop. If work remains, end your final report with this block; if the task is complete, just report.
HANDOFF
done: <what is finished, with file:line>
left: <what remains, in order>
facts: <file:line facts the next agent must not re-derive>
next: <the exact prompt a fresh agent should start from>
relay: this agent is finished -- start a fresh one from this block; never message or resume it.

HARD REFUSAL, when pct >= ceiling -- every tool call is refused with it, and it replaces the SOFT NOTICE wherever that would appear. Exact text ({pct} and {ceiling} substituted, 7 lines): this line, then the same six lines as the SOFT NOTICE (HANDOFF through relay:):
[context-meter] context is at {pct}% of this agent's window, past the {ceiling}% ceiling: tool calls are refused. Write your final report now and stop. If work remains, end it with this block:

HANDOFF detection (the relay side): a report hands off when it contains a line that is exactly HANDOFF (surrounding whitespace allowed) and the block's left: value is not empty/none/nothing/n/a/- (a missing left: line still counts as a handoff); the block is that line through the end of the report.

REVISED 2026-09-24 (claude-orca-7lz.6): the texts above replaced the first versions after real runs showed the soft notice is advisory on small tasks and a refused agent without the template improvises; the ceiling is the enforcement. Delivery: Claude sub-agents via PostToolUse additionalContext / PreToolUse deny; opencode via the system prompt (experimental.chat.system.transform) and a thrown tool error -- never tool output, which models ignore.

SLICES: .1 Claude-side meter hook + agent definitions; .2 opencode plugin meter; .3 orca relay (handoff -> bead notes -> re-dispatch) and reaper (stalled / closed-bead workers are released and their terminals closed). In-process idle agents: measured after the slices land (ListAgents), acted on only if finished agents are shown resident.
notes:
IN-PROCESS IDLE MEASURED 2026-09-23: ListAgents shows a finished Agent-tool executor as 'completed' (not running); ps shows no process for it (in-process), and the three recon runs from this session left no opencode process. Finished in-process agents are not resident -- no reaper needed there; the hard ceiling is what stops a spent one.
REAL RUNS 2026-09-24 (headless claude -p, repo hook wired via --settings, haiku scout, 5-file listing task): (1) BUDGET=1 CEILING=95: the soft notice reached the scout on every tool result; it still read all five files (small, well-scoped task) and ended its report with a correct HANDOFF block (left: none) -- the block format is followed, 'stop exploring' is weak on a small task. (2) BUDGET=1 CEILING=3: the scout started at 5% (a fresh scout's own prompt+tools is ~11k tokens), so all five Reads were refused ('PreToolUse:Read hook error: [context-meter] ... past the 3% ceiling'); main loop untouched; but its report had NO HANDOFF block -- it never saw the soft notice's template, and the HARD REFUSAL only names the fields. Sessions fb3bcd5b (soft), 3d4aa6d1 (hard).
close_reason: Shipped: Claude sub-agents metered by context-meter (PostToolUse notice from 30%, PreToolUse refusal from 40%); opencode workers/recon by config/opencode/plugin/context-meter.js (system-prompt notice, thrown refusal); both texts carry the HANDOFF template; orca-wait relays a HANDOFF to bead notes and orch_spec continues from it; stalled/closed-bead workers are released and their terminals closed. Verified by 4 fresh real runs (7lz.9). In-process finished agents measured not resident.

title: 15-claude-on-path installs the latest Claude Code natively into the folder's home (download + sha256), no image copy
description:
OBJECTIVE: the folder's home holds the ONLY Claude Code: Claude Code's own native-install layout (~/.local/bin/claude -> ~/.local/share/claude/versions/<v>), which `claude update` manages. At every container start provision step 15 brings it to the latest release -- downloaded and sha256-verified, never copied from an image (slice .2 removes the image's copy). Parent: claude-orca-dbf.

FILES: scripts/container/provision.d/15-claude-on-path (rewrite), tests/provision-claude-on-path.bats (rewrite; FROZEN from its RED commit). Nothing else. Read the current versions of both first: the native-link detection (home_v), the plain-file refusal and the test helpers carry over.

SPEC -- the step (runs only inside the container: bash 4+ is fine, GNU tools are fine):
Variables: RELEASES="${CLAUDE_ORCA_CLAUDE_RELEASES:-https://downloads.claude.ai/claude-code-releases}" (tests point it at a file:// fixture dir; curl reads file:// URLs); AGENT_HOME="${HOME:-/home/agent}"; HOME_BIN="$AGENT_HOME/.local/bin/claude"; VDIR="$AGENT_HOME/.local/share/claude/versions". The step must NOT contain the strings /opt/claude or CLAUDE_ORCA_CLAUDE_DIR anywhere, comments included (say "the image's copy" in prose).
1. HOME_BIN exists and is not a symlink: stderr "<HOME_BIN> is a file, not Claude Code's native-install link; leaving it alone", exit 1, no network call.
2. home_v = semver of basename(readlink -f HOME_BIN) ONLY when HOME_BIN is a symlink whose readlink -f lies inside readlink -f VDIR and is executable; else empty (missing, broken, or a non-native target such as the image's old binary).
3. latest = curl -fsSL --max-time 10 "$RELEASES/latest", whitespace stripped, must match ^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$. Unreachable or not semver: home_v set -> stdout "cannot reach $RELEASES/latest; keeping claude $home_v", exit 0; home_v empty -> stderr "no Claude Code in $HOME_BIN and cannot reach $RELEASES/latest", exit 1.
4. home_v set and sort -V ranks home_v >= latest -> stdout "claude $home_v is current (latest $latest)", exit 0, nothing downloaded.
5. Else install latest: platform = linux-<arch> from uname -m (aarch64|arm64 -> arm64, x86_64|amd64 -> x64, anything else -> stderr + exit 1). manifest = curl -fsSL "$RELEASES/$latest/manifest.json"; checksum = jq -r ".platforms[\"$platform\"].checksum // empty", must match ^[a-f0-9]{64}$ else stderr + exit 1. mkdir -p VDIR and dirname(HOME_BIN). Download "$RELEASES/$latest/$platform/claude" to "$VDIR/.$latest.claude-orca.tmp"; verify (echo "$checksum  $tmp" | sha256sum -c - >/dev/null); chmod 755; mv -f to "$VDIR/$latest"; ln -sfn "$VDIR/$latest" "$HOME_BIN". Any failure: rm -f the tmp, HOME_BIN untouched, one stderr line, exit 1. Success: stdout "claude: $HOME_BIN -> $VDIR/$latest (was ${home_v:-no native install})", exit 0.
Header comment, rewritten: the image carries no Claude Code; this step is the template's install and update of Claude Code's own native install in the folder's home, the same layout `claude update` writes, so an update in a session moves the same link and the next start never downgrades it. Keep the measured history short (2026-09-22, real binaries: an old home copy shadowed every rebuild; zsh hashed the image's copy so `cs` ran it after `claude update`; a link at the image's binary is one `claude update` refuses to move). The comment must not contain a tilde-slash-dot-claude literal followed by anything but '-' (tests/config-sync.bats grep gate: ~/\.claude([^-]|$) and \$HOME/\.claude([^-]|$)); ~/.local/... is fine.

TESTS -- tests/provision-claude-on-path.bats, no network: every case runs the step as env -i PATH="$PATH" HOME="$H" PROJECT_DIR="$PROJ" CLAUDE_ORCA_CLAUDE_RELEASES="file://$R" bash "$STEP" (R = a fixture releases dir under BATS_TEST_TMPDIR). Helpers: ARCH computed like the step (aarch64|arm64 -> arm64, x86_64|amd64 -> x64); release <v> writes $R/<v>/linux-$ARCH/claude (a +x sh script: echo "<v> (Claude Code)") and $R/<v>/manifest.json = {"platforms":{"linux-$ARCH":{"checksum":"<sha256sum of that file>"}}}; latest <v> writes $R/latest; home_claude <v> as today (a script in $V/<v>, link to it). Twelve cases, in this order:
 1 no home install -> link = $V/<latest>, cmp -s with $R/<latest>/linux-$ARCH/claude, "$HOME_BIN" --version prints "<latest> (Claude Code)".
 2 older native 2.1.99, latest 2.1.280 -> link = $V/2.1.280; $V/2.1.99 still exists.
 3 numeric order: home 2.1.100, latest 2.1.99 (write only $R/latest, no release dir) -> exit 0, link unchanged.
 4 equal (home 2.1.280, latest 2.1.280, no release dir) -> exit 0, link unchanged, output contains "is current".
 5 non-native link (to an executable file outside $V, e.g. $BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/image/claude) -> replaced: link = $V/<latest>.
 6 broken link -> link = $V/<latest>.
 7 checksum mismatch (manifest checksum = sha256 of different bytes), home 2.1.99 -> exit 1, link still $V/2.1.99, no $V/2.1.280, no $V/.*tmp file left.
 8 unreachable (RELEASES=file:///nonexistent-dir), home 2.1.99 -> exit 0, link unchanged, output contains "keeping claude 2.1.99".
 9 unreachable, no home install -> exit 1, $HOME_BIN absent (neither -e nor -L).
 10 latest is not semver ("<html>"), home 2.1.99 -> exit 0, link unchanged.
 11 plain file at $HOME_BIN -> exit 1, still not a symlink, output mentions "is a file".
 12 second run is a no-op: install via run 1, touch -d 2020-01-01 $V/<latest>, run again -> exit 0 and mtime unchanged.

title: One Claude Code per folder: the home's native install, updated by the template and by claude update; none in the image
description: User (2026-09-22): 'Why do we need 2 binaries? I'd like to have Claude Code pulling in the template, but I'd also like the option to update claude code in session and just have it update whatever we installed initially. 1 binary, just like if we'd installed it locally.' Measured with real binaries: two copies (image /opt/claude/claude on /usr/local/bin, and the home's native ~/.local/bin/claude) gave three stale-copy cases -- an old home install shadowing each rebuild; zsh hashing /usr/local/bin/claude so cs ran the old copy after a claude update in the same shell; a link at the image binary that claude update refuses to move (7d3033b fixed that one by seeding from the image). Design: the image carries no Claude Code; provision step 15 installs/updates the latest release natively into the folder's home at every start; claude update in session moves the same link. title: recon routing text: rulebook, knowledge base, delegation-gate nudge and exemption, tier banner, scout.md, recon-fanout
description:
OBJECTIVE: the rulebook still says recon stays in-process, so the orchestrator never sends a recon question to the recon backend /tier bound (claude-orca-424). Every place that tells the orchestrator how recon is routed now says: recon follows its backend -- `recon "<question>"` (a Bash call; the sibling bead ships the command) when the recon role's backend is orca, a `scout` spawn otherwise. Parent: claude-orca-424. Text only, no behaviour change beyond one exempt-command addition.

FILES: config/claude-user-memory.md, knowledge-base/TIERED_ORCHESTRATION.md, python/delegation-gate.py, scripts/tier-prime.sh, config/agents/scout.md, config/workflows/recon-fanout.js, tests/recon-routing-docs.bats (new), and -- only if an existing assertion on the changed text forces it -- tests/delegation-gate.bats, tests/tier-hooks.bats, tests/prime-hook.bats. Nothing else.

SPEC
1. config/claude-user-memory.md line 41 currently reads: `Executor slices go through \`orca-dispatch <bead>\` when Orca is reachable and the Agent tool otherwise (explicit \`model\`); checkers and recon stay in-process. \`orca-wait\` ingests \`worker_done\`; \`orca-reply\` answers. Workers are headless runs that exit; a resident TUI is never left behind.` It becomes, verbatim:
   `Executor slices go through \`orca-dispatch <bead>\` when Orca is reachable, the Agent tool (explicit \`model\`) otherwise; recon goes through \`recon "<question>"\` when its backend is orca, a \`scout\` spawn otherwise; checkers stay in-process. \`orca-wait\` ingests \`worker_done\`; \`orca-reply\` answers. Workers are headless runs that exit, never a resident TUI.`
   The file is capped at 1300 words by tests/rulebook.bats (it is at 1293 now; the change above nets about +6). If wc -w is still above 1300 after this, apply exactly this second cut and no other: the Delegation sentence `Spawns are unnamed: the result comes back in the task notification, and the agent id in the spawn result is enough to continue one.` becomes `Spawns are unnamed: the result comes back in the task notification; the spawn result's agent id continues one.` Do not reword anything else.
2. knowledge-base/TIERED_ORCHESTRATION.md: (a) the Defaults paragraph around lines 115-125 ("**Recon = `subagent` haiku** ... both in-process on purpose — recon is cheap and read-only") -- keep the default statement, then add two or three sentences: an orca-backed recon (the hybrid presets' `luna@high`, or `/tier recon openrouter:<model>`) is asked with `recon "<question>"` -- a headless, read-only `opencode run` on the recon model in the project's working tree, no bead, no worktree, answer on stdout, cost in the delegate ledger; tier-gate denies a model-less `scout` spawn there with that command as the reason, and an explicit `model` on the spawn is the in-process fallback. (b) the bullet around line 209 `**Recon fans out freely** — several \`scout\` spawns in one message, no worktree, no Run.` becomes `**Recon fans out freely** — several \`scout\` spawns in one message (subagent backend) or several \`recon "<question>"\` calls with run_in_background (orca backend); no worktree, no Run either way.` (c) the Fallback section (around line 218) gets one sentence after the orca-dispatch exit-3 paragraph: `recon` does the same -- exit 3 with "spawn a scout" when the recon role is not orca+opencode or the guard token is missing.
3. python/delegation-gate.py: (a) the nudge string around line 556: `recon to a scout, edits and builds to an executor slice` becomes `recon to the recon backend (\`recon "<question>"\` when it is orca-backed, a scout otherwise), edits and builds to an executor slice`; (b) the string around line 569 `batch the remaining reads into a scout and work from its summary` becomes `batch the remaining reads into one recon call (\`recon "<question>"\`, or a scout) and work from its summary`; (c) `recon` joins the exempt-command alternation at line 181 (a Bash call that starts with `recon ` IS delegation and never counts), and the exempt list in the nudge text gains it: "`bd`, `git`, `gh`, `bats`, `lane`, `tier-` and `recon` calls never count"; update the comment at lines 137 and 543 that enumerate the exempt list.
4. scripts/tier-prime.sh line 111: `— an orca-backed role is dispatched with orca-dispatch, a subagent-backed one with the Agent tool` becomes `— an orca-backed worker is dispatched with orca-dispatch, orca-backed recon is asked with recon "<question>", a subagent-backed role runs through the Agent tool`.
5. config/agents/scout.md description (frontmatter, keep the YAML valid and the `model: haiku` line): after "Haiku by default — a fraction of the reasoning tier's cost)." add the sentence: `This is the in-process form; when /tier binds recon to an orca backend, ask with recon "<question>" in Bash instead — tier-gate denies a model-less scout spawn there and says so.`
6. config/workflows/recon-fanout.js: the header comment gains two lines saying this is the in-process (Claude haiku) fan-out and that under an orca-backed recon role the orchestrator runs one `recon "<question>"` Bash call per question instead; meta.description becomes `Fan out independent recon questions to one in-process scout-grade agent() call per question (subagent recon backend; under an orca-backed recon role use recon "<question>" per question instead), each returning typed findings anchored to file:line.` Keep `meta` a pure literal.

title: recon: bead-less, read-only headless opencode run on the tier's recon backend -- answer on stdout, cost in the ledger
description:
OBJECTIVE: a recon question has no bead, so nothing today can send it to the tier's recon backend -- every scout of the past week ran on in-process Haiku while tier.json said orca:opencode:gpt-5.6-luna@high (claude-orca-424). Add `recon`, a bead-less, synchronous, read-only headless opencode run on the recon role bound in tier.json: the question goes in on the command line, the answer comes out on stdout, the cost lands in cost-mirror's delegate ledger. Parent: claude-orca-424.

FILES: scripts/recon.sh (new), bin/recon (new relative symlink ../scripts/recon.sh, like the other 43 in bin/), tests/recon.bats (new). Nothing else. Do NOT modify scripts/lib/orca-orch.sh, scripts/orca-worker-run.sh or scripts/delegate.sh -- read them, mirror them.

SPEC -- scripts/recon.sh, bash 3.2 clean (scripts/lint-bash32.sh scans all of scripts/; no mapfile, no associative arrays, no ${x^^}, no += onto an empty array under set -u). Copy the _resolve_script_path / SCRIPT_DIR / `. lib/paths.sh` / `. lib/tier-roles.sh` preamble from scripts/tier-gate.sh.

Usage (also `recon --help`, exit 0):
  recon [--timeout <s>] [--dir <path>] <question ...>
  recon [--timeout <s>] [--dir <path>] --prompt-file <file>
No question and no --prompt-file: usage on stderr, exit 64.

1. State: RECON_STATE_FILE (tests) else tier_state_file (lib/tier-roles.sh). Read the recon role with tier_role_field <file> recon backend|agent|model|variant. When the file is absent, or backend != orca, or agent != opencode: print ONE stderr line
     recon: recon backend is <backend> (<agent> <model>[@<variant>]) -- spawn a scout (Agent tool, subagent_type "scout") for this question
   (with 'unbound' for a missing file) and exit 3. This is the same exit-3 knowing fallback orca-dispatch uses.
2. Run dir: RECON_RUN_DIR (tests) else run_dir (lib/paths.sh). Guard token = the content of <run_dir>/openrouter-guard.token. Missing or empty: stderr `recon: no OpenRouter guard token at <path> -- the guard is down; spawn a scout`, exit 3.
3. Launch config: write <run_dir>/opencode-launch/recon-<slug>.json (mkdir -p; umask 077; chmod 600; slug = model with / and : replaced by -, plus -<variant> when set), the SAME shape orca_opencode_command writes in scripts/lib/orca-orch.sh lines 389-406, with these differences: permission is {"*":"allow","edit":"deny","write":"deny","bash":{"*":"allow","git push":"deny","git push *":"deny"},"external_directory":{"*":"allow"}}; provider.openrouter.options is always {"apiKey":"{env:OPENROUTER_API_KEY}","baseURL":"http://127.0.0.1:<CLAUDE_ORCA_GUARD_PORT or 4141>/api/v1"}; provider.openrouter.models.<model minus the openrouter/ prefix>.options.reasoning.effort = variant when variant is non-empty, no models key otherwise. NEVER write or touch <run_dir>/openrouter-guard.env: dispatched workers source that file when their terminal starts, and rewriting it would hand them this read-only config.
4. Prompt = this preamble, a blank line, then the question verbatim:
     You are doing read-only recon for an orchestrator that will act on your findings without re-reading the files itself. Answer with concrete file:line references for every claim; state negative results explicitly ("X appears nowhere under src/"); compact bullets, verbatim snippets only when the exact text is load-bearing; answer the question asked, at the size asked, then stop. Your permissions deny edits.
5. Run, in the foreground: with OPENROUTER_API_KEY=<token> and OPENCODE_CONFIG=<cfg> exported for this one process (the token never on a command line), `opencode run -m <model> --dir <dir> --auto --format json "<prompt>"` with <dir> = --dir else project_dir (lib/paths.sh) -- the working tree, uncommitted changes included, no worktree. stdout+stderr of opencode go to the log <run_dir>/recon/<UTC timestamp>-<slug>.log (mkdir -p; chmod 600). Timeout: --timeout else CLAUDE_ORCA_RECON_TIMEOUT_S else 600 seconds; on expiry kill the run, print `recon: timed out after <s>s (log <path>)` on stderr, exit 124. Implement the timeout with a background process + kill, as orca-worker-run.sh does for its watchdog; do not rely on coreutils `timeout` (absent on macOS).
6. Output: stdout = the .part.text of every `type=="text"` line of the log, in order, joined by "\n" (jq -r 'select(.type=="text") | .part.text'). stderr = one summary line: `recon: <model>[@<variant>] · <wall>s · in <I> out <O> reasoning <R> · $<usd> · log <path>` where I/O/R are the sums of .part.tokens.input/.output/.reasoning over `type=="step_finish"` lines and usd is the sum of .part.cost (null when no step_finish carried a cost; print $0 then). Exit with opencode's own exit code.
7. Receipt: <run_dir>/recon/<same stem>.receipt.json, chmod 600, the delegate.sh receipt shape (lines 536-558): {job:"recon-<epoch>-<6 hex>", route:"recon", model, bead:null, branch:null, tokens_in, tokens_out, wall_seconds, usd, exit_code, started_at, finished_at, variant (null when empty)}. Then the SAME fail-open hand-off delegate.sh does at lines 568-574 (cost-mirror.sh --ingest-delegate-receipt when python/cost-mirror.py contains that string). The token must appear in no log and no receipt.
8. Header comment: what it is, why it exists (the paragraph above, short), the exit codes (0/opencode's, 3 fallback, 64 usage, 124 timeout), and the env knobs (RECON_STATE_FILE, RECON_RUN_DIR, CLAUDE_ORCA_RECON_TIMEOUT_S, CLAUDE_ORCA_GUARD_PORT).

and exits ${STUB_EXIT:-0} after sleeping ${STUB_SLEEP:-0}. Run the script by its path ($BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../scripts/recon.sh), unset ambient PROJECT_DIR, CLAUDE_ORCA_ROOT, BEADS_DIR first, set PROJECT_DIR to the fixture. Exactly these 10 cases, in this order:

title: Recon tier never reaches its OpenRouter model: scouts under the hybrid presets all run on in-process Haiku
description:
DIAGNOSIS (2026-09-21, from transcripts and dispatch records of the prior 8 days).

Under the hybrid presets tier.json binds recon = orca:opencode:openrouter/openai/gpt-5.6-luna@high, but nothing routes recon work there:
- Rulebook, config/claude-user-memory.md:41: 'checkers and recon stay in-process' -> every recon question is an Agent-tool scout spawn.
- scripts/tier-gate.sh:186-199: for an orca-backed recon role with a non-Claude agent the hook only prints a once-per-session note and exits 0; the spawn proceeds on config/agents/scout.md's frontmatter model (haiku). The note's own wording ('runs on the orchestrator's own model') is wrong -- it is Haiku.
- The Agent tool accepts Claude aliases only, so an in-process scout can never be luna.
- orca-dispatch requires a bead (scripts/orca-dispatch.sh:99), so it is no path for a recon question. The bead-less path that does exist -- 'delegate run --route luna-high --prompt <text>' (scout-grade routes are prompt-only) -- is named by no rule, hook or nudge; delegation-gate's nudge says 'recon to a scout'.
- config/workflows/recon-fanout.js hard-codes model: 'haiku'.

MEASURED: 41 scout spawns, 41 on claude-haiku-4-5 (31 transcript files, 0 on any OpenRouter model); 178 orca-dispatch calls, 4 with --recon; 5 'delegate run' calls on luna/luna-high; dispatch records: 39 glm-5.3-flash, 1 luna. That matches the OpenRouter dashboard (1200 glm-flash calls vs 1 luna): the recon category is not narrow, it is routed to Anthropic Haiku.

DIRECTION is a pending decision in chat: (a) make recon follow its backend -- tier-gate refuses the in-process scout when the recon role is orca/non-Claude and returns the exact delegate command, rulebook line and delegation-gate nudge and recon-fanout follow; or (b) keep recon in-process on Haiku and take luna out of the presets so the banner stops advertising a model that is never called. Either way the change touches the rulebook and hook wiring -> deep lane, contract first.
close_reason: Fixed by 424.1 (recon command), 424.2 (tier-gate deny), 424.3 (rulebook/nudges/banner), 424.4 (test ledger fixture). Live proof 2026-09-22: a model-less scout spawn is denied by the hook with the recon command as the reason; two real recon runs answered from gpt-5.6-luna@high with reasoning tokens (104, 87), $0.005 each, receipts in the cost ledger. Recon under the hybrid presets now reaches luna.

title: container: own, seed and migrate onto the scratch volumes the launcher mounts (CLAUDE_ORCA_VOLUME_DIRS)
description:
OBJECTIVE: the launcher (separate bead) now mounts four docker volumes under the agent home -- /home/agent/.cache, /home/agent/.npm, /home/agent/.local/share/opencode, /home/agent/worktrees -- and names them in the env var CLAUDE_ORCA_VOLUME_DIRS (colon-separated guest paths). Reason, measured in claude-orca-19o: file-creating work on the macOS share costs 15x the wall time and 185x the VM interrupts of a docker volume. This slice is the CONTAINER half: own those dirs, point Orca's worker worktrees at the volume, and migrate what the old bind-mounted copies hold. /home/agent is the SAME host directory as $PROJECT_DIR/.claude-dev/home (mounted twice), so once a volume sits on /home/agent/.cache the OLD content is still reachable -- and only reachable -- at $PROJECT_DIR/.claude-dev/home/.cache. The project folder stays a bind mount; nothing in this slice moves or hides it.

FILES: scripts/container/volume-dirs.sh (new, sourced lib), scripts/container/entrypoint.sh, scripts/container/seed-orca-state.sh, scripts/container/provision.d/45-scratch-volumes (new, executable, same conventions as its siblings), scripts/container/smoke.sh, tests/scratch-volumes-container.bats (new). Do NOT touch scripts/launcher.sh or CLAUDE.md.

SPEC
1. scripts/container/volume-dirs.sh defines volume_dirs <agent-home>: prints, one per line, each entry of $CLAUDE_ORCA_VOLUME_DIRS that (a) starts with "<agent-home>/", (b) has no '..' path segment, and (c) `mountpoint -q` confirms is a mount point. Anything else is dropped with one 'ignored' line on stderr. Unset/empty variable: prints nothing, exit 0. It never creates a directory.
2. entrypoint.sh, root phase, directly after the existing `chown_agent_tree "$USER_DATA_DIR"` (about line 395, under the same PRIVDROP condition): for each volume_dirs "$AGENT_HOME" entry whose owner (stat -c %u) is not $AGENT_UID, chown_agent_tree it. Non-fatal. A dir already owned by the agent is not walked.
3. seed-orca-state.sh: the worktree base is "<agent home>/worktrees" when that exact path is among volume_dirs, else today's "$PROJECT_DIR/.orca-worktrees". And where the script today exits early because orca-data.json already exists: when the volume base applies, first rewrite -- jq, tmp file in the same directory, mv -- every repos[] entry whose .path == $PROJECT_DIR AND whose .worktreeBasePath == "$PROJECT_DIR/.orca-worktrees" to the volume base and log one line; any other value is left alone; jq missing or failing leaves the file byte-identical, warns, and still exits 0. (The entrypoint runs this before `orca-ide --serve` starts, so Orca is not holding the file.) Update the header comment: why worktrees left the share, and that worktrees already under .orca-worktrees keep working because git tracks them by path and worktree-gc is path-agnostic.
4. provision.d/45-scratch-volumes (runs as agent; idempotent; the step's exit code is its status). For each volume_dirs entry D, with rel="${D#$AGENT_HOME/}" and legacy="$PROJECT_DIR/.claude-dev/home/$rel":
   GUARD -- act only when PROJECT_DIR is non-empty, legacy is an existing directory, and stat -c %d differs between D and legacy (a separate filesystem). Same device, or D not a mount: log '<D>: not a separate mount -- untouched' and touch NOTHING. This guard is the point of the slice: without the volume, D and legacy are the same directory and a delete would destroy live data.
   rel = .cache or .npm (regenerable): rm -rf "$legacy".
   rel = .local/share/opencode (sessions db): when "$D/.migrated-from-home" exists just rm -rf "$legacy". Otherwise rm -rf "$D/.migrating"; cp -a "$legacy/." "$D/.migrating/"; on failure remove .migrating, leave legacy intact, exit non-zero. On success move each top-level entry of .migrating into D -- an entry D already has is NOT overwritten, it lands as "<entry>.from-home" -- then remove .migrating, create "$D/.migrated-from-home", and only then rm -rf "$legacy".
   any other rel (worktrees included): nothing to migrate, untouched.
5. scripts/container/smoke.sh about line 228 checks the seeded worktreeBasePath: make it expect the volume base when "<agent home>/worktrees" is a mount point, else the old path.

TESTS -- tests/scratch-volumes-container.bats, modelled on tests/provision.bats, tests/chown-sockets.bats and tests/container-entrypoint-seed.bats (read how they fake the home, stub tools on PATH and observe chown). Stub `mountpoint` on PATH. For a REAL second filesystem use a unique dir under /dev/shm (tmpfs) against $BATS_TEST_TMPDIR, and `skip` when stat -c %d shows they are the same device. Exactly these 9 cases, in this order:
 1 'volume_dirs keeps only real mounts under the agent home': an entry outside the home, one with '..', and one that is not a mount point are dropped; two good ones are printed in order.
 2 'the entrypoint chowns a volume dir owned by someone else, and only then'.
 3 'a fresh seed puts worktrees on the volume when it is mounted': .repos[0].worktreeBasePath == "<home>/worktrees".
 4 'without the volume the seed keeps <project>/.orca-worktrees'.
 5 'an existing orca-data.json on the old default is rewritten, a custom path is left alone'.
 6 'shadowed caches are deleted only behind a separate mount': same directory / same device -> .cache content still there and the log says 'not a separate mount'; real second filesystem -> legacy .cache and .npm gone, the volume dirs untouched.
 7 'opencode data is copied before the old copy is removed and nothing on the volume is overwritten': legacy has opencode.db and auth.json, the volume already has its own auth.json -> afterwards the volume has legacy's opencode.db, its own auth.json unchanged, legacy's as auth.json.from-home, the marker file, no .migrating, and legacy is gone.
 8 'a failed copy leaves the old data where it was': make cp fail (stub it) -> legacy intact, no marker, the step exits non-zero.
 9 'the step is idempotent': a second run changes nothing and exits 0.

title: launcher: caches, opencode data and worker worktrees mount on per-container docker volumes; the project folder stays a bind mount
description:
OBJECTIVE: the project folder and /home/agent are macOS bind mounts, and file-creating work on that share is what the Docker VM process pays for (measured in claude-orca-19o: 3000 small files create/stat/rm = 901 ms and 61,129 VM interrupts on the share vs 59 ms and 330 on a docker volume; a full checkout 842 ms / 55,654 vs 283 ms / 10,848). Move the write-heavy, regenerable agent state onto per-container docker volumes, exactly the way ~/.config/orca already is (state_volume). The project folder itself and the rest of the home STAY bind mounts -- the user must keep seeing the folder the template was started in, on the Mac and in Orca. This slice is the LAUNCHER half; the container half is a separate bead and the only interface between them is the env var below.

FILES: scripts/launcher.sh (bash 3.2 only), tests/scratch-volumes.bats (new), tests/helpers/setup.bash (additive only, if needed), CLAUDE.md. This slice is built ON TOP of the cpu-cap slice already committed in this worktree.

SPEC
1. Next to state_volume() add, with a comment giving the measured reason above and saying the project and home stay bind mounts:
   SCRATCH_VOLUMES="cache:/home/agent/.cache npm:/home/agent/.npm opencode:/home/agent/.local/share/opencode worktrees:/home/agent/worktrees"
   scratch_volume() { printf '%s-%s\n' "$1" "$2"; }      # <container name> <suffix>
2. container_create: directly after the state-volume --volume line, one --volume "$(scratch_volume "$name" <suffix>):<guest path>" per pair in SCRATCH_VOLUMES order, and one -e "CLAUDE_ORCA_VOLUME_DIRS=<the four guest paths joined by ':'>". Same for the built-image path and the runtime path. The two existing bind-mount --volume lines are not changed and stay first.
3. container_matches: after the home-mount check, for each pair require a line of $mounts ending in ":<guest path>". A missing one prints on stderr
     container <name> predates the scratch volumes (nothing mounted at <guest path>) -- recreating it
   (two leading spaces) and returns 1. CTR_RUNTIME=local still returns 0 before any of this.
4. Teardown (about line 3142): after the state volume, ctr volume rm "$(scratch_volume "$name" <suffix>)" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true for each pair.
5. CLAUDE.md, Architecture Overview, the paragraph that starts "`HOME` is `<project>/.claude-dev/home`": after the sentences about the ~/.config/orca volume add at most 10 lines: the four scratch volumes and their guest paths, the measured reason (the numbers above), that worker worktrees now land in /home/agent/worktrees instead of <project>/.orca-worktrees, that teardown removes them, and that the project folder and the rest of home remain bind mounts the Mac can see.

title: launcher: a null cpus means a default cap of half the Docker VM's cores (live-applied to kept containers)
description:

title: Parallel agents can saturate the Mac: containers run uncapped, write-heavy work sits on the macOS file share
description:
REPORT (2026-09-21): ~6 agents in another folder's session, Docker VM service at ~600% CPU on the Mac.

MEASURED in this container (VM has 10 vCPUs; /proc/stat here is VM-wide, so other containers are visible as 'VM minus this cgroup'):
- Template machinery is NOT the load. Per Bash tool call: 6 PreToolUse hooks + worktree-gc + Orca hook = ~70 ms CPU total. statusline 12 ms. cost-mirror 54 ms/prompt. orca CLI call 80 ms, polled every 60 s by the spooler. code-map engine absent here (rc=3 in 6 ms).
- Agent runtimes: 6 parallel `opencode run` (glm-5.3-flash) = 429% of a core for the first 5 s (Bun startup), then 40-75% of ONE core total; mem peak 3.8 GiB. One headless worker steady ~9%. A Claude Code TUI merely waiting on a tool = 8.1% of a core (6.1% main render thread, 18 read syscalls/s -- not file polling). Orca main 2.5%. So 6 agents ~= 1 core sustained, never 6.
- Every VM-wide sample outside my own tests: whole VM 2-20% of a core, other containers 7-8%. The 600% was never live while sampling, and an idle guest means an idle VM process, so the spike was guest work: what the agents EXECUTE (tests, builds, installs), not the agents.
- No ceiling: launcher.sh:2321-2328 passes --cpus/--memory only when claude-orca.json has them; register seeds both null (launcher.sh:2629); cgroup cpu.max here = max.
- macOS file share penalty (project AND /home/agent are fakeowner/virtiofs bind mounts; only ~/.config/orca is a native volume): 3000 small files create/stat/rm = 901 ms + 61,129 VM interrupts on the bind mount vs 59 ms + 330 on the volume (15x wall, 185x VM exits, all served by the Docker VM process). Full checkout of this repo (what a new worker worktree costs): 842 ms / 55,654 intr vs 283 ms / 10,848. Warm reads are fine (git status, rg, bats docs.bats within 15%).
- Parallel-start defect seen once in 6: a worker died in 1 s with 'database is locked' -- opencode's shared 177 MB SQLite db under ~/.local/share/opencode.

FIX, in order of effect:
1. Default CPU cap at register: seed cpus to about half the host cores instead of null, and apply the same default to an existing folder whose key is null at next container create. Host-side (launcher.sh) -> mac-e2e evidence needed.
2. Move write-heavy state off the macOS share onto the per-container named volume pattern already used for ~/.config/orca: worker worktrees, ~/.cache, ~/.local/share/opencode. Teardown already removes the volume.
3. Bound concurrent workers in orca-dispatch (queue past N live dispatch records) and stagger starts to flatten the 429% launch burst.

RECORDER left running 12 h from 2026-09-21T21:18Z (pid 86130, scratchpad vm-load-recorder.py): appends to .claude-dev/run/vm-load.log whenever the whole VM exceeds 150% of a core -- user/sys split, forks/s, intr/s, this container vs others, top 3 processes here. High forks/s = test/build storm; high sys+intr = file-share churn; high user with low forks = a runaway process. Read it first when picking this up.

Fix 2 (scratch volumes) = claude-orca-7uy (launcher, merged 62a3b7c) + claude-orca-1eh (container, merged 296fa11). Fix 3 (bound concurrent workers) is DROPPED -- decided in chat 2026-09-21: the number of concurrent agents stays unlimited. Requirement kept: the folder the template is started in stays a bind mount, visible on the Mac and in Orca. Real run on main in this volume-less container: provision.d/45-scratch-volumes with the var unset, with the four paths (none a mount point) and with a real mount that has no policy -- file counts identical before/after (.cache 4836, .npm 2058, opencode 6368), nothing created. title: A recreated container downgrades the image's Orca to setup.sh's pin: the launcher builds at the app's version but never tells docker run
description:
Observed 2026-09-19 on the container the user rebuilt from the Mac. .claude-dev/run/build.log: 'RUN CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION=2.1.278 ORCA_VERSION=1.4.203 /opt/claude-orca-setup.sh --image', tag claude-orca:latest-orca1.4.203 -- the launcher builds at the Mac app's version because Orca refuses a client/runtime protocol mismatch (epic claude-orca-8uo). .claude-dev/run/setup.log from the SAME start: 'orca: installing 1.4.197'; /opt/orca/VERSION now reads 1.4.197.

Cause: the docker run command (scripts/launcher.sh, the 'set -- run -d --name' block at ~line 2202) carries no ORCA_VERSION, so the boot-time setup.sh falls back to its own pin (scripts/container/setup.sh:36), phase_orca (~line 499) sees stamp 1.4.203 != 1.4.197 and reinstalls the pin over the image's build: a download on every recreate, and a runtime that no longer matches the app the image was built for. The runtime path (plain ubuntu:24.04) has the same hole -- it installs the pin, never the app's version.

DECISION (orchestrator): the launcher hands docker run '-e ORCA_VERSION=<v>' where <v> is wanted_orca_version (scripts/launcher.sh ~line 1358) -- the ONE answer the image tag and the build arg already use: the app's version when this host has one, the Dockerfile's ARG default otherwise -- whenever that answer is non-empty. Boot-time setup.sh, setup.sh --check (10-toolchain-verify) and the runtime-path install then all agree with the image. Rejected: teaching setup.sh to adopt whatever stamp it finds when ORCA_VERSION is unset -- it loosens --check, which has to stay a strict reading of the box, and leaves the runtime path installing the pin.

Consequence, measured: with ORCA_VERSION in the container's environment every shell inherits it. Running the suite with ORCA_VERSION=1.4.203 ambient turns exactly one case red: tests/container-image.bats 'setup.sh parses, and --check reports every phase's result on any box', which reads the pin out of setup.sh's text while the script itself honours the environment. SUPERSEDE (test-only, of the claude-orca-qa2.6-frozen case, no assertion changed): directly after the case's '[ -n "$pin" ]' line add
    pin="${ORCA_VERSION:-$pin}"
with a one-sentence comment (the script honours an ambient ORCA_VERSION, so the case has to want what the script wants). That line goes in the RED commit.

scripts/launcher.sh runs on macOS bash 3.2.57: no associative arrays, no mapfile, no ${x^^}, no += onto an empty array under set -u. The docker run line is built with 'set -- "$@" ...'; add the new -e the way the CLAUDE_ORCA_SETUP conditional a few lines below the fixed block does.

Do, in one slice (Write/Edit in pieces of at most 150 lines, one file per response, report under 60 lines):
(A) tests/launcher-orca-version-run.bats (new). Model the fixture on tests/launcher-v3.bats 'open runs the container with ...' (line ~172: how the docker stub records the run line) and tests/launcher-v3-build.bats 'build passes --build-arg ORCA_VERSION from the installed app' (line ~327: how an installed app at a version is faked). Unset the ambient ORCA_VERSION, PROJECT_DIR, CLAUDE_ORCA_ROOT and BEADS_DIR in setup.
  case 1 "open passes the installed app's Orca version to docker run": with a fake app at 1.4.203 the recorded docker run line contains '-e ORCA_VERSION=1.4.203'.
  case 2 "with no app the run carries the Dockerfile's ARG default": the recorded run line contains '-e ORCA_VERSION=<v>' where <v> is read in the test from the repo Dockerfile's 'ARG ORCA_VERSION=' line, never a literal.
  case 3 "the run, the image tag and the build arg carry one version": in one open that builds with a fake app at 1.4.203, the recorded docker build line's '--build-arg ORCA_VERSION=', the '-orca<ver>' suffix of its --tag, and the run line's '-e ORCA_VERSION=' all say 1.4.203.
(B) tests/container-image.bats: the one SUPERSEDE line above, nothing else.
(C) scripts/launcher.sh: the conditional -e, with a comment of at most four lines giving the measured reason.
Commit RED ((A) and (B) only) then GREEN ((C) only); 'git commit -m ... -- <paths>', never bare, never amend. title: setup.sh --check FAILs every Mac folder: it wants agent at uid 1000 after the entrypoint re-mapped it to HOST_UID
description:
Observed 2026-09-19 on the container the user rebuilt from the Mac: the SessionStart hook's first line was '[provision] 10-toolchain-verify FAILED -- [check] FAIL  agent user: want uid 1000, got 501'. The launcher runs the container with -e HOST_UID=$(id -u) (501 on a Mac); scripts/container/entrypoint.sh:335-339 re-maps agent to it with usermod -u so the bind mounts stay the owner's; scripts/container/setup.sh run_checks (line ~759) still compares against the literal 1000 (introduced in 72c28a9, before the check ever ran in a running container). Every Mac folder therefore shows a FAILED provisioning row on its first prompt, and tests/container-image.bats case 'setup.sh parses, and --check reports every phase...' is red on such a box (line 183).
Fix: the row wants ${HOST_UID:-1000} -- the uid the entrypoint maps to when the launcher passed one, the image's 1000 otherwise. A failed usermod ('continuing') still shows as a FAIL naming both uids, which is the truth.

title: worktree-gc: append every run (mode, Orca reachability, exit, every line, busy pid) to run/worktree-gc.log so a hook run that left a worktree behind explains itself
description:
Diagnostic gap found in real use (2026-09-18): after `git merge joe-rayment/wt-ltd` the PostToolUse hook `worktree-gc --after-merge` ran but left the merged wt-ltd worktree in place; a by-hand `worktree-gc` minutes later removed it ("closed Orca's idle terminal"), and feeding the hook payload by hand to `--after-merge` also removed a fresh worktree. Nothing recorded what the hook run saw (Orca unreachable? busy process? a timing race with the terminal close), because hook stdout is transient. Fix: scripts/worktree-gc.sh appends one block per run to <project>/.claude-dev/run/worktree-gc.log: a header line "<ISO-8601 UTC> mode=<cli|quiet|report|after-merge|hook-session-start> orca=<reachable|unreachable> exit=<n>" followed by every line the run emitted (including the ones --quiet suppresses on stdout, and for a busy worktree the pid, ppid and cmdline of the first process that made it busy). Cap the file at 200 KB by truncating the oldest half when it grows past that. --after-merge also logs the command text that triggered it (first 200 chars). Nothing else in the script changes; all three FROZEN suites (tests/worktree-gc.bats, tests/container-provision-worktree-sweep.bats, tests/worktree-gc-wiring.bats) must stay green untouched.

"a busy worktree's log names the pid and cmdline that kept it" (occupy a worktree with `sleep 300` started in it; kill it in teardown); 3. title: worktree-gc: keep a clean worktree whose branch is unmerged (report STRANDED, kept: unmerged) -- supersedes case 2 of tests/worktree-gc.bats (claude-orca-6zg)
description:
Policy fix for scripts/worktree-gc.sh, found in real use 2026-09-18: a CLEAN worktree whose branch has commits not in main is removed by step 2 (the branch is kept and reported STRANDED). In practice that is the state of every finished-but-not-yet-verified worker: merging slice A's branch fires the PostToolUse `worktree-gc --after-merge`, which removed slice B's finished worktree while the verifier was still running its CHECK in it (claude-orca-kbu today; the branch survived, the worktree had to be re-added by hand). Removing such a worktree frees ~4 MB and buys nothing; the branch is the data and it stays anyway. New rule for step 2: a clean worktree is removed ONLY when its branch is contained in main/master (`git merge-base --is-ancestor `) or when it is detached with HEAD contained in the base. A clean worktree whose branch has commits not in the base is KEPT and reported "STRANDED branch : N commit(s) not in main (worktree

kept: unmerged)" with exit 1 -- the same shape the busy/dirty kept-worktree lines already use. Busy, dirty and directory-gone handling are unchanged. title: orca-worker-run: headless opencode worker that runs the spec, heartbeats, writes a receipt, sends worker_done and exits (no resident TUI)
description:
Problem (user, 2026-09-18): worker slices dispatched with `orca-dispatch <bead> --agent opencode` run as a resident opencode TUI inside an Orca terminal. Measured today: ~900 MB RSS per TUI for as long as the terminal lives, three of them resident at once with only one working, the harness killing background tasks for low memory; a headless `opencode run --format json` of the same model peaked at 708 MB and exited after 10 s, freeing everything. The user's direction: Claude orchestrates, OpenRouter models execute beads -- nobody watches the TUI, so workers must be headless runs that exit, never resident processes.

Slice 1 of 2: the headless runner. Write files in pieces of at most 150 lines per Write/Edit call, one file per response, report under 60 lines. bash, `set -uo pipefail`, bash-3.2-clean (scripts/lint-bash32.sh scans scripts/).

(A) New scripts/orca-worker-run.sh + symlink bin/orca-worker-run -> ../scripts/orca-worker-run.sh. Resolve its own path like scripts/orca-dispatch.sh (_resolve_script_path), source scripts/lib/paths.sh and scripts/lib/orca-orch.sh (for orca_call / orca_field and the run-dir helpers already there -- read them first).
    orca-worker-run --task <task_id> --spec <file> --model <openrouter/...> --dir <worktree> [--run-dir <dir>] [--heartbeat-s <n>] [--bead <id>]
  Behaviour, in order:
   1. Guard env: `set -a; . <run-dir>/openrouter-guard.env; set +a` exactly as orca_opencode_command does (scripts/lib/orca-orch.sh ~360-418); die with exit 2 and one stderr line when the env file is missing.
   2. Dispatch id: poll <run-dir>/orchestration/dispatch/*.json for the record whose .task_id equals --task, up to 30 s (orca-dispatch writes it right after `orchestration dispatch`); take .dispatch_id. If none appears, continue with an empty dispatch id (worker_done still carries --task-id).
   3. Record the base: `base=$(git -C <dir> rev-parse HEAD)`.
   4. Run headless: `opencode run -m <model> --dir <dir> --auto --format json "$(cat <spec>)"` with stdout+stderr to <run-dir>/orchestration/workers/<task_id>.log (mkdir -p), in the background; while it runs, every --heartbeat-s seconds (default 240) send `orchestration send --type heartbeat --subject alive --dispatch-id <d> --json` (skip when the dispatch id is empty) so orca-wait's stall watch stays quiet. Wait for it; capture the exit code.
   5. Receipt: parse the json log the way scripts/delegate.sh does (tokens_in, tokens_out, usd, wall_seconds; copy its jq) into <run-dir>/orchestration/workers/<task_id>.receipt.json with fields {task_id, dispatch_id, bead, model, dir, exit_code, tokens_in, tokens_out, usd, wall_seconds, started_at, finished_at}; hand it to cost-mirror with the same best-effort call delegate.sh makes (`cost-mirror --ingest-delegate-receipt <file>`, fail-open).
   6. Report: files = `git -C <dir> diff --name-only <base>..HEAD` joined by commas (plus `git status --porcelain` paths, deduplicated); body = the last assistant text in the log (the final "text" part in the json events; fall back to the last 20 non-empty lines of the log), trimmed to 1500 chars; then `orchestration send --type worker_done --subject "<bead or task_id> done" --body "<body>" --task-id <task_id> --dispatch-id <d> --outcome succeeded|failed (failed when exit code != 0 or when the log's last event is an error) --files-modified <files> --json`. Never skip the send: a failed run reports failed, so the orchestrator is never left waiting.
   7. Exit with opencode's exit code. Redact the guard token from the log and the receipt the way delegate.sh's redact_secret does.
(B) New tests/orca-worker-run.bats. Stubs on PATH in a tmpdir: `opencode` (asserts argv contains `run`, `-m <model>`, `--dir <dir>`, `--format json`; prints a canned json event stream with a "text" part reading "did the thing" and token usage the receipt jq can read; writes <dir>/made-by-worker.txt and commits it so diff --name-only shows it; sleeps $STUB_SLEEP seconds; exits $STUB_EXIT), `orca-ide` (appends argv to $ORCA_STUB_LOG; answers `{"ok":true}`), `cost-mirror` (records argv). A real git repo as <dir>. Named cases, each its own @test:
   1. "worker-run sends worker_done succeeded with the task id, the dispatch id read from the dispatch record, and the committed file in --files-modified"
   2. "worker-run reports failed when opencode exits non-zero and still sends worker_done"
   3. "worker-run writes a receipt with tokens, usd and the exit code and hands it to cost-mirror"
   4. "worker-run sends at least one heartbeat during a long run" (STUB_SLEEP=3, --heartbeat-s 1)
   5. "worker-run proceeds with an empty dispatch id when no record appears" (no record; worker_done still sent with --task-id; no heartbeat sent)
   6. "worker-run exits 2 with one stderr line when the guard env file is missing"
   7. "worker-run redacts the guard token from the log and the receipt"
Commit RED (test, script absent) then GREEN; `git commit -m ... -- <paths>`, never bare, never amend; the test is FROZEN from RED -- if it has a bug, stop and report it in worker_done instead of editing it.

Wiring for worktree-gc (built in the sibling bead; scripts/worktree-gc.sh exists on main when this starts) and branch-guard (bin/branch-guard, sibling bead). Nothing here changes either script's core behaviour. Write files in pieces of at most 150 lines per Write/Edit call, one file per response, and report in under 60 lines. Do, in one slice (bash-3.2-clean under scripts/): (A) config/claude-settings.json (jq-valid, keep the existing `[ -x "__HOST__/template/bin/X" ] && exec ... ; exit 0` shape): - PreToolUse, matcher Bash: add `branch-guard` right after bd-guard. - PostToolUse (new event), matcher Bash: `[ -x "__HOST__/template/bin/worktree-gc" ] && exec "__HOST__/template/bin/worktree-gc" --after-merge; exit 0`. - SessionStart: add `worktree-gc --quiet` after the provision status entry (its stdout reaches the agent's first prompt: STRANDED lines and the one summary line only). (B) scripts/worktree-gc.sh: add `--after-merge` -- read the PostToolUse hook JSON from stdin; exit 0 silently unless .tool_input.command matches `git merge` or `git branch -d` / `git branch -D` (word boundaries); then run the normal gc in --quiet mode. Add the flag to the usage header. (C) scripts/session-end-audit.sh: after the existing dirty-tree note, run `"$(dirname "$0")/worktree-gc.sh" --quiet --project "$cwd"` (resolve the symlink the way the other scripts do), and for every STRANDED line it prints, `dev-log change "session ended with stranded work: " ...` -- still fail-open, still exit 0. (D) scripts/disk-cleanup.sh: a new numbered section that runs `worktree-gc --quiet` on the project (PROJECT_DIR, else the toplevel of $PWD) and notes its summary line via note(); --report additionally lists the size of /.claude-dev/delegate with the label "delegate job dirs (worktree-gc sweeps home/ and config/ of finished jobs)". tests/disk-cleanup.bats and tests/disk-cleanup-ondemand.bats are FROZEN for closed beads -- add nothing there; new cases go in the new file below. (E) tests: new tests/worktree-gc-wiring.bats, named cases each its own @test: 1. "claude-settings.json wires branch-guard under PreToolUse Bash, worktree-gc --after-merge under PostToolUse Bash and worktree-gc --quiet under SessionStart" 2. "worktree-gc --after-merge ignores a command that is not a merge or branch delete" (payload `git status` -> exit 0, empty output) 3. "worktree-gc --after-merge sweeps a merged worktree after a git merge command" (real repo + worktree merged into main, payload command `git merge wt-x`, cwd = repo -> the worktree is gone, output has "removed") 4. "session-end-audit calls worktree-gc and dev-logs a STRANDED line" (stub dev-log on PATH recording argv; repo with an unmerged branch) 5. "disk-cleanup --report names the delegate job dirs" Update tests/no-residue.bats's required-event loop to include PostToolUse. (F) Docs: in CLAUDE.md AND AGENTS.md (tests/docs.bats requires the same sections), add one paragraph to the Architecture Overview describing worktree-gc (what it removes, what STRANDED means, where it runs: boot step 65, after `git merge`, SessionStart, SessionEnd, disk-cleanup) and one sentence on branch-guard. knowledge-base/README.md: if a delegation or sandbox page lists the hooks, add both there; otherwise leave it. Commit RED (tests) then GREEN; `git commit -m ... -- `, never bare, never amend, test untouched after RED. CHECK: bats tests/worktree-gc-wiring.bats tests/no-residue.bats tests/docs.bats tests/config-sync.bats 0' config/claude-settings.json` exits 0. FROZEN: tests/worktree-gc-wiring.bats CLASS: feature ADDENDUM (found while verifying the sibling beads, 2026-09-18): (B2) scripts/worktree-gc.sh step 3 skips a branch that is checked out in a KEPT worktree (busy or dirty) silently, so unmerged work in a live or dirty worktree never shows. Change: for each kept worktree whose branch has commits not in main, print "STRANDED branch : N commit(s) not in main (worktree

kept: busy)" or "(... kept: uncommitted changes)" and exit 1. Merged-and-kept stays silent. tests/worktree-gc.bats is FROZEN -- its 9 cases must stay green; the new behaviour is tested in tests/worktree-gc-wiring.bats. (G) scripts/worktree-gc.sh busy scan. Measured 2026-09-18 on the real folder: every Orca worktree carries an idle default terminal (a `zsh -l`, parent = the /opt/Orca/orca-ide daemon-entry.js process, no children, cwd = the worktree), so the /proc cwd scan calls a finished, merged worktree "busy" forever and the sweep never reaches it. Also measured: `orca-ide worktree rm --worktree path:

--json` on such a worktree returns {"removed":true}, deletes the directory, kills that shell, closes the terminal in Orca and drops the merged branch. Change: when Orca is reachable, a process does NOT count as busy if its parent's /proc//cmdline contains "orca-ide" AND it has no child processes (no /proc/*/status with PPid == it) -- those are Orca's own idle worktree terminals and `orca worktree rm` closes them. Any other process (a user's editor, a running build, a shell with children, a shell whose parent is not orca-ide) still means busy. When Orca is unreachable, count every process as today (plain `git worktree remove` cannot close a terminal). Print "removed

(closed Orca's idle terminal)" in that case so the log says what happened. Put the "is this an idle Orca terminal shell" test in a small function with the pid as argument, so a test can drive it. Do NOT touch scripts/orca-wait.sh. (E2) Two more cases in tests/worktree-gc-wiring.bats (plan becomes 1..7): 6. "worktree-gc reports STRANDED for an unmerged branch checked out in a kept dirty worktree" (real repo, worktree with a commit not in main plus an untracked file -> output has both "FAIL: kept" and "STRANDED branch", exit 1) 7. "worktree-gc treats an idle shell whose parent is orca-ide as not busy when Orca is reachable, and as busy when it is not" -- build the occupant as `(cd && exec -a orca-ide-parent bash -c 'sleep 300 & wait')` in the background, so the `sleep` has cwd and a parent whose cmdline contains "orca-ide" and no children of its own; with the stub orca-ide reachable (ORCA_STUB_REACHABLE=true, the stub's `worktree rm` removes the path as in tests/container-provision-worktree-sweep.bats) the worktree is "removed"; with the stub unreachable the same setup is "busy". Kill the background processes in teardown. PASS-IF gains: plan 1..7 in tests/worktree-gc-wiring.bats; tests/worktree-gc.bats and tests/container-provision-worktree-sweep.bats still zero 'not ok'.

title: worktree-gc: one sweep for merged worktrees, merged branches, stranded work and finished delegate job dirs; 65-worktree-sweep delegates to it
description:
Problem (user, 2026-09-18): the template leaves git worktrees and branches lying around after work is merged. Measured in this folder: 2 clean, fully-merged delegate worktrees still checked out, 15 merged branches (delegate/*, worktree-agent-*, joe-rayment/wt-*, integration, s8, v2...), and 329 MB under .claude-dev/delegate -- of which the worktrees are 4 MB each and each job's home/.npm/_cacache (94 MB) + config/opencode/node_modules (62 MB) are the rest. Today the ONLY cleanup is scripts/container/provision.d/65-worktree-sweep, which runs at container boot, never deletes a branch, and never touches job dirs. The user also wants stranded work (a branch with commits not in main) to be impossible to miss, never silently deleted. Do, in one slice (bash, `set -uo pipefail`, no bash-4-only syntax -- scripts/lint-bash32.sh scans scripts/). Write files in pieces of at most 150 lines per Write/Edit call, one file per response, and report in under 60 lines. (A) New scripts/worktree-gc.sh with symlink bin/worktree-gc -> ../scripts/worktree-gc.sh (same shape as bin/bd-guard). Resolve its own path the way scripts/orca-dispatch.sh does (_resolve_script_path) and source scripts/lib/paths.sh. Usage: worktree-gc [--report] [--quiet] [--project ] Project dir: --project, else $PROJECT_DIR, else `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` of $PWD; the MAIN worktree is the first line of `git worktree list --porcelain`. Exit 0 when nothing is stranded, 1 when any STRANDED/FAIL line was printed, 0 with "not a git repo" when there is no repo. --report prints exactly the lines it WOULD print but deletes nothing (prefix each with "would "). --quiet prints only STRANDED/FAIL lines and one final summary line "worktree-gc: removed N worktree(s), deleted M branch(es), swept K job dir(s)" -- and prints nothing at all when all counts are 0 and nothing is stranded. Steps, in order: 1. HEAD of the main worktree: if `git symbolic-ref --short HEAD` is neither main nor master (or detached), print "STRANDED HEAD is on , not main -- the live version is main; merge back or switch" and set exit 1. Never switch branches itself. 2. Every worktree other than the main one, exactly the current 65-worktree-sweep semantics and wording (copy its code: /proc cwd scan for busy, `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all` for dirty, `orca-ide worktree rm --worktree path:

--json` when `orca-ide status --json` says .result.runtime.reachable==true, else `git worktree remove` then --force, then `git worktree prune`): lines "pruned

(directory gone)", "busy

(a running process has it as its cwd)", "FAIL: kept

(uncommitted or untracked changes)" (exit 1), "removed

". NEW: remember each removed worktree's branch for step 3. 3. Every local branch other than main/master and the checked-out one (`git for-each-ref refs/heads`): if `git merge-base --is-ancestor main` -> `git branch -d ` and print "deleted branch (merged)"; else print "STRANDED branch : N commit(s) not in main -- merge it or `git branch -D ` to drop the work" where N is `git rev-list --count main..`, exit 1, delete nothing. Use master when there is no main. A branch still checked out in a kept worktree is skipped silently. 4. Delegate job dirs: for each /.claude-dev/delegate// whose pid file names a dead process (or has no pid) AND whose worktree/ directory is gone (step 2 removed it, or it never existed): rm -rf its home/ and config/ only, print "swept job (home, config)"; keep receipt.json, runner.log, branch, env, pid, worktree-add.log and the dir itself. A job whose pid is alive is untouched. (B) scripts/container/provision.d/65-worktree-sweep becomes a thin wrapper: it keeps its header comment (rewrite it to say it delegates), its PROJECT_DIR / not-a-repo early exits, then `exec "$(dirname "$0")/../../worktree-gc.sh" --project "$PROJECT_DIR"`. tests/container-provision-worktree-sweep.bats is FROZEN and must stay green UNCHANGED -- its stub orca-ide is found on PATH as `orca-ide`, honour that (resolve the CLI exactly as the step does today: $ORCA_CLI, then the known paths, then `command -v orca orca-ide`). (C) New tests/worktree-gc.bats, modelled on tests/container-provision-worktree-sweep.bats (real `git init -b main`, real `git worktree add`, the same stub orca-ide, short_tmpdir under /tmp). Named cases, each its own @test: 1. "gc removes a clean worktree whose branch is merged into main and deletes the branch" 2. "gc removes a clean worktree whose branch has commits not in main, keeps the branch and reports STRANDED with the count" (exit 1; the line contains "STRANDED branch" and "1 commit") 3. "gc keeps a dirty worktree and reports FAIL: kept" (exit 1) 4. "gc deletes merged branches with no worktree -- delegate/x, wt/y, worktree-agent-z and a plain name -- and keeps an unmerged one as STRANDED" 5. "gc reports STRANDED when the main worktree's HEAD is not on main and deletes nothing" 6. "gc sweeps home/ and config/ of a finished delegate job but keeps its receipt, log, branch and env; a job with a live pid is untouched" (live pid: start `sleep 300 &` and write its pid; kill it in teardown) 7. "gc --report prints would-lines and deletes nothing" 8. "gc --quiet prints nothing on a clean repo and exits 0" 9. "gc uses orca-ide worktree rm when Orca is reachable" (stub log records the argv) (D) Commit the test RED first (RED-AT -- the script absent, tests failing), then the implementation GREEN; use `git commit -m ... -- ` (never a bare commit), never amend, never edit the test after RED. title: branch-guard: PreToolUse hook denying branch creation or switching off main without BRANCH_OK=1
description:
Problem (user, 2026-09-18): the agent sometimes starts working on a git branch unprompted, and the user then loses time asking why changes do not appear in the live version. This template is for solo development: work lands on main, in the one working tree the user is looking at. A branch is rare, deliberate, and always merged back in the same session.

Do, in one slice (bash, `set -uo pipefail`, bash-3.2-clean -- scripts/lint-bash32.sh scans scripts/). Write files in pieces of at most 150 lines per Write/Edit call, one file per response, and report in under 60 lines.

(A) New scripts/branch-guard.sh with symlink bin/branch-guard -> ../scripts/branch-guard.sh. A PreToolUse hook for the Bash tool, the SAME shape as scripts/outbound-guard.sh: read the hook JSON from stdin (exit 0 silently when stdin is a tty, empty, not JSON, tool_name != "Bash", or .tool_input.command absent), decide on `.tool_input.command`, and deny by printing the hookSpecificOutput JSON {hookEventName:"PreToolUse", permissionDecision:"deny", permissionDecisionReason:<reason>} and exiting 0 (copy outbound-guard's deny()). Allowed calls print nothing and exit 0. Fail open on every error.
  Denied -- word-boundary matches anywhere in the command text, including after && ; | and inside $( ):
    git checkout -b <x>  and  git checkout -B <x>
    git switch -c <x>, git switch -C <x>, git switch --create <x>
    git worktree add ...
    git branch <name>   (creation: a first non-option argument, and none of the flags that delete, move, copy, list or filter: d, D, m, M, c, C, a, r, l, list, merged, no-merged, contains, show-current, format, v, vv)
    git switch <name>   where <name> is not main, master or the single dash (switch only ever takes a branch)
    git checkout <name> where <name> is a single bare word that is not main/master/dash/double-dash, contains no "--", AND `git -C <cwd> show-ref --verify --quiet refs/heads/<name>` succeeds (cwd = .cwd from the payload, else $PWD) -- so `git checkout somefile`, `git checkout -- path`, `git checkout HEAD~1 -- path`, `git checkout <sha> -- path` all pass.
  Escape hatch: the command text contains the token BRANCH_OK=1 (as an env prefix, e.g. `BRANCH_OK=1 git switch -c x`) -> allowed. The reason text must say, in one or two sentences: this template is solo development on main; the live version the user sees is main's working tree, so a branch hides the work; create one only when the user asked or a delegated slice needs isolation, prefix the command with BRANCH_OK=1 to proceed, and then merge it back into main before the turn ends (worktree-gc reports what is stranded).
  Never denied: git branch with no name, or with the list/delete/filter flags above; git worktree list, remove, prune; git merge <x>; git switch main|master|dash; git checkout main|master; git log/diff/status/rebase and every other verb; git push (outbound-guard owns that); anything that is not a git invocation.
(B) New tests/branch-guard.bats, the pattern of tests/outbound-guard.bats (jq -n builds the payload with tool_name Bash and tool_input.command; `run` the guard with the payload on stdin; assert status 0 and either empty output or .hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision == "deny"). For the `git checkout <name>` cases build a real repo in a tmpdir with a branch `feature` and pass its path as .cwd. Named cases, each its own @test:
   1. "denies git checkout -b, checkout -B, switch -c, switch -C and switch --create"
   2. "denies git worktree add"
   3. "denies git branch <newname> but allows the list, delete, merged and show-current forms"
   4. "denies git switch <branch> other than main, master and dash"
   5. "denies git checkout <existing-branch> in the payload's cwd but allows checkout of a path, of -- path, of HEAD~1 -- path and of a word that is not a branch"
   6. "allows git checkout main and git switch main"
   7. "denies a branch creation chained after cd && or inside a command substitution"
   8. "allows anything prefixed BRANCH_OK=1"
   9. "the deny reason names main, BRANCH_OK=1 and merging back"
  10. "exits 0 with no output on a tty, empty stdin, non-JSON, a non-Bash tool and a payload without a command"
(C) Do NOT edit config/claude-settings.json in this slice (another bead wires the hook). Commit the test RED first (guard absent), then GREEN; `git commit -m ... -- <paths>`, never bare, never amend, never touch the test after RED.
