title: on-demand instruments: browsers (and other task-only tooling) are fetched when the work needs them, never carried by default -- the rule keeps the principle (verify the real thing, no proxy checks) without the weight
description:
User direction 2026-09-18: browsers/playwright must not be part of the template or home by default -- instructions (or an automatic first-use install) instead. Not every task needs a browser; the screenshot rule exists to stop artificial checks that do not map onto real usage (e.g. a script asserting what it believes is representative and passing while the real thing is broken), so re-orient the rule to keep that principle without the weight.
Measured: playwright is NOT in the image; ~/.cache/ms-playwright (849 MB) + ~/.cache/claude-orca-playwright are the on-demand fetch from an earlier take-screenshot/playwright-mcp use, and scripts/disk-cleanup.sh deliberately spares them (lines ~29-31). take-screenshot.sh:237 exits 3 with an install hint instead of installing. ~/.npm/_npx holds npx residue (asar, skills); ~/.local/share/claude/versions/* is Claude Code's own auto-updater (216 MB per version) on top of the image's /opt/claude.

title: mg8 regression: orca-dispatch's real spooler leaks into bats runs (inherits fd 3, never exits) and hangs ./run-tests.sh in frozen-hook.bats
description:
Seen 2026-09-17 on main da4f27f: ./run-tests.sh sat 49 minutes inside tests/frozen-hook.bats 'orca-dispatch and delegate suites stay green' (it nests bats tests/orca-dispatch-launch.bats tests/delegate.bats). Two 'orca-wait.sh --spool --from <the orchestrator's real ORCA_TERMINAL_HANDLE>' processes, started by orca-dispatch during that nested run, were reparented to init, looping on 'sleep 0.1' 48 minutes later, and held bats's output pipe open (bats-core's fd 3), so the run never finished. Three defects:
(a) the spooler launch in scripts/orca-dispatch.sh does not close inherited descriptors: it must run as `setsid nohup ... </dev/null >>"$log" 2>&1 3>&- &` (fd 3 is what bats waits on) -- and scripts/orca-wait.sh --spool should `exec 3>&-` defensively at start;
(b) the spooler does not exit when its root or dispatch dir disappears: with no readable dispatch dir it must exit at once, and the idle exit (CLAUDE_ORCA_SPOOL_IDLE_S) must count from the last LIVE record, so a stub-driven spooler whose tmpdir is gone dies within seconds, not never; the poll interval must respect CLAUDE_ORCA_WAIT_POLL_S (the 0.1s sleep seen is not it);
(c) tests that drive orca-dispatch through the orca stub must never start a real spooler: tests/helpers/orca-stub.bash's orca_stub_init exports CLAUDE_ORCA_SPOOL_CMD to a no-op shim (one place) so orca-dispatch-launch.bats, orca-dispatch.bats, frozen-hook.bats, orca-two-coordinators.bats, variant-carry.bats etc. inherit it; the one test that WANTS the real spooler (orca-wait-spool.bats case 1) sets it back explicitly.
Files: scripts/orca-dispatch.sh, scripts/orca-wait.sh, tests/helpers/orca-stub.bash, new tests/orca-spool-detach.bats (tests/orca-wait-spool.bats stays as is -- it was FROZEN for the closed mg8; add nothing there unless case 1 needs the explicit un-shim).

title: openrouter-guard: a 429 from one allowlisted provider must fail over to the next allowlisted one -- policy gains an explicit provider order
description:
Seen 2026-09-17 21:04-21:20Z: seven glm-5.3-flash workers and a single probe all got 429 '[DeepInfra] z-ai/glm-5.3-flash is temporarily rate-limited upstream' through the guard for 15+ minutes, while the same request with provider.order ["baseten"] answered 200 at once (fireworks/coreweave/deepinfra 429). Cause: config/provider-policy.json forces allow_fallbacks=false and opencode sends no provider.order, so OpenRouter tries only its default pick (DeepInfra) inside `only` and errors instead of hopping to another allowlisted provider. The user's rule (data never routes to China) is enforced by `only`; failing over INSIDE that list breaks nothing.

Design (decided): config/provider-policy.json gains "order": [<every allow[].slug, most reliable first: baseten, fireworks, together, parasail, coreweave, crusoe, deepinfra, nebius, groq, cerebras, google-vertex, amazon-bedrock, azure, mistral, venice, digitalocean>] with a _doc line; the guard's policy loader rejects a policy whose order carries a slug not in allow (or is missing/empty: fall back to the allow order and log once). force_provider: when the client sent no usable order, set provider.order to the policy order (client orders that are all-allowlisted are still kept as today; allow_fallbacks stays false; only stays the allowlist). The guard log line gains "order_source": "client"|"policy".
Files: scripts/container/openrouter-guard.py (force_provider ~267-300, policy loader ~150-190), config/provider-policy.json, the guard's bats/python tests (find them: grep -l 'force_provider\|openrouter-guard' tests/*.bats tests/**/*.py).

title: outbound-guard: gate git push on a GitHub connection, not on the prompt's wording
description:
The guard was ported (b1cabb2) as a mechanical restatement of config/claude-user-memory.md:12 -- 'push only when the current prompt asks for it'. The user's stated original intent was the opposite gate: avoid pushing when there is NO GitHub connection, and be biased to pushing when there is one. No connection check was ever written: the script has no gh invocation, no GH_TOKEN read and no network call (confirmed by reading it in full).

Observed cost, this session: I asked 'shall I push?', the user answered 'yes', PROMPT_RE did not match 'yes', line 158 cleared the marker, and the push was denied. The user had to retype the literal verb.

Scope of the change:
  - git push: gated on a GitHub connection (gh auth status, exit 0) instead of the marker. Connected -> ALLOW.
  - gh pr create / gh repo create: UNCHANGED, still marker-gated. They create outward artifacts other people see, which the user's instruction did not name.
  - bd dolt push: UNCHANGED, still marker-gated. Not GitHub, no connection concept applies.
  - the data-warehouse CLI rules: UNCHANGED, unconditional deny.
  - every existing fail-open path preserved.
  - config/claude-user-memory.md paragraph rewritten to match, or the prose keeps contradicting the mechanism and the prose is what gets read every session.

The connection check runs ONLY after PUSH_RE matches, so a plain Bash call never pays for it (measured: gh auth status is 0.39s here). Timeout via OUTBOUND_GUARD_GH_TIMEOUT (default 10s); timeout or error -> not connected -> deny, since a push would hang or fail too.
design:
OBJECTIVE
Replace the prompt-marker gate for 'git push' ONLY with a GitHub-connection gate. Connected -> allow. Not connected -> deny. Everything else in the guard keeps its current behaviour exactly.

FILES (touch these and no others)
  scripts/outbound-guard.sh      the gate
  tests/outbound-guard.bats      the contract (FROZEN from RED-AT)
  config/claude-user-memory.md   the paragraph at line 11-12

HOW
1. Add a connection check, called ONLY after PUSH_RE has already matched, so an ordinary Bash call never pays for it:
     gh_connected() { command -v gh >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
                      timeout "${OUTBOUND_GUARD_GH_TIMEOUT:-10}" gh auth status >/dev/null 2>&1; }
   Non-zero from timeout (124) or from gh, or gh absent -> NOT connected.
2. Split PUSH_RE into two regexes: GIT_PUSH_RE (git push) and MARKER_RE (gh pr create | gh repo create | bd dolt push). Keep the same word-boundary style -- explicit character classes, never GNU \\b.
3. Order inside the PreToolUse branch: the warehouse-CLI deny stays FIRST and unconditional. Then GIT_PUSH_RE -> gh_connected -> allow or deny. Then MARKER_RE -> the existing marker lookup, unchanged.
4. Preserve every fail-open path exactly as it is, including 'missing session_id fails open'. git push no longer needs a session_id at all (it does not read the marker), but the no-session_id payload must still exit 0.
5. Deny text for git push must name the connection, not the prompt. Something like:
     outbound-guard: no GitHub connection (gh auth status failed) -- a push would fail; run 'gh auth login' or commit locally.
6. Rewrite the paragraph in config/claude-user-memory.md so the prose matches the mechanism: git push is allowed whenever there is a GitHub connection and blocked when there is not; PRs, repo creation and dolt push still need the prompt to ask. The old sentence 'run only when the current prompt asks for them' must not survive for git push.
7. Update the script's own header comment, which currently documents the marker rule for all four verbs.

BOUNDARIES
- Do not touch the warehouse-CLI rules, SNOW_RE, SNOW_MODULE_RE or their tests.
- Do not remove the marker machinery or the --prompt mode; three verbs still use it.
- Do not edit config/claude-settings.json; the hook wiring does not change.
- No network calls in the tests: stub gh on PATH.

TEST NOTES (learned the expensive way)
- Copy the twelve PASS-IF case names into @test lines VERBATIM, one @test per name.
- Dry-run every assertion against a hand-built fixture before committing RED.
- bats here prints TAP with no summary line; do not assert on 'N tests, 0 failures'.
- For the timeout case set OUTBOUND_GUARD_GH_TIMEOUT=1 and make the gh stub sleep 3, so the case costs ~1s.
- For 'the connection check is not run for a non-outbound command', make the gh stub append to a file and assert the file does not exist after a 'git commit' payload.
- Write files in <=150-line Write/Edit pieces, one file per response; report under 60 lines.

COMMITS
Two: the test file RED first (subject 'tests: RED for the GitHub-connection push gate (claude-orca-diz)'), then the implementation GREEN. Record RED-AT and GREEN-AT SHAs on the bead with bd update --append-notes.
acceptance_criteria:
CHECK: bats tests/outbound-guard.bats

PASS-IF: the run prints a TAP plan line '1..N', zero lines beginning 'not ok', and one 'ok' line for each of these cases, named verbatim:
  git push is allowed when gh reports a GitHub connection
  git push is denied when gh reports no GitHub connection
  git push is denied when gh is not on PATH
  git push is denied when the connection check times out
  the git push deny message names the connection and not the prompt
  gh pr create still requires the prompt marker
  gh repo create still requires the prompt marker
  bd dolt push still requires the prompt marker
  the connection check is not run for a non-outbound command
  the warehouse CLI stays denied even when gh is connected
  git push with no session_id still fails open
  the rulebook paragraph describes the connection gate

CLASS: authorization guard -- this hook decides whether an outbound action reaches the network. The change LOOSENS it for one verb, so the contract pins both directions: allowed-when-connected AND denied-when-not, plus the three rules that must not move (gh pr create, gh repo create, bd dolt push) and the unconditional warehouse deny.

title: S5: the agent inside can see and repair its own provisioning
description:
'provision status' prints one row per step (name, ok/failed, when, the last line of its log) and 'provision run <step>' re-runs one. Both live in the template's bin/ like lane and tier-set, so they are typeable by name inside the container.

The session-start hook surfaces FAILED steps only -- a clean folder says nothing, a broken one puts the failing step and its last log line in front of the agent on the first prompt. That is the whole point of the epic: the environment reports its own faults to the thing that can fix them.

'claude-dev --doctor' on the Mac side grows the same rows, so a folder can be diagnosed from either side.

title: S4: provision.d -- the project-shaped work moves after Orca is serving
description:
Everything that is about THIS FOLDER rather than about the image comes out of the blocking path and becomes a numbered, idempotent step under scripts/container/provision.d/, run after orca-ide --serve has published its URL: toolchain verify (setup.sh --check), bd init, the instruction/config sync, orca repo add, git identity, the OpenRouter guard.

Each step writes run/provision/<step>.log and run/provision/<step>.status. No step is fatal. A step that fails leaves a status a human and an agent can both read, and the next start re-runs it -- idempotence is the whole contract, so every step must be safe to run on an already-provisioned folder.

The ordering constraint that made this necessary: the steps a folder needs are exactly the steps most likely to fail (a network hiccup, a half-written config, a bad token), and they were all in front of the thing that could have reported them.

title: S1: split the Dockerfile into claude-orca-base and the folder image
description:
Dockerfile.base carries the apt half (setup.sh --image) and the six payload phases (bats, dolt, bd, orca, opencode, claude) and builds the image claude-orca-base:<IMAGE_TAG>. Dockerfile becomes FROM claude-orca-base:<tag>, plus 'COPY --chown=agent:agent . /opt/claude-orca' and the template phase -- two layers.

acquire_image builds the base first when the daemon does not already hold it, then the folder image. A base that is present is never rebuilt implicitly: only --prebuild (S2) and a pin move rebuild it, because the base is the 15-minute half and nothing should pay it by surprise.

Pins stay in setup.sh; the ARG lines move to Dockerfile.base with them. .dockerignore already excludes .claude-dev, .git and tests/.cache -- the top image's context stays ~2 MB.

title: S2: claude-dev --prebuild, and an update that does not block on the base
description:
A command that builds or refreshes claude-orca-base without a folder waiting on it, so the 15-minute half is paid deliberately rather than by whoever registers next. --update builds the base in the background and leaves the folder on its current image until the new one is ready, so an update never stops the world -- the thing that just went wrong twice.

Reports the base image id before and after, the same way cmd_update_v3 already reports the folder image, so 'it did not move' is a sentence the output can say.

title: Two-image build, and a startup that cannot wall off the agent
description:
Two related changes, one cause. The image is now built on the machine that runs it (commit pending, this session): no CI, no registry, no token. This epic splits that build in two and moves everything project-shaped out of the blocking path.

MEASURED PAYLOAD (read off the live container, 2026-09-08): Orca 529M, Claude Code 206M, opencode 176M, bd 128M, dolt 114M, bats 0.1M -- ~1.15 GB that moves only when a pin moves, sitting under ~2 MB of repo that moves every push.

HONEST CORRECTION to the argument that opened this: the per-push chain is ALREADY short. Dockerfile:35 copies setup.sh on its own line above the six payload RUNs, and the repo copy is the last layer, so editing a script today invalidates only 'COPY . /opt/claude-orca' and the template phase. The split does NOT buy a cheaper push -- the layer order already did. What it buys is a base that can be built deliberately and early (prebuild/warm) instead of only as a side effect of someone's first register, insurance against a cold or pruned cache, and a clean seam if the base is ever worth publishing once a quarter.

THE OTHER HALF, which is the user's original ask and the more important one: scripts/container/entrypoint.sh:230 calls die() when setup.sh fails, which exits before Orca ever starts. A failing step 1 therefore removes the observer -- no Orca, no terminal, no Claude Code, and nothing inside that could report the failure. Features got built on top of a foundation nobody could see was broken. Orca must come up even when provisioning is broken, and the steps must be visible and re-runnable from inside.
close_reason: The half that mattered is delivered and verified: a failed setup no longer removes the observer (dbu.6), the folder-shaped work runs as idempotent provision.d steps after Orca serves (dbu.4), and the agent inside can see and repair its own provisioning with 'provision status/run', a hook that speaks only on failure, and doctor rows on the Mac (dbu.5). The two-image split (dbu.1, dbu.2) stays DEFERRED as standalone beads by the epic's own admission that it buys no cheaper push.

title: Epic: an index-card panel beside Claude Code, written by a small model
description:
A pane next to the Claude Code terminal holding ONE index card -- what is happening, why, what is done, what is next, what is stuck. It never scrolls: the card is replaced, not appended. Opus writes long and buries the point; the card is written by haiku, which is the whole reason the feature exists.

MECHANISM (all of it verified on 2026-09-08 before this was written):
* Orca has no plugin, webview or custom-pane API -- its right sidebar is
  hardcoded (explorer/search/sourceControl/checks/ports) and plugins only
  contribute VM recipes. What it does have is
  'orca terminal split --terminal <handle> --direction vertical --command <cmd>',
  which puts an arbitrary program in a pane of the current tab. That is the panel.
* A terminal knows its own identity from the environment Orca sets:
  ORCA_PANE_KEY is '<tabId>:<leafId>', and leafId matches a row of
  'orca terminal list --json'. So a hook running inside the session can find the
  handle of the terminal it is running in, and split THAT one.
* Claude Code hook payloads carry .transcript_path (confirmed in the binary), and
  the transcript is JSONL of user/assistant entries whose content blocks are
  text / tool_use / thinking. Dropping thinking leaves a compact record of the turn.
* 'claude -p --model claude-haiku-4-5-20251001' answers in ~4s cold, ~47s for a
  6k-character transcript tail. It runs from the Stop hook, backgrounded, so it
  can never make a turn wait.

SHAPE:
  scripts/card.sh (bin/card)  on | off | toggle | status | autostart
  scripts/card-update.sh      Stop hook: transcript tail -> haiku -> run/card.md
  scripts/card-view.sh        runs IN the pane: clear, draw one boxed card, wait
  config/claude-commands/card.md   the /card slash command -- the control
  config/claude-settings.json      SessionStart -> card autostart (background)
                                   Stop         -> card update   (background)
  .claude-dev/run/card.state  on|off, default on   .claude-dev/run/card.pane  handle
                              .claude-dev/run/card.md  the card itself

THE CONTROL: /card toggles, /card on and /card off are explicit. One word to
remember, in the TUI the person is already typing in -- not a shell command that
would mean leaving the session.

EVERY PIECE FAILS OPEN. These run in hooks: no Orca, no jq, no model, no
transcript must each mean 'exit 0, no card', never a session that will not start.
close_reason: Closed

title: startup v4 S2b: supersedes qa2.10 -- the image no longer carries the toolchain, so 'which image' stopped being the same question as 'does this start install anything'; weburl_timeout needs both halves
design:
qa2.10 froze this file when 'which image is it' and 'does this start install anything' were the same question. The image now carries only apt (setup.sh IMAGE_PHASES); the toolchain -- Orca, Claude Code, opencode, bd, dolt, bats -- installs on a folder's first start into <project>/.claude-dev/toolchain, mounted over /usr/local, /opt/Orca and /opt/claude.

So the two questions came apart, in both directions: a PULLED image with an empty cache has ~5 minutes of toolchain to install, and a RUNTIME image reinstalls its apt half on every recreate however full that cache is (dpkg state cannot live in a bind mount). weburl_timeout now asks start_installs_nothing() -- cache populated AND image not runtime -- and only then waits 120s.

Measured on a real Mac (2026-09-07, Docker Desktop 29): keyed on the toolchain cache alone, a runtime-path recreate got 120s for a 280s job and the launcher gave up on a container that was working fine. The corrected case is red against the qa2.10 launcher (pulled + empty cache answers 120, must answer 1800) and green against this one.

Only case 5 changes. The other six are qa2.10's, unedited.

title: Install flow: register hands off to Orca with no prompts (auto beads init, auto-open, warn-not-refuse on availability probes)
description:
Why: the user hit 'Step 1/6: Claude login ... waiting for .credentials.json' at the end of the bootstrap one-liner and called it a needless barrier; the install must be 'run one command, start working'. register currently ends in an interactive 'Walk through setup now? [Y/n]' (default Y) and refuses to hand off on ANY failed self-test probe.

What: (1) register_setup_offer goes away: register never reads /dev/tty; it prints one 'Optional extras: claude-dev setup (...)' pointer line. (2) register runs 'bd init --prefix <derived name>' itself when bd is on PATH and .beads is absent, best-effort, quiet, unless CLAUDE_ORCA_SKIP_BEADS=1 (the test harness sets that globally so the real bd never runs from make_project). (3) After a passing self-test, register prints the run-it block and then opens Orca in the background (cmd_open) when CLAUDE_ORCA_OPEN=1, or when CLAUDE_ORCA_OPEN is unset AND uname -s is Darwin AND stdout is a terminal; CLAUDE_ORCA_OPEN=0 never opens. (4) Self-test refusal is limited to confinement probes: write-outside-denied, read-real-home-denied, keychain-denied, sibling-worktree-denied, tmp-outside-denied, network-blocked-domain, host-files-write-denied, orca-profile-active, git-hooks-audit, and the synthetic srt-launch probe. A FAIL on any other probe prints a one-line warning naming the probe and its detail plus 'claude-dev --doctor', then hands off normally (exit 0). (5) README install section describes the new shape: one command, Orca opens, sign in inside Orca on first run.
design: Decisions: security guarantee unchanged (no hand-off when confinement fails); availability failures (network reachability, srt pin, Orca socket, sandbox-exec presence, home-redirected, orca-data-in-folder, project/worktree writable) degrade to warnings because they do not make the hand-off unsafe. cmd_open gains an optional dir argument so register can call it for $dir. Env knobs: CLAUDE_ORCA_OPEN (1/0/unset), CLAUDE_ORCA_SKIP_BEADS. Existing test in tests/setup-menu.bats that pins the old pointer string is updated in this slice (not frozen). New cases live in a NEW file tests/register-flow.bats so FROZEN does not overlap the setup-menu slice.

title: S5 Auth inside the sandbox: Claude credentials file, masked gh token, git identity, auth-guard
description:

title: S6 Orca integration: managed hooks merge, statusline chain, sub-agent rows, transcript visibility
description:
Why: the point of Orca is seeing what agents do — working/waiting/done dots, sub-agent child rows, session history. Orca implements these through hooks it writes into the real ~/.claude/settings.json, which the sandboxed Claude (own config dir) never loads unless we carry them over.

What: the wrapper (host side, every launch) merges Orca's managed entries — identified by the ~/.orca/agent-hooks/claude-hook.sh command — for SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, Stop, StopFailure, SubagentStart, SubagentStop, TeammateIdle, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, PermissionRequest, PostCompact from ~/.claude/settings.json into <config dir>/settings.json without duplicating ours; removes them when Orca's are gone; chains Orca's claude-statusline.sh before our statusline; allowRead ~/.orca/agent-hooks (already in S2); ORCA_* env passes through untouched; Orca's curl uses --noproxy 127.0.0.1 and allowLocalBinding covers the POST. Transcript visibility: verify on the Mac whether Orca's session history / usage see $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/projects (Orca reads the env of its own process, not the agent's); if not, the wrapper writes a symlink ~/.claude/projects/<slug> → <config dir>/projects/<slug> (host side, outside the sandbox). Registration prints the one-time Settings → Repository worktree base path suggestion (<project>/.orca-worktrees).

Boundaries: no Orca CLI/socket access (S9).

title: claude_orca: port claude_docker to a macOS Seatbelt sandbox managed by Orca
description:
Port the claude_docker template to a macOS-native design: agents run under Apple's Seatbelt (sandbox-exec via Anthropic's pinned `srt` runtime) scoped to the project folder, and Orca (onorca.dev) manages sessions, worktrees, status and sub-agent rows. Keep beads, --dangerously-skip-permissions, /tier, and the hook/guard suite. Claude Code stays primary; Codex/Gemini/OpenCode run inside the same sandbox and take instructions from Claude. Drop the tmux fleet sidebar, worktree-sessions (cs-new/peers/session-title) and all Docker-bound machinery.

Plan with findings, design, risks and slice table: .claude/plans/orca-port.md (this repo). Source material: attachments/claude_docker (old template), Orca 1.4.197 and srt 0.0.75 sources (cloned during planning; refs in the plan).

Trust-boundary invariant every slice must respect: nothing that runs unsandboxed executes or sources anything agent-writable. Host-owned root is ~/.claude-orca (bin, template clone, srt, shellrc); project-owned root is <project>/ (including .claude-dev/{home,tmp,state,sandbox.json}). No ./claude-dev launcher lives in the project root; the launcher is `claude-dev` on PATH.

Verification split: this container is Linux. Each slice's CHECK is Linux-runnable (bats over the shell logic with srt/brew/gh/npm stubbed; schema validation against the pinned srt). Slices with macOS-only behaviour also carry a MAC-CHECK line naming the self-test that bootstrap runs on the Mac and refuses to hand over without; MAC-CHECK is informational for the verifier, never a reason to close.

GitHub: repo name claude_orca (beads prefix is already claude-orca). Creation from this session is blocked — the gh token cannot create repositories (GraphQL createRepository and REST POST /user/repos → 403). When joe-rayment/claude_orca exists: add it as origin and publish main.
close_reason: All slices S1–S12 (+S2b) implemented, independently verified under their acceptance contracts, and merged into main at 3d59e31; ./run-tests.sh 673 ok; bead-auditor held all 13 active closures. Open follow-ups recorded in .claude/plans/orca-port.md §8 (Mac self-test run, gh-token masking default, --prompt-file coverage).

title: S1 Bootstrap & claude-dev launcher for macOS (brew tools, template clone, srt pin, project registration)
description:
Why: the entry point of the whole template — one command run in a project folder must install the host side once and register the project. Replaces bootstrap.sh + claude-dev + Dockerfile/docker-compose from claude_docker.

What: bootstrap.sh (curl|bash via `gh api repos/joe-rayment/claude_orca/contents/bootstrap.sh -H "Accept: application/vnd.github.raw" | bash`), scripts/launcher.sh installed as ~/.claude-orca/bin/claude-dev (commands: register (default, cwd=project), --doctor, --update, --teardown, --uninstall — the last three are S12/S3 stubs here), Brewfile (git gh jq ripgrep node bats-core bd; no helix/tmux), scripts/install-tools.sh (brew bundle check/install, Orca cask presence → prints `brew install --cask stablyai/orca/orca` if missing), scripts/install-srt.sh (`npm --prefix ~/.claude-orca/srt install @anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime@0.0.75`, node >= 20.11 check), template clone into ~/.claude-orca/template, per-project registration: creates <project>/.claude-dev/{home,tmp,state}, sandbox.json defaults, seeds .gitignore (.claude-dev/, .mcp.json, attachments/, .claude/logs/), creates attachments/, prints "open this folder in Orca".

Boundaries: no sandbox logic (S2), no config sync (S4), no self-test (S3). Requires macOS at runtime; on Linux the scripts must still be unit-testable with stubbed brew/gh/npm/git on PATH.
design: Stubs live in tests/helpers/stubs/<tool> and are prepended to PATH by tests/helpers/setup.bash (port of the old helper). Host root ~/.claude-orca is overridable via CLAUDE_ORCA_HOME for tests. Launcher is derived from attachments/claude_docker/claude-dev with all Docker code removed. Template clone URL: https://github.com/joe-rayment/claude_orca.git (main). The launcher must never exec anything under the project folder (trust boundary in the epic).

Router (~/.local/share/claude-dev/ghostty-pane, a COPY): walk up from $PWD (max ~40 levels, stop at /) to the first dir holding .claude-dev/claude-orca.json; if that file contains `"route": false` (grep, no jq -- jq may not exist on a fresh Mac) or <dir>/claude-dev is not executable, fall through; else `exec "<dir>/claude-dev" pane "<dir>"`. Fall-through and every doubt: `exec "${SHELL:-/bin/zsh}" -l`. Nothing else (no docker, no network, ~10 stat calls). CLAUDE_DEV_ROUTER_TRACE=1 prints the decision to stderr (tests).

Install (`claude-dev ghostty`, function ghostty_install; seams CLAUDE_ORCA_GHOSTTY_CONFIG_DIR / HOME for tests):
- Which config Ghostty loads: first existing of ${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/ghostty/config.ghostty, .../ghostty/config, "$HOME/Library/Application Support/com.mitchellh.ghostty/config.ghostty", .../config; none -> create ${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/ghostty/config.ghostty.
- The include file is written BESIDE that config (config-file paths are relative to the including file), with @SHELL_INTEGRATION@ = basename of $SHELL when it is one of zsh bash fish elvish, else `detect`.
- Refuse (exit 1, message naming the line) when the user's config already sets `command =` itself (ignore comments and our own include line): that command is the routing; say how to proceed (remove it, or keep it and skip routing).
- Append exactly one line `config-file = ?claude-dev.ghostty` if it is not already present (add a newline first if the file does not end in one). Record what install did in ~/.local/state/claude-dev/ghostty-install (plain key=value: config=<path>, created=0|1, added_newline=0|1, version=<N>) so uninstall can restore the file byte-for-byte.
- Copy scripts/mac/ghostty-pane to ~/.local/share/claude-dev/ghostty-pane (755).
- Print one line: "Ghostty settings v<N> installed (<config path>) -- new panes use them; reload with cmd+shift+, ".
- --uninstall: remove our line (and the newline we added), delete the config file if we created it and it is now empty, remove the include file, the router and the record. Afterwards the config is byte-identical to before install (the test proves it with cmp).
- Stale check (function ghostty_refresh_if_stale, called at the top of open and the slow path of pane): when the record exists and its version != the template's first-line version, reinstall quietly and print "Ghostty settings updated to v<N> -- new panes use them". When there is no record, do nothing (never install uninvited from open). Must cost ~1 ms: two `head -1`, no Ghostty CLI.
- --check (and two doctor/verify rows "ghostty settings", "ghostty splits"): Ghostty CLI = CLAUDE_ORCA_GHOSTTY_BIN or /Applications/Ghostty.app/Contents/MacOS/ghostty (absent -> row says not installed, informational). `+validate-config` exits 0; `+show-config` has command = our router line, shell-integration = the expected value, window-inherit-working-directory = false; `+list-keybinds` has super+d -> new_split:right and super+shift+d -> new_split:down (Ghostty prints `keybind = super+d=new_split:right` style lines -- accept either the `cmd`/`super` spelling); `+version` >= 1.3; warn when clipboard-write = deny. title: B4 clipboard bridge: ctrl+v pastes Mac images into Claude Code
description: Objective: Claude Code's ctrl+v image paste works in container panes. scripts/mac/clip-listen (nc -lU + one FIFO per connection, socket ~/.local/state/claude-dev/clip-<name>.sock mode 600, started by claude-dev pane, exits with the folder's ssh master via an ssh -O check watchdog) and clip-serve (GET /targets, GET /png via the same osascript PNGf calls native Claude Code uses, «class furl» image files with sips conversion, POST /copy -> pbcopy, text reads always refused, size cap); RemoteForward /tmp/cdev-clip.sock -> that socket; container bin/xclip shim (images only; curl --unix-socket with 3 retries; exit 1 without a socket); "clipboard": false opt-out. Files: scripts/mac/, bin/xclip, scripts/launcher.sh, B2's ssh config. Check: OpenBSD nc + osascript/sips stubs serving fixtures (PNG, file URL, JPEG, refused text), real ssh RemoteForward, real Claude Code ctrl+v -> [Image #1] over ssh on this box; bats; lint-bash32. Plan .claude/plans/ghostty.md § Images.
notes:
SLICE SPEC B4 (claude-orca-9bh.9, orchestrator 2026-10-15) -- the clipboard bridge (images only)
Objective: ctrl+v in Claude Code inside a sandbox pane pastes the Mac clipboard's IMAGE (screenshot, copied image, image file copied in Finder). Text never crosses Mac->container. Plan .claude/plans/ghostty.md § "Images" and the clipboard rows of § "Mac side"/"Container side".
Measured (bd memories ghostty-ssh): Linux Claude Code 2.1.300 pastes images only via `xclip -selection clipboard -t TARGETS -o` then `xclip -selection clipboard -t image/png -o`; a shim first on PATH is enough; no DISPLAY needed. A RemoteForward of a unix socket lands mode 600. The prototype pieces are in ~/.cache/claude-orca-test/{clip-listen,clip-serve,xclip} (read them: ~30 lines each).

Files: new scripts/mac/clip-listen, scripts/mac/clip-serve (bash 3.2, stock macOS tools only: nc, mkfifo, osascript, sips, pbcopy), new scripts/container/xclip + bin/xclip symlink (container side; check bin/ is ahead of /usr/bin on the container PATH -- grep how PATH is built in config/.zshrc / entrypoint and say), scripts/launcher.sh (ssh config RemoteForward line at the spot B2 marked; start/stop of the listener), tests/clipboard-bridge.bats.

Mac side:
- Socket ~/.local/state/claude-dev/clip-<name>.sock (dir 700), pid file clip-<name>.pid, log clip-<name>.log.
- clip-listen <sock> <ssh-cfg> <host>: loop { rm -f sock fifo; mkfifo -m 600 fifo; nc -lU sock <fifo | clip-serve >fifo }, umask 077 so the socket is 600; a watchdog subshell runs `ssh -F <cfg> -O check <host>` every 60 s (CLAUDE_ORCA_CLIP_WATCH_S) and on failure kills the loop, removes sock/fifo/pid, exits. Single instance per folder: launcher starts it only when the pid file's pid is not alive; started detached (nohup, setsid when present -- macOS has no setsid; use `( ... ) &` + disown) from `claude-dev pane` on BOTH paths (fast path cost: one `kill -0`).

    GET /targets -> 200 "image/png\n" when the clipboard holds an image (osascript `clipboard info` lists «class PNGf» or «class TIFF», or «class furl» whose POSIX path has extension png/jpg/jpeg/gif/webp/heic/heif/tif/tiff/bmp), else 204 with no body.

title: B2 launcher speaks ssh: keys, claude-dev pane, sshd.ready
description: Objective: the Mac side reaches the container over ssh. Generate client + host keypairs and known_hosts into .claude-dev/state/ssh/ (no TOFU, nothing in ~/.ssh); write state/ssh/config (ControlMaster auto, ControlPersist 30m, ControlPath ~/.local/state/claude-dev/cm-%C, SetEnv TERM_PROGRAM/TERM_PROGRAM_VERSION/COLORTERM, RemoteForward for the clipboard); claude-dev pane (fast path ssh -O check -> exec ssh -tt -o SetEnv=CDEV_CWD=<rel>; slow path starts Docker/container, waits run/sshd.ready, pushes terminfo once via infocmp|tic; on failure banner 'Mac shell - NOT sandboxed' + Mac shell, logged to run/pane.log); ./claude-dev with no args execs ssh in the current terminal; doctor/verify rows (sshd answers, key auth, router installed). Files: scripts/launcher.sh, bootstrap.sh (bash 3.2). Check: launcher bats with the docker stub; the real launcher against CLAUDE_ORCA_RUNTIME=local (bash launcher -> booted entrypoint -> sshd -> pane) on this box; lint-bash32. Commit subject says UNVERIFIED on a Mac (CLAUDE.md definition of done). Plan .claude/plans/ghostty.md § Mac side.
notes:
SLICE SPEC B2 (claude-orca-9bh.7, orchestrator 2026-10-15) -- the launcher speaks ssh
Objective: `./claude-dev` (no args / open) starts or adopts the folder's container exactly as today, then -- instead of waiting for Orca's web URL and handing off to the Orca app -- waits for sshd and turns the CURRENT terminal into a sandbox pane (`exec ssh`). New `claude-dev pane` does the same with a fast path for splits. Orca still runs inside the container until C1, but the Mac no longer uses it; the dead Orca hand-off code is deleted later by C2 (leave it in place, just stop calling it from open).
Container side already provides (slice B1): sshd on CLAUDE_ORCA_SSHD_PORT (default 2222) inside the container, AuthorizedKeysFile <project>/.claude-dev/state/ssh/authorized_keys, host key read from state/ssh/host_ed25519, run/sshd.ready (`port=N`, `host_key_sha256=SHA256:...`), ForceCommand pane-entry which honours SetEnv CDEV_CWD (relative path) and runs SSH_ORIGINAL_COMMAND under a login shell.

Design (all bash 3.2, stock macOS tools: ssh, ssh-keygen, infocmp; scripts/launcher.sh unless noted):
1. Keys (function ssh_ensure_keys <dir>): <dir>/.claude-dev/state/ssh/ (700) holds client_ed25519(+.pub), host_ed25519(+.pub), authorized_keys, known_hosts, config. Generate missing keys with `ssh-keygen -q -t ed25519 -N '' -C claude-dev-<name>-{client,host} -f ...`. authorized_keys = `restrict,pty,port-forwarding <client pub>` (restrict = no agent/X11/tcp forwarding; pty + port-forwarding re-enable what a pane and B4's unix-socket RemoteForward need; sshd_config still denies TCP forwarding). known_hosts = `claude-dev-<name> <host pub key type+blob>` (HostKeyAlias, so no TOFU). Rewrite authorized_keys/known_hosts from the keys every time (cheap, self-healing). Never touch ~/.ssh. Keys are made BEFORE container create/start so sshd finds them at boot.
2. ssh config (function ssh_write_config <dir> <port>): state/ssh/config, regenerated each open:
     Host claude-dev-<name>
       HostName 127.0.0.1
       Port <port>
       User agent
       IdentityFile "<dir>/.claude-dev/state/ssh/client_ed25519"
       IdentitiesOnly yes
       UserKnownHostsFile "<dir>/.claude-dev/state/ssh/known_hosts"
       HostKeyAlias claude-dev-<name>
       StrictHostKeyChecking yes
       ControlMaster auto
       ControlPath ~/.local/state/claude-dev/cm-%C
       ControlPersist 30m
       ServerAliveInterval 30
       ForwardAgent no
       ForwardX11 no
       LogLevel ERROR
   (quote paths: the folder may contain spaces; mkdir -p ~/.local/state/claude-dev 700). B4 later adds a RemoteForward line -- leave a clearly marked spot.
3. The container: pass `-e CLAUDE_ORCA_SSHD_PORT=<port>` and keep publishing `127.0.0.1:<port>:<port>`; move Orca off that port inside the container (`ORCA_PORT=<port+1>`, NOT published; C1 removes it). In the local runtime (CTR_RUNTIME=local) the same env reaches the entrypoint, so sshd listens on <port> on this host. An existing container created without CLAUDE_ORCA_SSHD_PORT in its env (docker inspect .Config.Env) counts as not matching (container_matches) and is recreated -- that is the migration for old folders. Bump the IMAGE_TAG file's value (read how image_tag uses it) so a plain ./claude-dev builds the image that carries openssh-server instead of reusing the old one.
4. wait_for_sshd_ready <dir> <name>: same shape and return codes as wait_for_web_url (0 ready, 1 timeout, 2 container died) polling run/sshd.ready; then verify its host_key_sha256 equals `ssh-keygen -lf state/ssh/host_ed25519.pub` (mismatch = error naming both). Timeout from the existing weburl_timeout logic.

title: A1 worker runtime without Orca: dispatch / worker-run / workers
description: Objective: Orca-free headless workers. dispatch <bead> composes the spec (orch_spec, moved to scripts/lib/workers.sh), cuts ~/worktrees/<bead> on branch work/<bead> (or --worktree main), installs the frozen hook, writes run/workers/<job>/, starts worker-run detached (setsid nohup) and prints the receipt. worker-run takes a flock slot (maxWorkers from claude-orca.json, default 3; extra jobs queue), runs opencode run / claude -p under nice 10, writes log+receipt, appends the bead note and ONE inbox.jsonl line under flock (replaces the Orca mailbox and the --spool process). workers: list | wait [--until] | reply <job> <text> (resumes the same session: claude -p --resume / opencode run -s) | tail <job> | stop <job>. Stall watch ported from orca-wait. Files: scripts/{dispatch,worker-run,workers}.sh, scripts/lib/workers.sh, bin/ links. Check: real opencode run against the stub provider (openai-stub-real.bats pattern) and one real claude -p haiku run in a throwaway repo, both landing in inbox + bead notes; 4 dispatches at maxWorkers=2 show 2 running / 2 queued; bats per behaviour. Boundaries: old orca-* scripts stay until C1; no Orca calls. Plan .claude/plans/ghostty.md § Workers and /tier.
notes:
SLICE SPEC (orchestrator, 2026-10-15)
Objective: Orca-free headless workers -- three commands that replace orca-dispatch / orca-worker-run / orca-wait / orca-reply / orca-workers without calling Orca at all. The old orca-* scripts stay untouched and working (C1 deletes them).

Files (new unless noted): scripts/lib/workers.sh, scripts/dispatch.sh, scripts/worker-run.sh, scripts/workers.sh, bin/dispatch, bin/worker-run, bin/workers (relative symlinks ../scripts/X.sh like the existing bin/ entries), tests/workers-dispatch.bats, tests/workers-run.bats, tests/workers-cli.bats. scripts/lib/orca-orch.sh (existing): MOVE orch_root, orch_bead_json, orch_spec (and what they need, e.g. orch_last_handoff, orch_note_bead) into lib/workers.sh and make orca-orch.sh source lib/workers.sh so every old caller keeps working unchanged.

Design (plan .claude/plans/ghostty.md § "Workers and /tier, without Orca"):
1. `dispatch <bead> [--worker|--checker] [--agent claude|opencode] [--model M] [--variant V] [--effort E] [--worktree new|main|path:<dir>] [--prompt-file F]`
   - agent/model/variant come from tier.json via scripts/lib/tier-roles.sh when not given (tier_role_field); an openrouter/* or openai/* model means agent opencode (same rule as orca-dispatch). Do NOT change tier files (slice A2); only read them.
   - Spec = orch_spec of `bd show` (the same text orca-dispatch composes today, WORKER RULES included).
   - Worktree default `new`: a git worktree at WT_DIR/<bead> on a new branch work/<bead> cut from main, WT_DIR = ${CLAUDE_ORCA_WORKTREES_DIR:-$HOME/worktrees}. If that branch/dir already exists, reuse it (re-dispatch of the same bead) rather than fail. `main` = the project root itself. Install the frozen hook (scripts/lib/frozen-hook.sh install_frozen_hook + frozen_hook_env) exactly as orca-dispatch does.
   - Job id `<bead>-<epoch>-<4hex>`; job dir `<root>/.claude-dev/run/workers/<job>/` holding spec.md, job.json {job,bead,role,agent,model,variant,effort,dir,branch,state,created}, later pid, log.jsonl, receipt.json.
   - Starts `worker-run <job-dir>` detached (setsid nohup, stdin </dev/null, its own stderr log) and prints ONE line of receipt JSON on stdout at once (job, bead, agent, model, dir, branch, state). Human notes on stderr. Exit 0 started, 2 usage/bead error.
2. `worker-run <job-dir> [--resume <session-id> --message <text>]`
   - Slot cap: maxWorkers = env CLAUDE_ORCA_MAX_WORKERS, else `.maxWorkers` from <root>/.claude-dev/claude-orca.json (jq, read as data), else 3. Slots are lock files run/workers/slots/<i>.lock taken with `flock -n` on an fd held for the life of the run; with none free, job.json state=queued and it retries every ~1 s (CLAUDE_ORCA_SLOT_POLL_S) until one frees.
   - state=running, pid recorded, then runs under `nice -n 10` in the worktree:
       opencode: `opencode run -m <model> [--variant V] --format json` with the spec as the message; the provider env comes from the guard exactly as orca-worker-run/orca-dispatch build it today (guard token from run/openrouter-guard.token as OPENROUTER_API_KEY, OPENROUTER_BASE_URL at the guard) -- read scripts/orca-worker-run.sh, scripts/orca-dispatch.sh and scripts/lib/opencode-launch.sh and reuse; never the real key.
       claude: `claude -p --model <m> [--effort E only if this claude supports it -- check claude --help] --output-format stream-json --verbose --permission-mode bypassPermissions`, spec on stdin (unset CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION for the child if it is set).
     Test seam CLAUDE_ORCA_WORKER_CMD: a command run instead of opencode/claude, with the same args + env, so bats can use a stub runner.
   - Captures the session id (claude stream-json `session_id`; opencode json `sessionID`) into job.json so a reply can resume it.
   - Writes log.jsonl (raw stream), receipt.json (job, bead, agent, model, exit, started, ended, wall_s, tokens/usd when the stream reports them, session_id, summary = last assistant text truncated to ~2000 chars), appends a short note to the bead (`bd update <bead> --append-notes`, best effort, same shape orca-worker-run writes), and appends ONE line to <root>/.claude-dev/run/orchestration/inbox.jsonl under `flock` on inbox.lock. The line keeps the schema today's inbox readers parse (read scripts/orca-wait.sh: the fields of a worker_done line and how emit_unread prints them) plus job/bead/receipt; type `worker_done`, or `question` when the final text has a line starting `QUESTION:`, or `worker_failed` on a non-zero exit.
   - Releases the slot; state=done|question|failed. Exit = the runner's exit code (2 for usage/env errors).
   - --resume: one more headless turn in the same worktree on the same session (`claude -p --resume <sid>` / `opencode run -s <sid>`), same slot/receipt/inbox handling, receipts numbered (receipt-2.json, ...).
3. `workers [list] | wait [--until <s>] | reply <job> "<text>" | tail <job> | stop <job>`
   - list: one row per job dir, newest first: job, bead, agent:model, state, pid alive?, elapsed, last event; header `workers R/MAX running · Q queued`.
   - wait: orca-wait's bare-read and --until behaviour (same inbox.jsonl and the SAME inbox.cursor, so the hooks/statusline that read it keep working; exit 4 on silence like orca-wait --until). Port orca-wait's stall watch (a running job whose log has not grown in CLAUDE_ORCA_STALL_S prints one STALL line, once per job) with no Orca call.
   - reply: starts `worker-run <job-dir> --resume <sid> --message <text>` detached; error if no session id.
   - tail: readable live view of log.jsonl (tool calls and assistant text as plain lines), following until the job ends; `--raw` prints the jsonl.
   - stop: kill the job's process group, state=stopped, release the slot, one inbox line type worker_stopped.
   All bash 3.2 clean, jq for JSON.

How it is checked (do all, report each result):
- bats with the stub runner seam: dispatch creates worktree+branch+job dir and prints a receipt; worker-run writes receipt/inbox line/bead note (a stub bd first on PATH is fine for the note); QUESTION: becomes type question; reply resumes with the recorded session id; stop kills; FOUR dispatches with maxWorkers=2 and a sleeping stub show exactly 2 running + 2 queued in `workers list`, then all 4 done; inbox appends from parallel runs never interleave (each line valid JSON).
- REAL runs in a throwaway git repo in a scratch dir (a script you run once is fine, not bats): (a) one real `claude -p` on haiku with a trivial spec ("create hello.txt containing hi and commit it") -- the worktree gets the commit, receipt + inbox line land; (b) one real `opencode run` against the stub OpenAI-compatible provider tests/openai-stub-real.bats stands up (read it for how) -- receipt + inbox line land. Report the commands and the receipt lines.
- scripts/lint-bash32.sh on the new scripts.

title: Residency rule restated as a country allowlist: rebuild the image so a running folder gets it
description:

The guard loads the policy next to its OWN script -- /opt/claude-orca/config/provider-policy.json, the copy baked into the image -- never from the project tree, because the project tree is agent-writable. title: /tier presets: one name for a top/worker/recon combination, a bare /tier that offers them like /model, the current binding shipped as 'hybrid'
description:
User request 2026-09-19: "For the /tier behaviour, I'd like to add presets for combination. I'd like the behaviour to be basically like /model behaviour. I'd like our current settings to be one of the presets." Current settings = /tier fable glm-flash luna@high.

DESIGN (orchestrator; do not redesign):
A preset is ONE NAME for an existing /tier argument form, so every parsing, validation, pin and effort rule in scripts/tier-set.sh is reused unchanged. /model's behaviour is: bare -> a picker of the choices with the current one marked; '<name>' -> switch directly and say so. /tier gets the same two halves.

1. config/tier-presets.json (new; data, read with jq, never sourced), found the way ROUTES_FILE is (tier-set.sh ~line 98-104): PRESETS_FILE="${TIER_PRESETS_FILE:-<root>/config/tier-presets.json}". Shape and shipped content, in this order:
   {"presets":[
    {"name":"hybrid","summary":"Fable orchestrates, GLM 5.3 flash works, GPT-5.6 Luna (high) scouts -- low-cost OpenRouter workers","args":["fable","glm-flash","luna@high"]},
    {"name":"hybrid-glm","summary":"as hybrid, with full-size GLM 5.3 workers for slices flash flounders on","args":["fable","glm","luna@high"]},
    {"name":"opus-hybrid","summary":"Opus orchestrates over the same low-cost OpenRouter workers","args":["opus","glm-flash","luna@high"]},
    {"name":"all-claude","summary":"no OpenRouter: Fable, with the Claude worker and recon it derives","args":["fable"]}
   ]}
   At most 4 presets are ever offered in the picker (the AskUserQuestion tool takes 2-4 options); the listing shows all.
2. scripts/tier-set.sh:
   a. '/tier <name>' -- exactly one argument that is a preset name and NOT a reserved word (show help overdrive auth models checker worker recon, the Claude aliases fable opus sonnet haiku in any case, any route name in ROUTES_FILE; reserved words always win): re-run this same script with the preset's args (so the unchanged path does the binding), and only if that exits 0 stamp the name into the state file with jq ('.preset = $n', tmp file + mv like the other writers), then print one line 'preset <name> -- <summary>' followed by the child's own output. write_state/write_state_v3 build the state with 'jq -n', so ANY later non-preset bind drops .preset by construction -- do not add code for that, test it.
   b. bare '/tier' and '/tier show': after the existing state lines and BEFORE show_guide, a section
        presets -- /tier <name>:
          * hybrid        fable glm-flash luna@high   <summary>   (current)
            hybrid-glm    fable glm luna@high         <summary>
      '*' and '(current)' mark the preset named in the state's .preset; none is marked when .preset is absent. A missing or invalid presets file prints nothing here and never fails the command.
   c. bare '/tier' ONLY (not 'show'), and only when stdout is NOT a terminal ([ -t 1 ] is false -- that is how the slash command and bats both run it): end the output with
        [tier-picker]
        current: <name or none>
        option: <name> -- <summary>
        ... (the current preset first when there is one, then file order, at most 4)
        [/tier-picker]
   d. show_guide gains ONE line for the preset form, e.g. '  /tier hybrid                          a preset -- one name for a whole combination; bare /tier lists them'. Keep every existing guide line byte-identical.
3. config/claude-commands/tier.md: description mentions presets and that a bare /tier offers them; argument-hint gains 'hybrid' first; allowed-tools becomes 'Bash(tier-set:*), AskUserQuestion'; model/effort unchanged; the body keeps the '!`tier-set "$ARGUMENTS"`' line first and then says, in this order: (i) if the output ends with a [tier-picker] block, call AskUserQuestion ONCE -- question 'Which tier preset?', header 'Tier', one option per 'option:' line in that order (label = the name, plus ' (current)' on the current one; description = the summary) -- then run 'tier-set <chosen name>' (for the free-text 'Other' answer: 'tier-set <the text as typed>') and print THAT output verbatim and nothing else; if the question is dismissed, print the output above without the [tier-picker] block; (ii) otherwise the existing verbatim-passthrough sentence, unchanged.
4. tests/tier-presets.bats (new). Model the fixture on tests/tier-phrases.bats (TIER_STATE_FILE / TIER_ROUTES_FILE style env overrides, a throwaway state file; unset ambient PROJECT_DIR, CLAUDE_ORCA_ROOT, BEADS_DIR; never touch /workspace/claude-orca/.claude-dev/run/tier.json). Cases:
   1 '/tier hybrid binds exactly what /tier fable glm-flash luna@high binds': the two state files are equal once .updated and .preset are deleted; .preset == "hybrid"; output's first line starts 'preset hybrid'.
   2 'any other bind drops the preset': after hybrid, 'tier-set opus' leaves no .preset key.
   3 'a one-word preset binds the derived ladder': all-claude -> top fable, worker sonnet, recon haiku, pinned false, .preset all-claude.
   4 'bare /tier lists every preset, marks the current one, and ends with the picker block': after hybrid; '(current)' on the hybrid line only; the block has 'current: hybrid', hybrid as the first option, <= 4 option lines, and is the END of the output. With no .preset: 'current: none' and no '(current)'.
   5 '/tier show lists the presets but prints no picker block'.
   6 'reserved words win': with a TIER_PRESETS_FILE that names a preset 'opus' (args ["haiku"]), 'tier-set opus' still binds top=opus and stamps no .preset.
   7 'the shipped presets file is sound': 1-4 presets; names match ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$, unique, none reserved, none a route name in config/delegate-routes.json; every args is an array of 1-3 non-empty strings; every summary non-empty.
   8 'a missing presets file changes nothing': TIER_PRESETS_FILE=/nonexistent -> bare output has no presets section, no picker block, exit 0; 'tier-set hybrid' behaves exactly as an unknown single word does today (capture that behaviour BEFORE you change the script and assert it).
   9 'the command file wires the picker': config/claude-commands/tier.md's allowed-tools holds both 'Bash(tier-set:*)' and 'AskUserQuestion'; its first body line is the tier-set line; the body names '[tier-picker]' and 'AskUserQuestion'; 'model: haiku' is still there.

title: 75-orca-skills leaves three untracked paths in the user's project root (.agents/skills/, .claude/skills/, skills-lock.json)
description:
Observed 2026-09-19 in /workspace/claude-orca: 'orca skills install --skill orchestration --local' (provision.d/75-orca-skills, claude-orca-ndy) writes .agents/skills/orchestration/SKILL.md, the symlink .claude/skills/orchestration -> ../../.agents/skills/orchestration, and skills-lock.json into the PROJECT root. None is gitignored, so every bootstrapped folder gains three untracked paths in the user's own repo on first start.

DECISION (orchestrator, 2026-09-19, on recon evidence): the seeded .gitignore carries the three exact paths.
- Rejected, install into the sandboxed home: 'orca skills install' has only --local and the global default; a global install lands in ~/.agents/skills plus a ~/.claude/skills symlink, and scripts/config-sync.sh:190 rm -rf's ~/.claude/skills on every sync, so Claude Code would lose the skill after each config change; four closed contracts also freeze --local in tests/provision-orca-skills.bats.
- Rejected, commit them: the template cannot commit into the user's repo, and the three paths are the sandbox's own artifacts -- the same class as orca.yaml, .orca/, .mcp.json and attachments/, which seed_gitignore already carries.
- The ignore is EXACT (.claude/skills/orchestration, never .claude/skills/): a user's own project skills must stay visible to git.
- Non-goal: teardown does not delete the three paths, just as it leaves orca.yaml and attachments/ behind; it only un-seeds the lines.

TWO lists mirror each other and both change: seed_gitignore's for-loop in scripts/container/seed-project.sh (~line 72) and the seeded() function inside gitignore_unseed's awk in scripts/launcher.sh (~line 195), which is what './claude-dev --teardown' uses to remove exactly what the seed wrote. scripts/launcher.sh runs on macOS bash 3.2.57: no associative arrays, no mapfile, no ${x^^}, no += onto an empty array under set -u.

Do, in one slice (Write/Edit in pieces of at most 150 lines, one file per response, report under 60 lines):
(A) tests/seed-gitignore-orca-skills.bats (new). Model the fixture on tests/seed-project.bats case 1 (line ~28: how scripts/container/seed-project.sh is run against a throwaway PROJECT_DIR) and on tests/lifecycle.bats case 1 (line ~17: how the real --teardown is driven with stubs).   case 2 "a folder seeded before this change gains exactly the three missing lines": start from a .gitignore holding a user line 'node_modules/', then the '# claude_orca' marker and the twelve patterns the seed writes today; run the seed; the three lines are present once each, 'node_modules/' is still there, and a second seed run leaves the file byte-identical (cmp).

  case 4 "teardown un-seeds what the seed wrote, byte for byte": a folder whose .gitignore is exactly 'node_modules/' is seeded by the real seed-project.sh, then torn down by the real --teardown; its .gitignore is byte-identical to the original again.

(C) scripts/launcher.sh: the same three strings join seeded() in gitignore_unseed.

title: orca-wait redesign (redo of claude-orca-n3e): detached spooler + cheap reader + --until; the orchestrator never runs the poll loop in its own turns
description:
Observed over one live session (2026-09-17, ~8h, 9 dispatches): the orchestrator called orca-wait ~20 times. Each call is a blocking Bash tool call: in the foreground it is capped at 10 minutes by the harness and burns a turn per timeout (workers take 20-60 min); in the background it was killed twice by the harness's low-memory guard and once ended early by the stall watch's fallback (fixed in claude-orca-20o). The mailbox, receipts, bead notes, release/close and stall watch are all sound; the flaw is WHO runs the loop -- the orchestrator, in its own context, as a poll.

Design: split orca-wait into a detached spooler and a cheap reader.
1. `orca-wait --spool` (started once per Run by orca-dispatch if not running; pid file under run/orchestration/) runs the existing loop forever, detached with nohup/setsid, and appends every receipt line (worker_done, question, escalation, stalled, timeout-free) to run/orchestration/inbox.jsonl, doing the release/close/bead-note/stall work itself. It exits when no record in dispatch/ is live for N minutes.
2. `orca-wait` (no flag) returns immediately: prints and consumes unread inbox lines (cursor in run/orchestration/inbox.cursor). `orca-wait --until <n>` blocks up to n seconds only until the inbox grows, via a cheap inotify/poll on the file, not on Orca.
3. The orchestrator waits with the harness's own primitive: the Monitor tool (an until-loop on `test -s inbox.jsonl` past the cursor) or a background `orca-wait --until 3600`, so a worker message wakes the orchestrator through a task notification with no turn spent polling and nothing 1 GB-sized to be memory-killed.
4. Questions still print reply_with: orca-reply <msg_id> -- unchanged.
Contract when picked up: bats with a stub orca -- spooler appends a worker_done receipt and marks the record done while no reader runs; reader prints unread lines once and nothing the second time; --until returns within 1s of a new line and after n seconds otherwise; spooler exits when all records are done; orca-wait.bats/-records/-retained stay green.

The assertions stand; only the stub answers for orchestration-task-create / orchestration-run-create are missing. The redo commits a corrected test as a NEW RED-AT under this bead, then GREEN. title: orca-wait redesign: the orchestrator should not run the mailbox poll loop in its own turns
description:
Observed over one live session (2026-09-17, ~8h, 9 dispatches): the orchestrator called orca-wait ~20 times. Each call is a blocking Bash tool call: in the foreground it is capped at 10 minutes by the harness and burns a turn per timeout (workers take 20-60 min); in the background it was killed twice by the harness's low-memory guard and once ended early by the stall watch's fallback (fixed in claude-orca-20o). The mailbox, receipts, bead notes, release/close and stall watch are all sound; the flaw is WHO runs the loop -- the orchestrator, in its own context, as a poll.

Design: split orca-wait into a detached spooler and a cheap reader.
1. `orca-wait --spool` (started once per Run by orca-dispatch if not running; pid file under run/orchestration/) runs the existing loop forever, detached with nohup/setsid, and appends every receipt line (worker_done, question, escalation, stalled, timeout-free) to run/orchestration/inbox.jsonl, doing the release/close/bead-note/stall work itself. It exits when no record in dispatch/ is live for N minutes.
2. `orca-wait` (no flag) returns immediately: prints and consumes unread inbox lines (cursor in run/orchestration/inbox.cursor). `orca-wait --until <n>` blocks up to n seconds only until the inbox grows, via a cheap inotify/poll on the file, not on Orca.
3. The orchestrator waits with the harness's own primitive: the Monitor tool (an until-loop on `test -s inbox.jsonl` past the cursor) or a background `orca-wait --until 3600`, so a worker message wakes the orchestrator through a task notification with no turn spent polling and nothing 1 GB-sized to be memory-killed.
4. Questions still print reply_with: orca-reply <msg_id> -- unchanged.
Contract when picked up: bats with a stub orca -- spooler appends a worker_done receipt and marks the record done while no reader runs; reader prints unread lines once and nothing the second time; --until returns within 1s of a new line and after n seconds otherwise; spooler exits when all records are done; orca-wait.bats/-records/-retained stay green.

title: Orca-launched Claude workers die on the 'Bypass Permissions mode' acceptance dialog (worker-start state=failed)
description:
Seen 2026-09-17 02:29-02:40: five orca-dispatch --agent claude --model sonnet launches (beads claude-orca-gh9, claude-orca-m57) came back state=failed. The terminal shows `claude '--dangerously-skip-permissions' '--model' 'sonnet'` stopped on "WARNING: Claude Code running in Bypass Permissions mode ... ❯ No, exit / Yes, I accept" and then the shell prompt: the dialog defaults to exit and Orca's worker-start sees the process die. The same launch worked at 23:26 the previous evening (ctx_41f201d7a2fe, ctx_901477575758). Setting .bypassPermissionsModeAccepted=true in /home/agent/.claude.json did NOT help (it was null before; still fails after), so either the worker runs with a different HOME/config dir or the acceptance lives under another key in this Claude Code version.
To do: find where Claude Code 2.x records the acceptance (grep the installed claude bundle for 'bypassPermissionsModeAccepted' / 'Bypass Permissions' and the settings key it reads; check what HOME and CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR Orca's worker-start gives the terminal, e.g. via `orca terminal create --command 'env | grep -E \"HOME|CLAUDE\"'`), seed it at provision time (scripts/container/provision.d/, the step that seeds the agent home) so a fresh folder never shows the dialog to a worker, and add a bats case. Until then Sonnet slices go through the Agent tool (which is what happened here).
notes:
Root cause: Claude Code 2.1.271 migrated ~/.claude.json's bypassPermissionsModeAccepted into settings.json's skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt (userSettings/localSettings/flagSettings/policySettings), deleting the old key once migrated (grep -o '.{80}bypassPermissionsModeAccepted.{80}' on the installed bundle shows migration fn 'yi'). provision.d/30-claude-first-run already seeds the new key once, but config-sync.sh's settings.json rewrite is a wholesale overwrite from the template and runs again independently later (host resync / /config-resync) without 30 re-running after it, so the seeded key gets wiped and the interactive Bypass Permissions dialog reappears -- matching the incident timeline (worked at 23:26, failed 02:29-02:40 after an intervening resync).

Repo fix (branch joe-rayment/wt-bypass-accept, commit 7960a77): config/claude-settings.json now ships skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt: true so every config-sync rewrite carries it, not just the first; settings.local.json still overrides. Added a bats case to tests/config-sync.bats proving the key survives a forced second sync and that a local override still wins (RED: null after first sync pre-fix; GREEN: true after first AND forced second sync post-fix, false with a local override). ./run-tests.sh: 58 files, 4 pre-existing not-ok unrelated to this change (opencode config sync test, start-professor cwd test, statusline legacy-fixture test, opencode-dispatch guard-token test) -- reproduce identically without this diff.

LIVE change in this container (not just the worktree): added "skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt": true to /home/agent/.claude/settings.json directly, so orca-dispatch --agent claude works now without waiting for a fresh provision run. Reproduced before/after via orca terminal create: before the live edit, 'claude --dangerously-skip-permissions --model sonnet' (interactive, no -p) stopped on the WARNING/Bypass Permissions dialog defaulting to 'No, exit'; after the edit, the same command landed straight in the REPL and answered a prompt (Crunched for 1s, turn completed) with no dialog.

title: OpenRouter guard: an upstream 429 is passed straight to the worker, which sits idle on it forever
description:
OBJECTIVE
Seen 2026-09-17 on the recon role (openrouter/openai/gpt-5.6-luna @high via opencode in an orca-dispatch terminal): OpenRouter answered {"code":429,"message":"openai/gpt-5.6-luna is temporarily rate-limited upstream. Please retry shortly ..."} and the opencode TUI printed it and stopped; no retry, no worker_done, no escalation, 20 minutes of silence until the orchestrator nudged it by hand. The guard (scripts/container/openrouter-guard.py, policy in config/provider-policy.json) is the one place every request passes through, so it is where a transient 429 should be absorbed.

FILES (yours): scripts/container/openrouter-guard.py, its tests (find them: grep -l openrouter-guard tests/*.bats tests/**/*.py; add cases to a NEW file tests/openrouter-guard-retry.bats or a new python test next to the existing guard tests -- match whatever the existing guard tests use; the new file is FROZEN after RED). Do not touch scripts/lib/orca-orch.sh, scripts/orca-wait.sh, scripts/delegate.sh.

SPEC
1. On an upstream HTTP 429 (and 502/503/529), the guard retries the same request up to GUARD_RETRY_MAX times (default 4) with exponential backoff starting at GUARD_RETRY_BASE_S (default 2s: 2,4,8,16), honouring an upstream Retry-After header when present (capped at 30s). Streaming requests are retried only if no byte of the body has been forwarded yet.
2. Every retry is one log line on the guard's JSON log: {"retry": n, "status": 429, "model": ..., "sleep_s": ...}; the final failure is logged with "retries_exhausted": true and passed through with the upstream status and body unchanged.
3. Env overrides: OPENROUTER_GUARD_RETRY_MAX=0 disables retries (tests for pass-through use this).

CONTRACT

PASS-IF: plan 1..N with N>=4 (or pytest: N passed, 0 failed), no failures. Cases against a local stub upstream (an http.server in the test on 127.0.0.1): (1) stub answers 429 twice then 200 -> the client gets 200 and the guard log has two retry lines; (2) stub answers 429 always with GUARD_RETRY_MAX=2 -> client gets 429, log has retries_exhausted; (3) Retry-After: 1 is honoured (sleep_s == 1 in the log); (4) OPENROUTER_GUARD_RETRY_MAX=0 -> a single 429 is passed straight through, no retry line; (5) existing guard tests stay green.

title: orca-wait: a finished dispatch stays 'ready' in its record, so the stall watch nudges dead workers and ends a live wait
description:
OBJECTIVE
Seen 2026-09-17: orca-wait, waiting on a LIVE recon dispatch (ctx_2c2eecfc6de4), printed "ctx_41f201d7a2fe (claude-orca-2j2) is still quiet 7538s after its nudge -- falling back to an in-process executor" and exited 0 -- for a dispatch whose worker_done had been ingested and whose terminal had been released two hours earlier (bead closed). Cause: process_batch (scripts/orca-wait.sh) on worker_done notes the bead and calls worker-release, but never updates the dispatch RECORD (.claude-dev/run/orchestration/dispatch/<id>.json, written by orca-dispatch, shape in scripts/lib/orca-orch.sh header), so state stays "ready"; stall_scan scans every record in ready/running/dispatched, nudges the dead terminal, and on the next pass returns 3, which ends the whole wait. Records from Sep 12 and Sep 16 are still "ready" today.

FILES (yours): scripts/orca-wait.sh, tests/orca-wait-records.bats (NEW, FROZEN after RED). Read tests/orca-wait.bats first for the stub-orca and fixture pattern and reuse it. Do not touch scripts/orca-dispatch.sh, scripts/lib/orca-orch.sh or tests/orca-wait.bats.

SPEC
1. On worker_done (and on the release it performs), process_batch writes the record: .state = "done", .outcome = <outcome or "unknown">, .finished_at = <epoch>, .released = true|false (true when worker-release succeeded). On question/escalation the record is only touched (rec_touch), as today.
2. stall_scan skips any record whose state is not ready/running/dispatched (already so) AND any record whose bead is closed: `bd show <bead> --json` status closed (use orch_bead_json if it exposes status; else jq on its output) -> mark that record .state = "done" .finished_at = now with a note "<disp> (<bead>): bead is closed -- marking the dispatch done" and continue. A failed bd lookup leaves the record alone.
3. The nudged-again fallback (return 3) must not end a wait when another dispatch in the same run is still live: instead of `return 3`, mark that record .state = "stalled" (so it is scanned no more), print the same {"type":"stalled",...,"fallback":...} line, and return 3 ONLY if no other record in $DISP_DIR is in ready/running/dispatched state; otherwise return 0 and keep waiting.
4. A `--keep` wait (no release) still marks the record done with released=false.

CONTRACT
CHECK: bats tests/orca-wait-records.bats
PASS-IF: plan 1..N with N>=5, no 'not ok'. Cases: (1) a stub `orca` that answers one worker_done for dispatch X: after orca-wait, X's record has state "done", outcome from the payload, finished_at > 0, released true; (2) same with --keep: state "done", released false; (3) a record for dispatch Y with state "ready", nudged_at set, activity 2h old, while a record Z is "ready" and fresh: orca-wait with --stall-after 60 and a stub whose check --wait returns count 0 prints one stalled line with fallback for Y, sets Y's state to "stalled", and does NOT exit until its --timeout-ms (assert it printed the {"type":"timeout"} line and Z is still "ready"); (4) the same Y alone (no Z): orca-wait exits after the fallback line without the timeout line (today's behaviour, kept); (5) a record whose bead the stub `bd` reports closed: never nudged (stub orca records no `terminal send`), record marked done with a note; (6) existing `bats tests/orca-wait.bats` stays green.
FROZEN: tests/orca-wait-records.bats from RED-AT on.
CLASS: bugfix.

PROCESS: commit the test file first, red ("RED: ..." subject; note RED-AT=<sha> on this bead), implement, commit green ("GREEN: ..."; note GREEN-AT=<sha>). Keep `bats tests/orca-wait.bats tests/orca-dispatch.bats` green. title: Carry the role's reasoning-effort variant into opencode: orca-dispatch, orca_opencode_command, delegate, luna route (claude-orca-1w8 slice B)
description:

title: tier-set: positional/per-role phrases with short names, catalogue lookup and @effort (claude-orca-1w8 slice A)
description:
OBJECTIVE
/tier must accept a trio like `fable glm-flash luna@high` or `fable, GLM 5.3 flash, GPT-5.6 Luna (high)` (POSITIONAL order: top, worker, recon) and per-role forms like `recon luna high`, resolve the names, and record a reasoning-effort variant per role. Today tier-set's positional form takes only Claude aliases and nothing knows about effort. The shared helper is already in: scripts/lib/tier-roles.sh (commit a46070f) prints a 5th column `variant` from roles.<role>.variant, tier_role_field accepts `variant`, tier_role_label appends `@<variant>`.

FILES (yours): scripts/tier-set.sh, scripts/tier-prime.sh, config/claude-commands/tier.md, tests/tier-phrases.bats (NEW, FROZEN after RED). Do NOT touch scripts/lib/tier-roles.sh, scripts/delegate.sh, scripts/orca-dispatch.sh, scripts/lib/orca-orch.sh, config/delegate-routes.json (another slice owns them).

SPEC
1. Argument normalisation, first thing in tier-set: when invoked with exactly ONE argument that contains a comma or whitespace, re-split it -- on commas when any are present (each phrase trimmed), else on whitespace -- and continue as if those were the args. An empty single argument behaves like no args (show). tier.md changes its one line to `!`tier-set "$ARGUMENTS"`` so commas/parentheses survive the shell, and its argument-hint documents the new forms (examples below). Keep tier.md a verbatim passthrough.
2. `help`, `-h`, `--help` print the explanation and bind NOTHING (today `tier-set --help` binds top=--help). Any positional token starting with `-` is rejected with a usage error, nothing bound.
3. Effort words: none minimal low medium high xhigh max. A phrase carries one as `<name>@<e>`, `<name> (<e>)` / `<name>(<e>)`, or a trailing bare word `<name> <e>` (whitespace inside a comma phrase, or the 3rd token of the per-role form `tier-set recon luna high`). Anything else after `@` is an error.
4. Resolution of a worker/recon phrase (a function, reused by positional and per-role forms), yielding backend/agent/model:
   a. Claude aliases fable|opus|sonnet|haiku (any case) and full claude-* ids -> as today (positional: write_state's rules; per-role: subagent/claude pinned).
   b. Existing specs unchanged: openrouter:<vendor/model>, openrouter, claude:<x>, codex:<id>, gemini:<id>, orca, subagent, inherit. `openrouter:<vendor/model>@high` works.
   c. A route NAME from config/delegate-routes.json (path overridable by TIER_ROUTES_FILE; default = <repo>/config/delegate-routes.json resolved via lib/paths.sh like tier-set finds tier-derive) resolves to that route's `.model` (e.g. glm-flash -> openrouter/z-ai/glm-5.3-flash) with backend orca, agent opencode, pinned true.
   d. A phrase containing `/` is an explicit OpenRouter id (a leading `openrouter/` is optional and normalised in): bound as typed, backend orca, agent opencode.
   e. Anything else is looked up in the catalogue: TIER_MODELS_FILE (default <run dir>/openrouter-models.json, i.e. next to tier.json) holding the raw JSON of GET https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models (public, no key). Fetch with curl -m 10 when the file is absent or older than 24h unless TIER_MODELS_FETCH=0; a failed fetch keeps any existing file. Matching: lowercase the query, split on whitespace, strip every non [a-z0-9] char from each word; a model matches when every word is a substring of the concatenation of its normalised id and name. Ids containing ':' (batch/free/exacto variants) are excluded unless the query itself contains ':'. Exactly one match -> bind it. Several, where one id is a prefix of every other -> bind that one (so "gpt-5.6 luna" beats luna-pro). Otherwise print up to 10 candidates as `<id>  <name>  $<prompt>/$<completion> per M` and exit 1 with "nothing bound". No catalogue and no fetch -> exit 1 saying so and suggesting the explicit vendor/model form.
5. `tier-set models [<words>]` prints the candidates for <words> (same matcher, no prefix rule, all shown) or, with no words, the ids of every route in delegate-routes.json plus the catalogue count/age. Exit 0.
6. State: positional `tier-set <top> <worker> [<recon>]` still writes top/worker/recon and pinned=true; for an OpenRouter worker/recon the role block becomes {backend: orca, agent: opencode, model: openrouter/<vendor/model>, pinned: true, variant: <e>} (variant key absent when none). A Claude role with an effort prints `tier: effort '<e>' applies to OpenRouter roles only -- ignored for <role>` and binds the model. Per-role form writes the same block via write_role (extend it to take an optional variant). Top stays a Claude alias/id; an effort on top is ignored with the same note.
7. Output: the bound lines use tier_role_label (which now shows @variant). tier-prime passes the 5th column into tier_role_label so the SessionStart/UserPromptSubmit lines read e.g. `worker=orca:opencode:openrouter/z-ai/glm-5.3-flash recon=orca:opencode:openrouter/openai/gpt-5.6-luna@high`.
8. Examples for tier.md's argument-hint: `fable glm-flash luna@high` | `fable, GLM 5.3 flash, GPT-5.6 Luna (high)` | `fable z-ai/glm-5.3-flash openai/gpt-5.6-luna@high` | `recon luna high` | `worker openrouter:qwen/qwen3-coder` | `models luna`.

No network, no real Orca (tier_orca_reachable must see nothing: unset ORCA_* or point CLAUDE_ORCA_ROOT at the fixture).

title: claude-dev --teardown leaves files that block git push
description:
ORIGINAL: When running claude-dev --teardown, some files are left in the working directory that shouldn't be there. These prevent pushing the repo to a separate git remote.

RECON (claude-orca-4tm, 2026-09-17, by the recon role): after teardown the folder still holds .orca-worktrees/** (Orca's linked git worktrees, each with a .git FILE pointing into the root .git/worktrees -- `git add -A` stages them as mode-160000 embedded-repo gitlinks, which is what breaks a push to a fresh remote), root .orca/** (Orca drops), .claude-dev-snapshots/<ts>/ (the beads snapshot, by design, TEARDOWN_RECOVERY.md), attachments/, and the user's .beads/. gitignore_unseed (scripts/launcher.sh ~186-215) removes every seeded ignore line, so the survivors become visible untracked files. Neither .orca/ nor .orca-worktrees/ is in the seed block (scripts/container/provision.d/50-seed-project ~63-75), so they show as untracked during the folder's whole life too (this checkout: `?? .orca/`).

OBJECTIVE: teardown leaves no Orca residue and the seed ignores Orca's on-disk state while the folder lives. The beads snapshot and attachments stay (documented recovery data; the user decides) -- out of scope here.

FILES: scripts/launcher.sh (cmd_teardown_v3 + the unseed list; bash 3.2 -- no mapfile/assoc arrays/${x^^}; scripts/lint-bash32.sh must pass), scripts/container/provision.d/50-seed-project (the seed block), tests/teardown-orca-residue.bats (NEW, FROZEN after RED). Do not edit tests/lifecycle.bats or tests/launcher-v3.bats; they must stay green as they are (they stub docker/open/uname/gh via tests/helpers -- copy their fixture pattern).

SPEC
1. cmd_teardown_v3, after removing .claude-dev and before gitignore_unseed: for every directory under <dir>/.orca-worktrees/*/ run `git -C <dir> worktree remove --force <path>` (ignore failures), then `git -C <dir> worktree prune`, then `rm -rf <dir>/.orca-worktrees <dir>/.orca`. Skip silently when <dir> is not a git repo. Print one line naming what was removed.
2. The seed block gains two lines, `.orca/` and `.orca-worktrees/`, and gitignore_unseed's seeded() list gains the same two, so a user's own lines are still restored byte for byte.
3. knowledge-base/TEARDOWN_RECOVERY.md: one sentence that teardown removes Orca's worktrees and drops.
