title: /tier: bind OpenRouter-hosted worker/recon by name with a reasoning effort (e.g. fable, glm-5.3-flash, gpt-5.6-luna@high)
description:
WHY IT NEVER CAME THROUGH (verified 2026-09-16 in this container):
- config/claude-commands/tier.md is a verbatim shell passthrough: !`tier-set $ARGUMENTS`, model haiku, effort low, 'no analysis'. Free text like 'GLM5.3 flash' or '(high)' reaches tier-set untouched.
- tier-set's 1/2/3-arg positional form only accepts Claude ladder aliases: valid_id() forbids '/' and ':', so no openrouter id can ride there. The ONLY OpenRouter form is per-role: /tier worker openrouter:z-ai/glm-5.3-flash.
- Nothing in tier-set, tier-roles.sh, tier-gate, orca-dispatch, orca_opencode_command or bin/delegate has an effort/variant concept.
- Bug found: `tier-set --help` binds top=--help (valid_id accepts it). Restored by hand.

GROUND TRUTH:
- OpenRouter ids (from the guard's /api/v1/models): z-ai/glm-5.3-flash ($0.075/$0.25 per M), z-ai/glm-5.3 ($1.4/$4.4), openai/gpt-5.6-luna ($0.2/$1.2), openai/gpt-5.6-luna-pro, -terra, -sol; all openai/gpt-5.6-* advertise reasoning_effort.
- opencode 1.18.25: `opencode run --variant high` is a built-in variant, needs NO config; on openrouter/openai/gpt-5.6-luna through the guard it turned reasoning tokens 0 -> 12 on a trivial prompt (cost 0.00151 -> 0.00153). Declaring variants.high.reasoning.effort in opencode.json gives the same result.
- delegate run --route glm-flash / glm work end to end through the guard (DELEGATION-OK; file written in worktree).
- The running container uses the IMAGE's entrypoint (pre-b30): no guard this boot until a restart; the guard now running was started by hand from opencode's auth.json.

PLAN (slices, each its own bead when work starts):
1. tier-set: positional worker/recon accept role specs (openrouter:<vendor/model>, claude:<alias>, subagent) and an '@<effort>' suffix (none|minimal|low|medium|high|xhigh); stored as roles.<role>.variant in tier.json; valid_model_ref admits '@'. Reject --help/-h explicitly. Positional 'top' stays a Claude alias (the orchestrator is this session).
2. tier-set `models [<words>]`: list/fuzzy-match ids from run/openrouter-models.json (cached from the guard's /models, refreshed when the token file changes). Unknown positional tokens resolve through it: unique match binds, ambiguity prints candidates and binds nothing. Deterministic, no LLM.
3. tier.md: argument-hint + a one-line rule: if tier-set prints candidates, pick by the user's words and re-run once. Stays a passthrough otherwise.
4. Carry the variant: orca_opencode_command appends --variant <v>; bin/delegate run passes --variant when the route or tier role carries one; tier-gate notes it for orca-backed roles. An openrouter recon MUST be orca-backed (a subagent is Claude only) -- tier-set sets backend=orca for it and tier-gate's scout note says 'orca-dispatch --recon'.
5. Auth path: opencode auth login openrouter in a plain Orca terminal -> auth.json -> entrypoint (b30) starts the guard on next boot. orca_opencode_command already uses the guard token when present and falls back to direct auth.json (2c3c003 unpinned). Decide whether orca-backed opencode may bypass the guard when no token exists.
6. Tests: bats for 1/2 (parse, suffix, fuzzy, ambiguity, --help), delegate --variant passthrough.

OPEN: which role is which in 'Fable, GLM5.3 flash, GPT-5.6 Luna (high)': worker=glm-flash recon=luna@high (positional order), or worker=luna@high recon=glm-flash (cost order)?
close_reason: Shipped: slices claude-orca-2j2 (tier-set phrases/routes/catalogue/@effort) and claude-orca-y0y (variant carried to opencode via OPENCODE_CONFIG on both orca-dispatch and delegate paths), both verified PASS; merged 95a90c0 + f123b1b; fast suite 1..621 green; live: 'fable, GLM 5.3 flash, GPT-5.6 Luna (high)' binds worker glm-5.3-flash / recon gpt-5.6-luna@high, delegate luna-high shows reasoning tokens 13 vs 0 control. Pushed to origin.

title: seed the OpenRouter guard from opencode's own login (auth.json) so a fresh folder needs no key ceremony
description:
DECIDED 2026-09-16 (settled in chat, nothing pending): a folder built fresh from the template must work after the login that happens anyway. 'opencode auth login openrouter' already writes the real key to ~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json inside the container; the guard reads it instead of demanding a second, separate key.

Two alternatives were considered and rejected: unpinning opencode's baseURL when no guard exists (would let OpenRouter traffic leave unpoliced and break knowledge-base/DATA_RESIDENCY.md), and leaving the key a deliberate per-folder step.

DEPENDS ON claude-orca-376, which establishes the file-based key chain in entrypoint.sh and removes the key from the docker run argv. This bead adds the third and last source to that same chain. Same file, so it runs after 376 is GREEN, not beside it.

WHY THIS KEEPS THE CHOKEPOINT: opencode's baseURL stays pinned at the guard, so every OpenRouter request still goes through it and still gets provider.only / allow_fallbacks=false / data_collection=deny forced onto it. The real key already sits in auth.json today -- this reads it, it does not put it there.

   Path: "${XDG_DATA_HOME:-$AGENT_HOME/.local/share}/opencode/auth.json",
   overridable with CLAUDE_ORCA_OPENCODE_AUTH. Read '.openrouter.key' with
   jq, and only when '.openrouter.type' == "api".
2. READ-ONLY, hard requirement: never write, chmod, move, copy or unlink
   auth.json, and do NOT cache what you read into $AGENT_HOME/.openrouter.key

title: the OpenRouter key should never leave the container: entrypoint reads the key file, the Mac stops carrying it
description:

Today the container cannot read it. entrypoint.sh:578 is 'OPENROUTER_REAL_KEY=${OPENROUTER_API_KEY:-}' with no file fallback, so the key's only way in is scripts/launcher.sh:2199-2204 putting it in the 'docker run' argv. title: opencode cannot connect: the guard baseURL is written even when no guard runs
description:

title: seed-project: never write through an orca.yaml symlink (supersedes claude-orca-8jb)
description:
claude-orca-8jb's verification found one defect in the new seed_orca_yaml() migration.

PROBE 7: when <project>/orca.yaml is a SYMLINK pointing outside the project, and the target's bytes are the old seeded content, the script follows the link and rewrites the target. '[ ! -e "$yaml" ]' and 'cat "$yaml"' both resolve the link, and '> "$yaml"' writes through it. Verifier observed: the link stayed a link, the outside file was rewritten, and it logged 'migrated'.

It does not violate the byte-identity rule (it only fires when the target really is the old seed), but it writes OUTSIDE PROJECT_DIR, and this whole architecture's boundary is that a folder's tooling touches only that folder. seed-project.sh runs on every start; a symlinked orca.yaml is a plausible thing for someone with a shared config to have.

FIX: one guard, before any read or write -- if [ -L "$yaml" ] then log that it is a symlink and left alone, return 0. Never read through it, never write through it, never replace the link itself. Applies to both the create path and the migrate path.

ACCEPTANCE CONTRACT
CLASS: behaviour
CHECK: bats tests/seed-project.bats tests/provision-git-init.bats
PASS-IF: TAP plan 1..N per file, no 'not ok'
FROZEN: tests/seed-project.bats, re-frozen at this bead's RED-AT
All of claude-orca-8jb's cases survive unchanged, PLUS:
 12. orca.yaml is a symlink whose target (outside the project) holds the old seeded content -> the target is byte-identical afterwards, the link is still a link, and the run logs it was left alone. Assert on the TARGET's bytes, not just the link.

BOUNDARIES: touch only scripts/container/seed-project.sh and tests/seed-project.bats. Everything else from 8jb stands. UNVERIFIED ON A MAC; claude-orca-dzt carries the Mac tab-count follow-up.

Verifier probes at HEAD: symlink to an outside file holding the old seed -> target byte-identical, still a link; dangling symlink -> left alone, no target created; symlink inside the project -> left alone; ordinary file byte-identical to the old seed -> migrated; old seed plus one extra line -> untouched; one byte changed mid-file -> untouched; CRLF copy -> untouched; read-only -> intact, exit 0; a directory named orca.yaml -> intact, no crash; user's own 'setup: make bootstrap' -> untouched; twice on a fresh project -> identical. title: startup: the seeded orca.yaml no longer opens a second terminal tab on workspace creation
description:
USER, 2026-09-15: bootstrapping a fresh project opens TWO terminal tabs in Orca. Only the Claude Code one is wanted -- "We don't need a terminal on by default".

ROOT CAUSE, confirmed by reading the code:
The same idempotent script runs twice, and one of those runs is deliberately visible.
  - scripts/container/provision.d/50-seed-project runs scripts/container/seed-project.sh during provisioning, inside the container, with its own run/provision/<step>.log and .status. Invisible, already correct.
  - seed-project.sh's seed_orca_yaml() writes <project>/orca.yaml containing:
        scripts:
          setup: bash /opt/claude-orca/scripts/container/seed-project.sh 2>/dev/null || bash .claude-dev/template/scripts/container/seed-project.sh
    and orca.yaml's own seeded comment says it plainly: "scripts.setup runs in a terminal when a workspace is created, so the work below is watchable". That terminal is the second tab, and what it runs is the SAME seeding that provisioning has already done.

The "watchable" rationale predates provision.d. Provisioning now gives every step a log and a status row that `provision status` and the SessionStart hook read back, so the visible terminal buys nothing and costs the user a tab on every workspace.

DESIGN (decided)
1. seed-project.sh, seed_orca_yaml(): still seed orca.yaml (it is where a project puts its OWN Orca config, and 55-git-init includes it in the seed commit -- keep that true), but WITHOUT any scripts: block. Seed a comment-only file that says what the file is for and that adding a scripts.setup here will open a terminal on workspace creation. Keep the existing never-overwrite rule for a file the project already has.
2. MIGRATION, for folders already carrying our seeded file (the user's fresh project is one, and it is git-tracked): when orca.yaml exists and is BYTE-IDENTICAL to a version this template previously seeded, replace it with the new comment-only content. Anything else -- a user's own setup script, our content with their edits, any byte that differs -- is left completely alone and logged as left alone. Byte-identity is the whole safety rule: never parse, never partially edit, never guess. Carry the known previous seeded content verbatim in the script for that comparison.
3. Idempotent, like everything else here: running it twice changes nothing the second time.

WHAT CHANGES DELIBERATELY, say it out loud rather than editing it green:
tests/seed-project.bats currently asserts the OPPOSITE of this bead at three lines -- `grep -q 'scripts:'`, `grep -q 'setup:'`, `grep -q 'seed-project.sh'` on the seeded orca.yaml (around lines 39-41). Those assertions encode the behaviour the user is asking to remove, so they change, and the commit must say so. Its sibling case "an orca.yaml the project already has is never overwritten" (line 54, the `make bootstrap` fixture) MUST keep passing untouched -- that is the never-clobber guarantee.
tests/provision-git-init.bats expects orca.yaml among the tracked files of the seed commit (lines 86, 177, 234). Keeping the file (design point 1) is what keeps those green; confirm they stay green rather than adjusting them.

ACCEPTANCE CONTRACT
CLASS: behaviour
CHECK: bats tests/seed-project.bats tests/provision-git-init.bats
PASS-IF: TAP plan 1..N per file, no 'not ok'
FROZEN: the new/changed cases in tests/seed-project.bats, from RED-AT
Cases:
 1. a fresh project -> orca.yaml is created and contains NO `scripts:` key and no `setup:` key at all.
 2. a fresh project -> orca.yaml still exists and is still picked up by the 55-git-init seed commit (provision-git-init.bats's tracked-file expectations stay green, unmodified).
 3. MIGRATION: a project whose orca.yaml is byte-identical to the previously-seeded content -> after the run, the file has no `scripts:`/`setup:` key.
 4. NEVER-CLOBBER: a project whose orca.yaml is `scripts:\n  setup: make bootstrap\n` -> byte-identical afterwards. Not one character changed.
 5. NEVER-CLOBBER, harder: a project whose orca.yaml is the previously-seeded content PLUS one extra user line -> left byte-identical, and the run logs that it was left alone.

title: provision: orchestration-skill install decides by exact name only, --json authoritative (supersedes claude-orca-4gx)
description:
Supersedes claude-orca-4gx (which superseded claude-orca-ndy). Same goal. Third contract; the first two both shipped a wrongful-skip hole, so the cases below are written to close the CLASS, not the instance.

THE BUG CLASS, stated once: this step decides whether to install by reading text. Every version so far has decided "already installed" from a word appearing somewhere in that text. When it guesses wrong in that direction, `skills install` never runs, the step exits 0, and `provision status` shows a green row — the user's "Orchestration: Not Installed" persists forever with the provisioning system reporting success. A wrongful SKIP is invisible and permanent. A wrongful INSTALL costs one idempotent network call. The step must be biased to install whenever it is not certain.

WHAT 4gx STILL GOT WRONG (verifier, reproduced against the real step):
  (b) --json unsupported, a flush-left prose line "pairs with the orchestration skill" -> SKIPPED. Wrong.
  (d) plain output carrying "warning: orchestration index stale" -> SKIPPED. Wrong.
4gx's fallback drops indented lines, then whole-token matches anywhere in what survives:
    grep -v -E '^[[:space:]]' | grep -qE '(^|[[:space:]])orchestration([[:space:]]|\(|$)'
Indentation is the only thing separating a name from prose there, and the token match floats anywhere in the line. Wrapped prose, a warning, or any flush-left diagnostic reopens the exact hole.
Correct in 4gx and to be preserved: (a) indented prose -> installs; (c) a skill named `orchestration-extras` -> installs (hyphen is not a boundary).

THE FIX, two parts.

1. Make --json AUTHORITATIVE. Today a confident --json "not installed" still falls through to the fuzzy fallback, which can then overrule it. It must not. Decide in this order:
   - run `"$cli" skills installed --json`; if it exits 0 AND its output PARSES as JSON (e.g. `jq -e . >/dev/null`), that answer is final: installed iff `jq -e '.result.skills[] | select(.name == "orchestration")'` matches. Never consult the plain path afterward, in either direction.
   - otherwise (non-zero exit, unparseable output, or no jq) fall through to 2.
   This alone kills (d): a zero exit carrying non-JSON no longer counts as authoritative, and no longer silently lands in the fuzzy path with its hole intact.

2. ANCHOR the fallback to the start of the line. A selector line begins with the name. Prose, warnings and locations do not:
       grep -qE '^orchestration([[:space:]]|\(|$)'
   ndy's frozen case-2 fixture prints one flush-left space-separated list of bare names ("beads orchestration snowpark-deploy"), where orchestration is not first — handle that as a SEPARATE, explicit alternative (e.g. a line consisting only of bare names, no parens and no prose punctuation, matched token-wise), not by loosening the anchor for everything. If that degenerate shape cannot be discriminated cleanly from prose, prefer INSTALLING over skipping and say so in your report — case 2's fixture predates the real two-line format and is the weakest thing in this contract.

Unchanged from 4gx and still required: `skills install --skill orchestration --local` (never drop --local -- bare default installs GLOBALLY across every project on the host); non-fatal but honest non-zero exit when install fails; exit 0 with a log line when no CLI resolves; default to attempting the install when nothing is confident.

ACCEPTANCE CONTRACT
CLASS: behaviour
CHECK: bats tests/provision-orca-skills.bats
PASS-IF: TAP plan 1..N, no 'not ok'
FROZEN: tests/provision-orca-skills.bats (re-frozen at this bead's RED-AT)
Cases: all 8 from 4gx survive, PLUS these, each asserting on CAPTURED ARGV (was `skills install` actually invoked?) and never on exit code alone:
  9.  --json unsupported; plain output has NO orchestration selector but a FLUSH-LEFT prose line mentioning "orchestration" -> MUST INSTALL. (verifier probe (b))
  10. --json unsupported; plain output has NO orchestration selector but a flush-left line "warning: orchestration index stale" -> MUST INSTALL. (verifier probe (d))
  11. `--json` exits 0 but prints non-JSON garbage; no orchestration installed -> MUST INSTALL. (the authoritativeness hole)
  12. `--json` exits 0 with VALID JSON listing orchestration as installed, while the plain output does NOT mention it at all -> MUST NOT INSTALL (json is authoritative in the positive direction).
  13. `--json` exits 0 with VALID JSON that does NOT list orchestration, while the plain output DOES contain a flush-left line mentioning orchestration -> MUST INSTALL (json authoritative in the negative direction; the fallback must never overrule it).

BOUNDARIES
- Do not touch entrypoint.sh, config-sync.sh, 20-config-sync, or claude-orca-0jn's early-sync block.
- Tests MUST override `ORCA_CLI`, never only `ORCA_BIN` — `resolve_cli()` ignores ORCA_BIN, so an ORCA_BIN-only stub runs the REAL binary and performs a REAL network install into this repo. That has already happened once and left untracked `.agents/skills/orchestration/`, `.claude/skills/`, `skills-lock.json` to be cleaned by hand. Run `git status --porcelain` before each commit and confirm none of those three appear.
- Run tests/provision-orca-skills.bats, tests/provision.bats, and lint-bash32.sh on the step. Not ./run-tests.sh --all.

title: provision: install the orchestration skill with an EXACT installed-check (supersedes claude-orca-ndy)
description:
Supersedes claude-orca-ndy. Same goal, contract widened by one case that ndy's frozen tests could not catch.

WHY ndy FAILED VERIFICATION. Its step checked idempotency like this:

    installed="$("$cli" skills installed 2>/dev/null)"
    case "$installed" in
        *orchestration*) echo "already installed"; exit 0 ;;
    esac

That is an unanchored substring match over the ENTIRE stdout of `orca skills installed`, which prints a two-line record per skill -- a `name (hash)` selector line AND an indented prose description, plus a location line. Orca's bundled skill descriptions cross-reference each other by name ("Use `orca-cli` instead for...", "pairs with the orchestration skill..."), so a skill that is NOT orchestration can carry the word "orchestration" in its description and satisfy the match.

Reproduced by the verifier against the real step with a stub emitting the real format (beads + snowpark-deploy installed, NO orchestration selector, snowpark-deploy's description mentioning "the orchestration skill"):

    the orchestration skill is already installed; nothing to do
    step exit=0
    --- install log ---
    (end log)

`skills install` never ran, the step exited 0, and `provision status` records a green row. The user's symptom -- Settings showing "Orchestration: Not Installed" -- would persist silently on every boot forever, with the provisioning system actively reporting success. That failure mode is worse than the original bug, because it is invisible.

ndy's four frozen cases do not cover it: its "already installed" fixture puts `orchestration` in a selector position, so selector-vs-description is never discriminated.

THE FIX
`orca skills installed --json` exists and is exact -- it returns `{"result":{"skills":[{"name":"snowpark-deploy",...}]}}`, with names in a field distinct from descriptions. ndy's own DESIGN line asked for --json first; the implementation used the plain form.

  - primary: `"$cli" skills installed --json`, matched with `jq -e '.result.skills[] | select(.name == "orchestration")'`. Exact field equality, never substring.
  - fallback, when jq is missing or --json is unsupported by an older Orca: anchor to the selector line's real shape, `grep -qE '^orchestration \('` -- start of line, name, space, open paren. Never a bare substring over the whole output.
  - if BOTH paths are unavailable/inconclusive, prefer attempting the install over skipping it. `skills install` is itself idempotent (npx skills add re-resolves), so a redundant install costs a network call; a wrongful skip costs the entire feature, silently. Bias toward the recoverable error.
  - keep everything else ndy got right, unchanged: `--skill orchestration --local` (never drop --local -- the bare default installs GLOBALLY across every project on the host), non-fatal failure that exits non-zero so the status row is honest, graceful skip when no Orca CLI resolves.

ACCEPTANCE CONTRACT
CLASS: behaviour
CHECK: bats tests/provision-orca-skills.bats
PASS-IF: TAP plan 1..N, no 'not ok'
FROZEN: tests/provision-orca-skills.bats (re-frozen at this bead's RED-AT; ndy's four cases are inherited and must all survive)
Cases -- ndy's four, kept verbatim in intent, PLUS:
 5. THE REGRESSION CASE. Stub `skills installed` (both the --json and plain forms) so that NO installed skill is named orchestration, but another skill's DESCRIPTION contains the word "orchestration" in prose, in the real two-line format. The step MUST run `skills install`. Assert the install was actually invoked (captured argv), not merely that exit is 0.
 6. Stub where orchestration IS genuinely installed (a real selector/name entry) -> install is NOT invoked. Assert on captured argv, not exit code.
 7. Stub where `--json` is unsupported (exits non-zero on --json, works plain) -> the anchored fallback is used and still discriminates case 5 correctly.
 8. Every install invocation carries --local (grep captured argv across all cases that install).

BOUNDARIES
- Do not touch entrypoint.sh, config-sync.sh, 20-config-sync, or the claude-orca-0jn early-sync block.
- Do not run ./run-tests.sh --all. Run tests/provision-orca-skills.bats, tests/provision.bats, and lint-bash32.sh on the step.
- CRITICAL, learned the expensive way in this bead's own verification: `ORCA_BIN` is NOT an effective override for this step -- `resolve_cli()` has its own candidate list and `ORCA_CLI` is the real override. A test that sets only ORCA_BIN will run the REAL orca binary and perform a REAL network install into this repo, leaving untracked `.agents/skills/orchestration/`, `.claude/skills/` and `skills-lock.json` behind. That happened once already and had to be cleaned up by hand. Every test MUST override `ORCA_CLI`, and you MUST confirm `git status --porcelain` is clean of those three paths before you commit.
- UNVERIFIED ON A MAC applies (scripts/container/); a real npx install still cannot be proven here. claude-orca-g3z already carries the Mac follow-up -- reference it, do not file a second one.

title: provision: install Orca's orchestration skill so Settings stops showing Not Installed (restores riu.3's default)
description:
USER, 2026-09-15: a fresh project's Orca Settings shows "Orchestration: Not Installed".

ROOT CAUSE, confirmed by direct CLI evidence in this container (not inferred):
  orca skills installed        -> lists only "beads" and "snowpark-deploy"
  orca skills list             -> "orchestration" IS a bundled, installable skill
  orca skills install --dry-run --skill orchestration --local
                                -> resolves to: npx --yes skills add https://github.com/stablyai/orca
                                   --skill orchestration --agent claude-code --agent opencode
                                   --agent universal -y
Nothing in this template's provisioning ever runs `orca skills install`. Grepped every script under scripts/ and bin/: zero hits for "orca skills install", "sandbox.json", or any copy of config/orca-skills/* into a live config dir. config-sync.sh copies config/skills/* but never config/orca-skills/*.

WHY IT REGRESSED, not why it was never built: claude-orca-riu.3 (closed, P1, "Default orca.cli=true: native Orca orchestration enabled for registered folders") already recorded this exact user decision -- "native Orca orchestration on by default for newly registered folders". It shipped against an OLDER architecture: a Mac-side sandbox.json {"orca":{"cli":true}} flag threaded through a "register" step and gen-settings' allowUnixSockets, because Orca ran unsandboxed on the Mac and the sandboxed agent needed a socket bridge to reach it (config/orca-cli-addendum.md and config/orca-skills/orchestration/SKILL.md are that era's artifacts). The 8uo epic later moved Orca to run INSIDE the same container as the agent (current CLAUDE.md architecture) -- knowledge-base/ORCA_INTEGRATION.md already documents the new reality ("no socket to expose and no flag to set... simply available") -- but nothing ever ported riu.3's actual installation step onto the new `orca skills install` mechanism. The old sandbox.json path is dead code now; nothing reads it. This bead restores the already-decided default using the current mechanism, it does not make a new design call.

DESIGN (decided)
New provision.d step, `scripts/container/provision.d/75-orca-skills`, following the exact shape of the existing steps (source provision-lib.sh, non-fatal by the runner's own contract, idempotent, its own log/status row):
  - idempotent check first: `orca skills installed --json` (or plain, if --json on "installed" behaves like "install"'s), skip with a clear log line if "orchestration" is already present -- never re-run npx on every boot.
  - install: `orca skills install --skill orchestration --local` (no --agent override needed -- the dry-run above shows it already detects claude-code + opencode + universal correctly for this stack). --local is the deliberate, non-default choice: every other piece of state in this codebase is scoped to the folder (one container per folder, no central install -- see CLAUDE.md's Architecture Overview), and the bare command's default is GLOBAL (all projects on the host). Using the default here would be the one thing in this whole system that reaches outside the folder it started in. Do not omit --local.
  - this is a real network call (npx hitting a registry) -- exactly the shape 60-orca-repo-add and 70-openrouter-guard already are. It belongs in provision.d, not in the early-sync path claude-orca-0jn just added (that path is reserved for fast, non-network, must-not-race work). Do not touch scripts/container/entrypoint.sh for this bead.
  - non-fatal, matching every other step: a failed install (offline, npx missing, registry down) logs and moves on; the next start retries it, same as everything else under provision.d.

title: Real boot, natively: early config-sync puts statusLine in settings.json before Orca's URL, and a sabotaged config still serves
description:
Follow-up to claude-orca-0jn, verified at the bats/logic level only. Claude's item, not the user's.

claude-orca-0jn made entrypoint.sh run config-sync once, early, non-fatally, before Orca serve starts, so a brand-new project's first Claude Code session sees settings.json's statusLine key immediately. Everything about that is proven in the stubbed bats suite. Two things only a real Mac with a working daemon can show:

1. THE FIX WORKS: bootstrap a genuinely new folder, open it the moment the pairing URL/Orca.app appears, and confirm the statusline renders in the very first Claude Code session -- no restart needed. This is the user-visible symptom that started claude-orca-0jn.

2. THE CONSTRAINT SURVIVED: sabotage config-sync (rename the template's config/ dir, or chmod it unreadable) and confirm the container STILL comes up -- URL published, Orca serving, a terminal reachable -- exactly the anti-silent-failure guarantee claude-orca-dbu.4 built. A regression here is worse than the original bug: dbu.4 made a broken folder debuggable; a bad reordering could make it silent again.

Docker cannot run in this container (userns denied), so neither can be exercised here.

RUN ON A MAC, against pushed HEAD (mac-e2e.sh clones HEAD): tests/mac-e2e.sh, plus the two manual scenarios above; paste the summary table and both scenario outcomes into this bead.

PASS-IF: statusline present on first session with no restart, AND a sabotaged config-sync still yields a served, reachable folder.

title: entrypoint: sync config before the web URL publishes, so a first-run session never starts without statusLine
description:
USER, 2026-09-15: on a brand-new project the pairing URL (which unblocks Orca/the browser) is published, and provisioning -- including 20-config-sync, the ONLY thing that writes settings.json's statusLine key on a first-ever boot -- runs afterward, in the foreground. A Claude Code session started the moment the workspace opens can read a settings.json that does not exist yet, or exists without statusLine, and Claude Code only reads statusLine at process start, so it never catches up mid-session. User asked: fix it in the .sh and push.

CONSTRAINT THAT MUST SURVIVE (read scripts/container/provision-run.sh's header comment in full first): claude-orca-dbu.4 deliberately moved config-sync AFTER the URL publish so that a folder whose config-sync died would still come up -- "no Orca, no terminal, no Claude Code to say so" was the failure mode being fixed. This bead's change must NOT reintroduce that: the early sync must never be allowed to delay or block serve, and its failure must never stop serve from starting. It runs a second time, unchanged, as part of the normal provision.d sweep afterward (checksum-gated no-op) -- that is what still gives it a log/status row under run/provision/.

DESIGN (decided)
In scripts/container/entrypoint.sh, after privilege drop (PRIVDROP path established, agent user usable) and before starting the --serve command, run config-sync.sh once, directly (not through provision-run.sh):
  - resolve sync_host with the SAME three-way fallback provision.d/20-config-sync uses (PROJECT_DIR/.claude-dev/template/config, else dirname(TEMPLATE_ROOT) when its basename is "template", else HOST_DIR/template/config) -- copy that logic, do not diverge from it.
  - invoke via run_as_agent, exactly as run_provision's steps do, so ownership matches.
  - bounded by a timeout of CLAUDE_ORCA_EARLY_SYNC_TIMEOUT seconds (default 30) when the timeout binary exists, uncapped otherwise (matches the flock portability guard already in config-sync.sh).
  - failure is a warn(), never a die(): serve starts regardless, exit code discarded beyond the log line.
  - log to the same run/provision area or a clearly named early-sync log -- pick one and say why in the comment.
  - comment the WHY inline: this closes the first-run statusLine race; the anti-silent-failure property is preserved because failure here only means the LATER provision.d/20-config-sync (still running after the URL, still logged, still retried every start) does the job instead -- nothing about this step's failure is fatal or user-visible-as-a-hang.

ACCEPTANCE CONTRACT
CLASS: behaviour
CHECK: bats tests/container-entrypoint.bats
PASS-IF: TAP plan 1..N, no NEW not-ok case beyond the pre-existing reds (confirm the exact current set with git stash first -- do not assume the list from memory)
FROZEN: the new test case(s) added for this bead, once committed RED
Cases to add:
 1. a brand-new project (no .claude-dev/home at all) run through the entrypoint: run/home/.claude/settings.json exists AND its statusLine.command is non-empty BEFORE run/orca-web-url.txt is written (assert ordering, not just eventual presence -- e.g. a stub ORCA_BIN that blocks on a fifo until the test has already checked settings.json).
 2. a config-sync.sh that exits non-zero (stub it, or corrupt the template config) does NOT stop serve from starting and orca-web-url.txt is still written -- mirrors the existing case around line 278's pattern for a failing setup.sh.
 3. the early sync and the later provision.d/20-config-sync do not double-run destructively -- the second one is a checksum no-op (assert via config-sync's own log or the hash file's mtime not changing on the second call within the same boot).
 4. the existing case "entrypoint config-syncs from the folder's own template clone, not the image's frozen copy" (~line 1180) still passes unmodified in intent -- it may now observe the sync happening earlier; do not weaken its assertion, adjust its ordering expectations only if it literally checks against orca-web-url.txt timing.

BOUNDARIES
- Do not touch provision.d/20-config-sync or provision-run.sh's contract (log/status per step) -- it still runs, still records, still is the retry path.
- Do not change config-sync.sh itself.
- Do not run ./run-tests.sh --all; run bats tests/container-entrypoint.bats and scripts/lint-bash32.sh scripts/container/entrypoint.sh.
- This touches scripts/container/ -- UNVERIFIED on a Mac per CLAUDE.md; say so in the commit. tests/mac-e2e.sh owes the real proof (a fresh folder, watch settings.json land before the URL, confirm Orca still comes up when config-sync is sabotaged).

RED-AT: 8491c4a — bats tests/container-entrypoint.bats: 3 new cases (18,19,20) all failed for the right reason (feature absent); pre-existing reds unchanged (case 7 stub-ORCA_BIN exit code, case 13 template-root message, case 20/23 managed-settings default).

Early config-sync runs after privilege drop and before serve, non-fatal (warn, never die/exit), timeout-bounded, same host-fallback order as 20-config-sync. C6 (serve itself, not the test, checking settings.json the instant before speaking, on a folder with no prior .claude-dev/home): statusline_nonempty=yes. Suite: 25 cases, only the 3 pre-existing reds remain (7/13/23), stable across two runs.

title: message cap: finishing messages <= 100 words, measured every turn in the cost-mirror line
description:
USER, 2026-09-15 (third ask; Sunday's yz2 shipped an input diet and one shape rule, nothing that caps output): outputs must be MUCH more succinct; important details get lost in overlong explanations.

BASELINE this session (session-cost.py, top-level assistant text messages): 27 messages, mean 115 words, median 45, max 409; the five largest are 291-409 words and all are Done/progress messages to the user.

DESIGN (decided)
1. Rulebook: rewrite § Finishing a message in config/claude-user-memory.md to carry a NUMBER: a finishing message is <= 100 words, an interim update one line. Cut topics not words: no narrating what was done, no restating the user, no defending a choice already made, nothing an earlier message said, no adjacent observations. Keep the three ending shapes. config/claude-user-memory.md is capped at 1150 words by tests/rulebook.bats:68 (live copy is 1081) -- the rewrite must be net-neutral or shorter.
2. Readout: a new segment in python/cost-mirror.py's UserPromptSubmit line (joined with ' | ' like lane_segment/delegation_drift_segment): 'msg: last 409w (cap 100) · over 7/27'. Counts words of the LAST top-level assistant text message (group text blocks by message.id; skip isSidechain) and the running number of messages over the cap this session. Cap from env CLAUDE_ORCA_MSG_CAP, default 100. The number lives in the code once; the rulebook's number must equal it (lockstep test, the repo's pattern).
3. A Stop-hook block was considered and rejected: the long message has already streamed, so a block only appends a second one.

ACCEPTANCE CONTRACT
CLASS: behaviour
CHECK: bats tests/message-cap.bats tests/rulebook.bats
PASS-IF: TAP plan 1..N, no 'not ok', one 'ok' per case
FROZEN: tests/message-cap.bats
Cases:
 1. config/claude-user-memory.md § Finishing a message contains '100 words'
 2. the cap default in python/cost-mirror.py equals the rulebook's number (lockstep)
 3. fixture transcript, last top-level assistant message 300 words -> the cost-mirror line contains a msg segment with '300' and '100'
 4. fixture, last message 80 words -> segment reports within budget / over 0
 5. fixture where a 500-word isSidechain assistant entry FOLLOWS an 80-word top-level one -> reports 80 (sidechains ignored)
 6. fixture with a message split across several jsonl lines sharing one message.id -> counted once, words summed
 7. missing or malformed transcript -> exit 0, and the rest of the [cost-mirror] line still prints (fail open)
 8. tests/rulebook.bats stays green (1150-word cap on claude-user-memory.md)

Fixture format: python/session-cost.py's docstring documents the fields (entry.type, isSidechain, message.id, message.content blocks with .type text).

title: mac-e2e: prove a real docker build installs the RESOLVED Claude Code version (claude-orca-7a0)
description:
Follow-up to claude-orca-7a0, which is verified at the logic level only. Claude's item, not the user's.

claude-orca-7a0 made --update resolve the newest Claude Code and pass it as --build-arg CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION. Everything about that is proven by the bats suite EXCEPT the one thing only a machine with a working Docker daemon can show: that a real build consumes the arg, busts the cached payload layer, and lands the resolved version in /opt/claude/VERSION.

Docker cannot run in this container (failed to register layer: unshare: operation not permitted; userns denied), so this cannot be discharged here.

RUN ON A MAC, against pushed HEAD (mac-e2e.sh clones HEAD, so no local-only commits):
  1. tests/mac-e2e.sh -- paste its summary table into this bead.
  2. In the throwaway folder, confirm the build line carried the arg:
       grep -o -- '--build-arg CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION=[^ ]*' on the build log
  3. docker exec into the container: cat /opt/claude/VERSION should equal
       curl -fsSL https://downloads.claude.ai/claude-code-releases/latest
  4. The cache-bust case, which is the whole point: rebuild once with
       CLAUDE_ORCA_CLAUDE_VERSION set to an older real release (e.g. 2.1.261),
       confirm /opt/claude/VERSION follows it, then unset and rebuild and
       confirm it returns to latest. A cached layer surviving that is the bug.
  5. Offline path: with the network down or the base pointed at an
       unroutable host, a build must still SUCCEED at the fallback floor.

PASS-IF: steps 2-5 all hold and the mac-e2e summary table is pasted here.
Until then claude-orca-7a0's host-side surface stays UNVERIFIED.
notes: 2026-09-19 partial evidence from the user's real rebuild (read from inside the container): step 2 -- run/container.log 'docker build ... --build-arg CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION=2.1.278' (the previous build line carried 2.1.273, so the resolver moved with upstream) and run/build.log's layer reads 'RUN CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION=2.1.278 ORCA_VERSION=1.4.203 /opt/claude-orca-setup.sh --image'; step 3 -- /opt/claude/VERSION = 2.1.278 = curl downloads.claude.ai/claude-code-releases/latest at the same moment. Steps 4 (cache-bust with an older release and back) and 5 (offline floor) need a docker daemon driven from the Mac and are NOT observed; the bead stays open for them and the mac-e2e table.

title: claude-dev --update installs the newest Claude Code, not a hand-set pin
description:
USER REQUEST (asked three times, 2026-09-14): --update must get the LATEST Claude Code, not whatever literal a human last typed into the pin.

Today the pin is a literal in three lockstep files and a rebuild can only ever install that literal. Worse, the payload layer keys on the ARG value, so when the literal does not change Docker reuses the cached layer and the install step never re-runs (observed: /opt/claude/claude dated 2026-09-12 21:45 surviving a 2026-09-14 22:03 rebuild).

GROUND TRUTH established this session:
  https://downloads.claude.ai/claude-code-releases/latest -> '2.1.271', 7 bytes,
  no trailing newline, content-type text/plain, cache-control no-cache max-age=0.
  A sibling 'stable' pointer returns 2.1.236. npm dist-tags agree
  (stable=2.1.236, latest=2.1.271). curl -f exits 22 on a bad path.
  The resolved version always has a <version>/manifest.json carrying linux-arm64.

DESIGN (decided, not open):
  Resolution happens OUTSIDE the docker build and arrives as
  --build-arg CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION=<resolved>, reusing the ARG plumbing that
  already exists. Resolving INSIDE a RUN layer would be cached forever and
  reproduce the exact bug being fixed. When a new release ships the ARG value
  changes and the layer cache busts by itself; when nothing shipped the cache
  hits and the build stays fast.
  The existing literal stops being 'the version' and becomes the FALLBACK
  floor: offline, DNS-blocked or garbage response falls back to it and the
  build still succeeds. A build must never fail over a network blip.
  CLAUDE_ORCA_CLAUDE_VERSION=<x.y.z> forces an exact version and skips the
  network -- the rollback path, since 'always latest' otherwise removes the
  user's ability to escape a bad release.

ACCEPTANCE CONTRACT
CLASS: behaviour
CHECK: bats tests/claude-version-resolve.bats
PASS-IF: TAP plan 1..N with no 'not ok' line and one 'ok' per case
FROZEN: tests/claude-version-resolve.bats
Cases the contract requires:
  1. a stubbed 200 returning '2.1.271' resolves to exactly 2.1.271
  2. a stubbed curl failure (exit 22) falls back to the literal pin, exit 0
  3. a non-semver body (an HTML error page) is REJECTED and falls back --
     never passed through to a build-arg
  4. CLAUDE_ORCA_CLAUDE_VERSION=9.9.9 wins and makes no network call
  5. the resolver never prints an empty string
  6. the launcher's docker build call passes --build-arg CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION=
  7. scripts/lint-bash32.sh stays clean (host-side code is bash 3.2)

NOTE: tests/container-entrypoint.bats case 8 currently asserts the pin
lockstep ('ONE Claude Code pin in this repo'). Its premise is what the user
is deliberately changing, so that case legitimately changes meaning -- say so
in the commit rather than quietly editing it green.

Touches the Dockerfile and scripts/container/, so per CLAUDE.md the definition
of done needs tests/mac-e2e.sh on a real Mac; none here, so UNVERIFIED.
close_reason:
GREEN-AT-2 f2c170e, verifier PASS, pushed as 3c055a6. Host-side proof carried by claude-orca-y6q.

--update now resolves the newest Claude Code outside the docker build and passes it as --build-arg CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION, so the ARG value changes when a release ships and the payload layer cache busts by itself. Resolving inside a RUN layer would have been cached forever, reproducing the bug this fixes.

Shipped: scripts/resolve-claude-version.sh (never empty, always exit 0, semver-validated, falls back to the 2.1.271 floor offline or on a garbage body); launcher.sh try_build passes the arg unconditionally, guarded so a missing resolver degrades to the Dockerfile default instead of killing the build under set -e; setup.sh phase_claude resolves lazily only when no version was given, keeping the existing manifest+sha256 verification; --check no longer demands exact equality against a re-resolved latest, which would have spuriously failed 10-toolchain-verify a day after any build.

Two defects caught in review, both measured rather than argued:
 - the first cut made the build-arg conditional on differing from the Dockerfile default, green only while latest happened to equal the baked default. CLAUDE_ORCA_CLAUDE_VERSION=9.9.9 turned launcher-v3-build case 11 red, proving it would fail on the next upstream release. Fixed by passing unconditionally and narrowing that case to its documented intent.
 - it also made the suite hit the live network: one test went 1s to 11.3s against a blackholed endpoint. Fixed via the escape hatch in the shared bats setup; blackholed and clean runs now 22.89s vs 22.96s.

Verifier evidence: frozen diff empty since RED-AT; RED-AT genuinely red 7 of 8; 1..8 green at HEAD; inversion proves cases 1-4 exercise curl for real (they go red under a forced version); ./run-tests.sh 0 failures across 51 files; container suites byte-identical to b9d68b2.

Lockstep held: the container-image and container-entrypoint pin assertions stayed green untouched, since all literals still match. That contract now governs the fallback floor rather than the installed version.

title: provision: initialise a folder that is not a git repository, or has no commits, on main with a seed commit before orca repo add (Orca needs a base branch)
description:
PROBLEM. A folder bootstrapped with claude_orca shows up in the Orca app as a project with no workspace, and "Create worktree" fails with "No base branch found". Reproduced 2026-09-13 in an isolated Orca 1.4.197 runtime: `orca repo add` REJECTS a non-git folder ("Not a valid git repository"), ACCEPTS a `git init`ed repo with no commits (kind git, a main worktree listed) but every `worktree create` then throws "Could not resolve a default base ref for this repo" (the app renders that as "No base branch found"); a repo with one commit on main or master works with no remote at all. Orca resolves the base from origin/HEAD, origin/main, origin/master, refs/heads/main, refs/heads/master and nothing else. Nothing in bootstrap.sh, launcher.sh, entrypoint.sh or provision.d ever runs `git init` or a first commit in PROJECT_DIR.

OBJECTIVE. Add ONE provision step, scripts/container/provision.d/55-git-init (runs after 50-seed-project, before 60-orca-repo-add), that guarantees PROJECT_DIR is a git repository with at least one commit on a branch Orca can base a worktree on, plus its bats file, plus two doc sentences. bash 3.2 clean (no mapfile, no [[ ]] in tests, no ${x^^}, no += onto empty arrays under set -u). Source ../provision-lib.sh like the sibling steps; `set -uo pipefail`; header comment in the house style (why it exists, what it never does).

BEHAVIOUR of 55-git-init (PROJECT_DIR from provision-lib.sh; exit 1 with a message when it is not a directory or git is not on PATH):
1. inside="$(git -C "$PROJECT_DIR" rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree 2>&1)".
   a. inside = true: top="$(git -C "$PROJECT_DIR" rev-parse --show-toplevel)" compared with "$(cd "$PROJECT_DIR" && pwd -P)".
      - HEAD has commits (`git rev-parse --verify -q HEAD`): print "<dir> is a git repository with commits on <branch>; nothing to do" (name the toplevel when it is a parent folder) and exit 0.
      - HEAD unborn and toplevel == PROJECT_DIR: b="$(git symbolic-ref --short -q HEAD)"; if b is neither main nor master, `git symbolic-ref HEAD refs/heads/main` and print that the unborn HEAD was moved from '<b>' to main because Orca only bases worktrees on main/master. Then the seed commit (step 2).
      - HEAD unborn and toplevel is a PARENT folder: print "inside the repository at <top>, which has no commits; not touching a repository that is not this folder's" and exit 1.
   b. inside != true and "$PROJECT_DIR/.git" exists: git could not read the repository (dubious ownership, corruption): print "git cannot read the repository at <dir>: <git's message verbatim>" and exit 1. NEVER run git init here.
   c. inside != true and no .git: `git -C "$PROJECT_DIR" init -q -b main` (fallback for an old git: `git init -q` then `git symbolic-ref HEAD refs/heads/main`); print "initialised <dir> as a git repository on main". Then the seed commit.
2. Seed commit, in PROJECT_DIR, ONLY the seeds and never the user's files: for p in .gitignore orca.yaml .beads: skip if absent; `git add -- "$p" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true` (a .beads whose files are all ignored must not abort); keep p in the pathspec list only if `git ls-files --error-unmatch -- "$p"` succeeds. Identity: name="$(git config user.name 2>/dev/null || true)", email likewise; when empty use claude_orca / claude_orca@localhost via `-c user.name=... -c user.email=...` (never override a configured identity). Always `-c commit.gpgsign=false --no-verify` (bd installs hooks; no key in the container). If the pathspec list is empty: `git commit -q --allow-empty -m "$msg"`; else `git commit -q -m "$msg" -- $paths` (the pathspec form commits ONLY those paths even when the user has other files staged). msg = "claude_orca: seed commit (<paths>)" or "claude_orca: seed commit (empty)". Print "seed commit <short sha> on <branch>: <paths>". Exit 0. Idempotent: the second run takes branch 1a and does nothing.

TESTS. New tests/provision-git-init.bats (`load helpers/setup`, assertions with [ ] and functions, fixtures under $BATS_TEST_TMPDIR, run the step as `env -i PATH="$PATH" HOME="$h" PROJECT_DIR="$d" bash "$STEP"` with HOME a fresh empty dir unless the case seeds a .gitconfig, and unset GIT_AUTHOR_*/GIT_COMMITTER_*). Cases, one @test each:
 1 plain folder with a user file data.csv and pre-written .gitignore + orca.yaml: .git exists, HEAD is main, exactly one commit, `git ls-files` is exactly .gitignore and orca.yaml, `git status --porcelain` shows `?? data.csv`, output contains "initialised".
 2 unborn repo on master: the commit lands on master, no rename.
 3 unborn repo on trunk: HEAD is main afterwards and the output says it was moved.
 4 repo with commits: HEAD sha unchanged, output contains "nothing to do", exit 0.
 5 idempotence: two runs on a plain folder leave exactly one commit; the second output says nothing to do.
 6 identity: with no gitconfig the author email is claude_orca@localhost; with HOME/.gitconfig naming Jo <jo@example.com> the author is that.
 7 no seeds at all: an empty commit is made (one commit, `git ls-files` empty).
 8 unborn repo with the user's own file already staged: after the step the seed commit's tree (`git ls-tree --name-only HEAD`) holds only the seeds and `git diff --cached --name-only` still lists the user's file. If git refuses the pathspec form on a root commit, report that deviation in your result instead of changing the test.
 9 a subfolder of a repo with commits: exit 0, "nothing to do", no nested .git created.
 10 a .git git cannot read: run with GIT_TEST_ASSUME_DIFFERENT_OWNER=1 on an unborn repo: exit 1, output contains git's dubious-ownership message, no commit made.
 11 the step file is executable and `ls provision.d | sort` lists 55-git-init before 60-orca-repo-add and after 50-seed-project.
 12 a .beads directory seeded like bd init (config.yaml, issues.jsonl, and a .beads/.gitignore ignoring dolt/) is committed minus the ignored parts.
Then run `bats tests/provision-git-init.bats tests/provision.bats tests/seed-project.bats tests/container-entrypoint.bats tests/container-entrypoint-seed.bats` and `bash scripts/lint-bash32.sh` if it accepts container paths; report the TAP plan lines and every 'not ok' verbatim.

DOCS. README.md Quickstart step 1 (after "Re-running is safe."): one sentence that the folder need not be a git repository -- the first start initialises one on main with a seed commit (.gitignore, orca.yaml, the tracker) because Orca cannot create a workspace without a base branch, and the folder's own files stay untracked until added. README.md provision list (~line 413, "the first-run seeds, the git identity, the tracker, the `orca repo add`"): insert "the repository itself (initialised on `main` with a seed commit when the folder is not one, or has no commits yet)". description:

title: container: provision step sweeps stale worktrees at every start (clean ones removed through Orca, dirty or busy ones kept and reported)
description:
WHY
Nothing in the repo ever removes a worktree (orca-run.sh, delegate.sh and by-hand executors all create them; no script calls `orca worktree rm` or `git worktree remove`). Orca rediscovers every git worktree from .git/worktrees at load and lists each as a workspace under the project, so the user's sidebar filled with "claude-orca (Detached HEAD)", "wt/dbu", "wt/tests-b". The user wants that noise cleared by the script.

WHAT
A new step scripts/container/provision.d/65-worktree-sweep following the provision.d conventions (sources provision-lib.sh; idempotent; never fatal; writes the row `provision status` reads). For every worktree of PROJECT_DIR from `git worktree list --porcelain` other than the main one:
- directory missing -> `git worktree prune` covers it; log "pruned <path>".
- some process has its cwd inside it (scan /proc/[0-9]*/cwd; readlink) -> keep; log "busy <path>".
- `git -C <path> status --porcelain --untracked-files=all` empty -> remove: when `orca-ide status --json` reports .result.runtime.reachable == true use `orca-ide worktree rm --worktree path:<path> --json` (Orca also drops the branch when it can prove it merged, keeps it otherwise); when Orca is unreachable use `git worktree remove <path>`; then `git worktree prune`; log "removed <path>".
- otherwise (uncommitted or untracked files) -> keep; log "kept <path>: uncommitted changes".
Status: ok when nothing was kept for uncommitted changes (busy is ok); FAIL naming each kept-dirty path otherwise, so the SessionStart hook surfaces it at the first prompt and Claude deals with it. The CLI is resolved the way the other steps resolve orca-ide (read 60-orca-repo-add).

title: desktop conduit: launch Orca.app on a launcher-owned profile that holds only this folder's environment; zero local projects, fail-closed
description:
WHY
The user's rule: nothing the launcher opens may run outside the container, no exception. Orca.app 1.4.197 can open LOCAL workspaces (allowLocalRuntime = !isWebClient, no knob), and today the launcher launches the user's own Orca profile, which already held this folder as a local project (badge "Local Mac"). Detection at hand-off (c4c5a4b) is not enough.

2. Every orca CLI call the launcher makes (orca_hand_off: status/environment rm/add; orca_env_forget; cmd_verify's local-repos row; any other cli call) runs with ORCA_USER_DATA_PATH=<profile> in its environment (verified fact: the CLI resolves the instance per that env var; `status --json` under an empty profile reports reachable:false).

Skip the launch when `status --json` under the profile already reports reachable (an earlier ./claude-dev left the conduit running). CLAUDE_ORCA_OPEN=0 still skips it.

Reuse orca_lists_local_repo or replace it with an any-repo check -- keep the function names the tests already use where possible.
6. Teardown: orca_env_forget runs environment rm under the profile, then rm -rf the profile dir.

title: C: orchestrator context diet -- delegation gate denies Bash streaks, output-cap hook, subagent cache TTL, autoContinueAtUsageLimit
description:

Behaviour:
1. Delegation gate: in the main loop (agent_id unset) every Bash call counts toward the streak unless its command matches the small read-only exempt list that already exists (keep that list, do not grow it), and past DELEGATION_GATE_DENY_AT the gate DENIES a Bash call the same way it denies edits, with the denial text naming the exact spawn to use (scout for recon, executor via orca-dispatch or Agent for edits). Subagent calls stay skipped entirely. lane express keeps its current exemption.
2. scripts/output-cap.sh, a PreToolUse hook on Bash: main loop only; skipped when tool_input.run_in_background is true, when CLAUDE_ORCA_OUTPUT_CAP is 0, or when the command already ends in a pipe to head/tail/wc. Otherwise it rewrites tool_input.command through hookSpecificOutput.updatedInput (the tier-gate.sh precedent) into a wrapper that runs the original command with stdout+stderr into a file under ${CLAUDE_ORCA_OUTPUT_DIR:-${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/claude-orca-output/<session_id>}, prints the first CLAUDE_ORCA_OUTPUT_CAP bytes (default 6000), appends one line '[output capped at N bytes of M; full output: <path>]' only when it was cut, and exits with the original command's exit code. The wrapper must survive commands containing single quotes, heredocs and && chains: write the original command to a file and run it with 'bash <file>' rather than interpolating it.
3. config/claude-settings.json: register output-cap on PreToolUse matcher Bash AFTER the existing guards; add "subagentPromptCacheTtl": "1h" at top level.
4. scripts/container/entrypoint.sh (runs as root before the privilege drop): if /etc/claude-code/managed-settings.json is absent, write {"autoContinueAtUsageLimit": true} there (mode 644); if it exists without the key, merge the key in with jq; never overwrite other keys. Skip silently when not root (tests run unprivileged: honour a CLAUDE_ORCA_MANAGED_SETTINGS override path so the test can point it at a temp file).

title: A: dispatch reliability -- heartbeat, stall rule with nudge and fallback, launch diagnostics, new-child naming, stagger
description:
Slice A -- dispatch reliability (Win 1). Files: scripts/orca-dispatch.sh, scripts/orca-wait.sh, scripts/lib/orca-orch.sh, NEW tests/orca-wait.bats, NEW tests/orca-dispatch-launch.bats (both driven by a stub orca-ide/orca on PATH that replays canned JSON from fixture files and logs every argv to a file; the existing tests/orca-dispatch.bats uses the real xvfb CLI and is not part of this contract).
Behaviour:
1. The dispatch record (.claude-dev/run/orchestration/dispatch/<id>.json) gains started_at (epoch seconds) and worktree_path (the directory behind a path: selector, else empty).
2. orca-wait gains --stall-after <sec> (default 600) and --poll <sec> (default 60): it loops on 'orchestration check --wait' in poll-sized waits until the overall --timeout-ms, and between waits inspects every dispatch record in state ready/running. Activity for a record = the newest of: started_at, the time of the last heartbeat/question/escalation message seen from that dispatch (persist last_activity in the record when a message arrives), the HEAD commit time of worktree_path, and the newest mtime among files 'git -C worktree_path status --porcelain' lists. If now - activity > stall-after: print one receipt {"type":"stalled","bead","dispatch_id","terminal","idle_s","nudge":"orca terminal send --terminal <h> --text ... --enter"} and, unless --no-nudge, send exactly one nudge through 'orca terminal send' telling the worker to continue and to heartbeat, recording nudged_at in the record. If a record already has nudged_at and stalls again, print {"type":"stalled","nudged":true,"fallback":"<the Agent-tool spec, as orch_fallback prints it>","worktree_path":...} and return 0 so the orchestrator can re-run the slice in-process on the same worktree.
3. WORKER RULES (orch_spec in lib/orca-orch.sh) gain one rule: after every commit and at least every 5 minutes of work, send 'orca-ide orchestration send --type heartbeat --subject alive --task-id <t> --dispatch-id <d> --json'; and orca-wait treats a heartbeat as activity without printing a receipt for it beyond one stderr note.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# claude-orca-xyr CHECK: a SECOND folder whose template clone comes from
# origin (GitHub, the way bootstrap and --update deliver it) runs ITS OWN
# config-sync and ends up with no /card command and no card hook entry.
set -uo pipefail
ORIGIN="https://github.com/joe-rayment/claude_orca.git"
WORK="${1:?usage: xyr-check.sh <scratch-dir>}"
FOLDER="$WORK/second-folder"
rm -rf "$FOLDER"
mkdir -p "$FOLDER/.claude-dev/home" "$FOLDER/.claude-dev/run"
echo '{}' > "$FOLDER/.claude-dev/claude-orca.json"

echo "== 1. template clone from origin/main"
git clone -q --branch main "$ORIGIN" "$FOLDER/.claude-dev/template" || { echo "FAIL clone"; exit 1; }
sha=$(git -C "$FOLDER/.claude-dev/template" rev-parse HEAD)
echo "template HEAD = $sha"

echo "== 2. the FOLDER's own config-sync, ambient identity stripped"
env -u PROJECT_DIR -u CLAUDE_ORCA_ROOT -u CLAUDE_ORCA_HOST_DIR -u CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR \
    HOME="$FOLDER/.claude-dev/home" \
    "$FOLDER/.claude-dev/template/scripts/config-sync.sh" \
        --project "$FOLDER" --host "$FOLDER/.claude-dev" \
    || { echo "FAIL config-sync exit $?"; exit 1; }

CFG="$FOLDER/.claude-dev/home/.claude"
echo "== 3. assertions on $CFG"
fail=0
if [ -e "$CFG/commands/card.md" ]; then echo "FAIL commands/card.md present"; fail=1
else echo "ok   no commands/card.md"; fi
ls "$CFG/commands" 2>/dev/null | sed 's/^/     commands: /'

n=$(jq '[.hooks[][].hooks[].command | select(test("bin/card"))] | length' "$CFG/settings.json") \
    || { echo "FAIL settings.json unreadable"; exit 1; }
if [ "$n" = "0" ]; then echo "ok   0 hook entries match bin/card"
else echo "FAIL $n hook entries match bin/card"; fail=1; fi

if grep -qiE '(^|[^a-z])card([^a-z]|$)' "$CFG/settings.json"; then
    echo "FAIL the word 'card' appears in the synced settings.json"; fail=1
else echo "ok   no word 'card' in the synced settings.json"; fi

total=$(jq '[.hooks[][].hooks[]] | length' "$CFG/settings.json")
echo "     $total hook entries synced in total (non-vacuous: the sync ran)"
[ "$total" -gt 0 ] || { echo "FAIL no hook entries at all -- sync did not run"; fail=1; }

if [ "$fail" = 0 ]; then echo "PASS xyr: second folder at origin/main $sha carries no /card"
else echo "FAIL xyr"; fi
exit "$fail"

title: OpenRouter guard: the real key is visible via ps/proc to any same-uid process while the guard runs (argv/environ), not just to the guard itself
description: Found by the qa2.21 verifier, does not affect that bead's PASS. entrypoint.sh starts the guard as 'env OPENROUTER_API_KEY=<real key> python3 <guard script> ...', so the key sits in that process's argv and /proc/<pid>/environ, readable by any process running as the same agent uid (e.g. a worker terminal doing ps -ef or reading /proc). The guard's whole purpose is to keep the key out of agent terminals' reach, so this is a real if narrow gap: an agent that specifically goes looking (ps -ef | grep OPENROUTER, or reads /proc/<guard-pid>/environ) can still recover the real key, though normal agent env/config never shows it. Fix: pass the key to the guard via a pipe/fd or a mode-600 file read once at startup instead of argv/env, and have the guard scrub it from its own os.environ immediately after reading (argv still needs care: use env -u or read from stdin instead of an argv assignment).
notes: RED-AT e62e105 · GREEN-AT 9f99786 (wt/dbu). Verifier PASS: frozen diff empty; red not ok 19,20 (entrypoint) and 12 (provision); green 1..20 and 1..17 zero not ok, names verbatim; syntax/py_compile clean. Real guard started with a dummy key file: listening, /proc/<pid>/environ key matches 0, cmdline matches 0, no OPENROUTER_API_KEY line at all, key file unlinked, guard.log matches 0; whitespace-only key file -> exit 2, unlinked, logged. Mechanism: mode-600 agent-owned key file read once and unlinked, guard started with env -u, os.environ popped, provision-run's handoff also a key file unlinked on read, step 70 unsets before a restart (a real leak the restart case caught: /proc/<pid>/environ is fixed at exec, so env -u is load-bearing). Verifier note: read_api_key() keeps an OPENROUTER_API_KEY env fallback for by-hand runs, documented, unused by the image. Follow-up bead for the Mac run: claude-orca-1ca.

title: S9 Opt-in Orca orchestration mode (orca CLI socket inside the sandbox, skills, hardening checklist)
description:
Why: Orca's orchestration layer (runs, tasks, `orca orchestration worker-start --agent codex --worktree current`, messages, gates) is the most native way for Claude to direct other models and have Orca show every worker. But the orca CLI socket is a remote control for an unsandboxed app: `orca terminal create --command …` runs anything outside the sandbox unless the shell is in one of this project's worktrees, `orca goto/exec` drives an unsandboxed browser (network escape), automations and artifacts run outside too. So this is opt-in, off by default, and the residual surface is stated every time it is on.

What: <project>/.claude-dev/sandbox.json `{"orca": {"cli": true}}` → the wrapper adds allowUnixSockets [<real ~>/Library/Application Support/orca] and allowRead of that dir, passes ORCA_CLI_COMMAND through, installs the orca-cli + orchestration skills into the config dir (from the Orca repo's skills/, pinned copy under template/), and adds a rulebook addendum: Claude is the coordinator; a tier's executor slice may become `orca orchestration worker-start --task <id> --worktree current --agent <codex|claude|gemini>` (same worktree → sandboxed by S2); workers report worker_done; beads remain the source of truth. `claude-dev --doctor` prints the escape-surface warning and the Orca settings to harden (Floating Workspace off, public artifact links off, no per-repo setup hooks) whenever the mode is on. The self-test's orca-socket probe expects reachable in this mode.

Boundaries: no attempt to sandbox Orca itself.

title: S12 claude-dev --update / --teardown / --uninstall with beads snapshot
description:
Why: the template must be updatable and removable without losing beads, mirroring the old --update/--teardown with the new host/project split.

title: S9 Opt-in Orca orchestration mode (orca CLI socket inside the sandbox, skills, hardening checklist)
description:
Why: Orca's orchestration layer (runs, tasks, `orca orchestration worker-start --agent codex --worktree current`, messages, gates) is the most native way for Claude to direct other models and have Orca show every worker. But the orca CLI socket is a remote control for an unsandboxed app: `orca terminal create --command …` runs anything outside the sandbox unless the shell is in one of this project's worktrees, `orca goto/exec` drives an unsandboxed browser (network escape), automations and artifacts run outside too. So this is opt-in, off by default, and the residual surface is stated every time it is on.

What: <project>/.claude-dev/sandbox.json `{"orca": {"cli": true}}` → the wrapper adds allowUnixSockets [<real ~>/Library/Application Support/orca] and allowRead of that dir, passes ORCA_CLI_COMMAND through, installs the orca-cli + orchestration skills into the config dir (from the Orca repo's skills/, pinned copy under template/), and adds a rulebook addendum: Claude is the coordinator; a tier's executor slice may become `orca orchestration worker-start --task <id> --worktree current --agent <codex|claude|gemini>` (same worktree → sandboxed by S2); workers report worker_done; beads remain the source of truth. `claude-dev --doctor` prints the escape-surface warning and the Orca settings to harden (Floating Workspace off, public artifact links off, no per-repo setup hooks) whenever the mode is on. The self-test's orca-socket probe expects reachable in this mode.

Boundaries: no attempt to sandbox Orca itself.
design: Orca references: src/cli/runtime/metadata.ts:50-54 (runtime dir, ORCA_USER_DATA_PATH), docs/site/content/docs/cli/orchestration.mdx (worker-start, check, send, ask, gates), docs/.../cli/skills.mdx (skills install). Decision recorded in .claude/plans/orca-port.md §4.

title: S8 Multi-model delegation in the sandbox (routes: opencode, codex, gemini; masked provider keys)
description:
Why: "more than just Claude Code, with Claude Code always primary": Claude orchestrates; other models execute slices headless inside the same sandbox, taking their brief from a bead, and report through receipts and bead notes. The old delegate.sh already does this for opencode; it needs its Docker bindings replaced and two more runners.

What: scripts/delegate.sh ported — REPO_DIR from `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` (no /workspace), job worktrees under <primary>/.claude-dev/delegate/<job> (inside the sandbox scope), runners opencode (`opencode run`), codex (`codex exec`), gemini (`gemini -p`) selected by route.runner, egress preflight = check the route's provider host against the srt allowlist instead of iptables, receipt.json schema unchanged, bead notes get delegated-to/branch/receipt. config/delegate-routes.json gains codex and gemini example routes. Provider keys (OPENROUTER_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, GEMINI_API_KEY) are taken from the host env by the wrapper and masked via srt credentials with per-provider injectHosts (S5 pattern). Rulebook Delegation section: an executor slice may be routed with `delegate run --route <r> --bead <id>` when the bead's design names a route; tiers and routes stay orthogonal (knowledge-base/DELEGATION_ROUTES.md ported).

Boundaries: no Orca-native workers (S9); interactive Codex/Gemini sessions the user opens in Orca are already sandboxed by S2 and need nothing here.

title: glm route's provider pin can break when ~z-ai/glm-latest moves to a new GLM
description: Since the routes moved to OpenRouter ~latest aliases (luna -> ~openai/gpt-luna-latest, served as openai/gpt-6-luna on 2026-09-24), the glm route keeps pin {order: [deepinfra, parasail], allow_fallbacks: false} in config/delegate-routes.json. delegate.sh writes that pin into the opencode per-model provider options, so the day OpenRouter points ~z-ai/glm-latest at a GLM neither host serves, delegate --route glm fails with no endpoints instead of following the release. Decide: drop allow_fallbacks:false (the in-VM guard's provider-policy allowlist still bounds hosting), or keep the pin and have delegate check warn when the alias target has no pinned endpoint. Also: qwen-coder stays on the fixed qwen/qwen3-coder because OpenRouter publishes no qwen coder ~latest alias yet.
acceptance_criteria:
DECISION (orchestrator, 2026-10-02): drop the glm route's provider pin. The in-VM guard already forces config/provider-policy.json on every request -- provider.only = the allowlist, allow_fallbacks false, and its own .order whenever a client order is missing or empty -- so the pin adds nothing for residency and only breaks the day ~z-ai/glm-latest points at a GLM neither deepinfra nor parasail serves.
FILES: config/delegate-routes.json, tests/delegate.bats, knowledge-base/DELEGATION_ROUTES.md only.
CHANGE: remove the glm route's "pin" object (keep runner/model/grade). In tests/delegate.bats's case 'config/delegate-routes.json: ships glm and local plus codex and gemini example routes', replace the two pin assertions (pin.order == deepinfra,parasail and pin.allow_fallbacks == false) with one asserting the glm route has no pin ('.routes.glm | has("pin") | not'); keep the loop over pinned slugs (it stays valid for any future pin). DELEGATION_ROUTES.md's glm table row: drop '(provider-pinned: deepinfra, parasail, no fallbacks)' and say the guard's policy order picks the host. Leave the doc's generic description of the optional pin field.
CHECK: bats tests/delegate.bats </dev/null -> every case ok; 'delegate check' run for real prints a glm row (quote it in the commit body). Commit subject starts 'delegate:'.

title: orca-dispatch into an Orca-created worktree: 'mkdir: cannot create directory /workspace/.beads: Permission denied' and 'frozen-hook: could not install pre-commit hook'
description: Seen 2026-09-19 on both dispatches into .orca-worktrees/claude-orca/wt-vm1-jg1 (created with 'orca-ide worktree create', passed as --worktree id:...). The dispatch itself succeeded and both workers finished, but the frozen-test pre-commit hook (claude-orca-2m5) was NOT installed in that worktree, so only the verifier stood between a flash worker and an edited FROZEN test. The mkdir suggests a .beads path derived from the worktree's parent rather than from BEADS_DIR. Not investigated.
acceptance_criteria:
ROOT CAUSE (orchestrator, 2026-10-02): this repo's .git/config has core.hooksPath=/workspace/.beads/hooks, a stale absolute path from an older mount (a fresh 'bd init' writes <project>/.beads/hooks correctly). install_frozen_hook writes into 'git rev-parse --git-path hooks', i.e. that path -> mkdir fails. Even with a correct hooksPath the design is wrong: hooks are SHARED by every worktree (one claude-orca-bead file for parallel dispatches) and .beads/hooks is TRACKED, so the installer would rewrite tracked files in the main tree.
DESIGN: a private hooks dir per worktree, switched on for the worker's processes only through git's env config (git >= 2.31: GIT_CONFIG_COUNT/GIT_CONFIG_KEY_<n>/GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_<n> beat repo config). No repo config, no tracked file is touched.
FILES: scripts/lib/frozen-hook.sh, scripts/orca-dispatch.sh, scripts/delegate.sh, tests/frozen-hook.bats, tests/orca-dispatch-headless.bats, tests/delegate.bats only.
1. install_frozen_hook <worktree> <bead>: hooks dir = "$(git -C <wt> rev-parse --absolute-git-dir)/claude-orca-hooks" (a linked worktree's private .git/worktrees/<name>/, the main tree's .git/). Before writing, record the repo's OWN hooks dir -- 'git -C <wt> rev-parse --git-path hooks' made absolute -- in <dir>/claude-orca-chain. Write <dir>/claude-orca-bead and <dir>/pre-commit (the generated body), chmod +x. PRINT the hooks dir on stdout. Return non-zero only when <wt> is not a git work tree or the dir cannot be written.
2. The generated body: read the bead from CLAUDE_ORCA_BEAD or <its own dir>/claude-orca-bead (its own dir = the dir the hook file lives in: "$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"), and chain to <chain>/pre-commit first when that file exists, is executable and is not this same file (its failure still aborts). Everything else in the body unchanged (fail-open rules, RED-AT lookup, the frozen message).
3. A helper frozen_hook_env <hooks-dir> printing the three assignments, one per line: GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1, GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=core.hooksPath, GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=<dir>.
4. orca-dispatch: capture the dir from install_frozen_hook (FROZEN_WT known). Headless opencode: the composed COMMAND starts with 'env GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1 GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=core.hooksPath GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=<dir> ' before <template>/bin/orca-worker-run. TUI opencode: prefix the composed command with 'export GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1 GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=core.hooksPath GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=<dir>; '. claude/codex/gemini worker-start paths: unchanged (Claude workers carry the Claude-side contract-gate). The post-launch new-child install (around line 401): keep calling it, but say in the note that the hook only reaches processes started with the env, so a new-child worker is unprotected -- one line, no further work.
5. delegate.sh: for a --bead job, add the three assignments to env_args from the installer's dir (they then also land in the job's env record file, which is fine -- no secret).
6. Header comments of frozen-hook.sh: replace the 'shared hooks dir' explanation with the private-dir + env design and why (claude-orca-cdu).
TESTS (each new/changed case opens with '# Guards:' / '# Fails if:' / '# Run:'): update tests/frozen-hook.bats so its commits run with the env from frozen_hook_env (the behaviour they guard is unchanged); add: (a) a repo whose core.hooksPath points at a nonexistent absolute dir plus a LINKED worktree: install succeeds, prints a dir under the worktree's absolute git dir, a frozen-path commit made with the env is refused, the same commit WITHOUT the env goes through, and 'git config core.hooksPath' plus every tracked file are unchanged; (b) a repo whose hooksPath holds a pre-commit that writes a marker: with the env, a non-frozen commit still runs that hook (chain); (c) two worktrees installed for two different beads keep their own bead ids. tests/orca-dispatch-headless.bats: the headless composed command carries the GIT_CONFIG prefix naming the worktree's private dir. tests/delegate.bats: a --bead job's env record lists GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0.
REAL CHECK: in a scratch clone with a linked worktree, run the real install + a real 'git commit' with the env and quote the refusal line in the commit body.
CHECK: bats tests/frozen-hook.bats tests/orca-dispatch-headless.bats tests/delegate.bats tests/orca-worker-run.bats </dev/null -> every case ok; bash scripts/lint-bash32.sh exits 0. Commit subject starts 'frozen-hook:'.

RED-AT: 4e5a6da
GREEN-AT: f27a9b9 -- CHECK (bats tests/frozen-hook.bats tests/orca-dispatch-headless.bats tests/delegate.bats tests/orca-worker-run.bats </dev/null) 63/63 ok; bash scripts/lint-bash32.sh exit 0; REAL CHECK: stale core.hooksPath clone + linked worktree, install printed /tmp/gtest/real-clone/.git/worktrees/real-wt/claude-orca-hooks, real git commit with the env refused: "frozen: tests/frozen-hook.bats is frozen from 4e5a6da7343e0f05472779f482f75859b3516ab5 (claude-orca-cdu); do not commit changes to it -- if the test is wrong, run: bd supersede claude-orca-cdu", same commit without the env passed, repo config and tracked files unchanged

Redesigned per the acceptance contract: the hook now lives in a private dir per worktree (<abs-git-dir>/claude-orca-hooks) installed by scripts/lib/frozen-hook.sh, which also records the repo's own hooks dir in claude-orca-chain for the generated pre-commit to chain to, and frozen_hook_env prints the three GIT_CONFIG_* assignments that switch the dir on per process. orca-dispatch.sh prefixes the headless opencode command with 'env ...' and the TUI command with 'export ...;' when the worktree dir is known, and notes that a post-launch (new-child/id:) install cannot protect the already-started worker. delegate.sh adds the three assignments to a --bead job's env_args, so they reach the runner and the job env record.
